states.name: Alabama
notes: Alabama's property tax break is all-or-nothing. You must be 'permanently and totally disabled.' There is no partial break for a 10% to 90% VA rating.

The 2026 law (HB77) names the VA letter showing a '100 percent service-connected, permanent, and total disability' as the proof. No official Alabama source says whether TDIU alone counts. Ask your county Revenue Commissioner before you count on it.

You must apply at your county office, not the state. File between October 1 and December 31 to get the break for the current year. Filing later gets you the following year. Nothing is automatic and nothing is refunded for past years.

Starting October 1, 2026, P&T veterans no longer have to sign the yearly verification card (HB155). The release ends when the veteran dies or moves to a new home. Until then, keep mailing the card back.

The homestead exemption does not pass to a surviving spouse unless the spouse qualifies on his or her own (age 65+ or P&T disabled). Only the Specially Adapted Housing home exemption (Code 40-9-20) continues for an unremarried widow or widower.
Vehicle fee waivers do not erase the county ad valorem (property) tax on your car at any rating, even 100%. Only a vehicle paid for in whole or part with a VA grant is ad valorem exempt.
You must claim the vehicle registration fee exemption at the counter when you register or renew. If you forget, the state will not refund it.

The $5 extra-vehicle plate rate is for ratings above 50% (ALDOR says '51% and higher'; the ADVA guide calls it '60% or Higher'). Under 50% you get one fee-exempt vehicle only. You do not have to buy the Disabled Veteran plate to get the fee break.

The G.I. Dependents' Scholarship is for your children, stepchildren, spouse, or unremarried widow(er), not for you. The veteran needs a 40% rating, Alabama residency before entering service (or 5 years of residency if 100% P&T), and the student must be an Alabama resident. Kids must start before age 26.
Scholarship money is capped at $400 per semester hour for tuition and $1,000 per semester for books and fees combined. Other grants are applied first. Benefits are never retroactive.

Hunting and fishing discounts are for Alabama residents only and are decided by your driver license. Fishing needs 20%, hunting needs 50% (cheaper at 100%), and lifetime licenses need 20% (fishing) or 40% (hunting). Bring your VA rating letter.
Alabama taxes income, but military retirement pay, SBP survivor benefits, and all VA compensation are exempt. Active-duty base pay of Alabama residents is still taxed.

benefits.benefit: Homestead exemption for permanently and totally disabled homeowners
benefits.details: A homeowner who is permanently and totally disabled pays no state, county, or city property tax on the primary home and up to 160 acres, with no income limit and no value cap. Alabama has no partial break for lower VA ratings; the test is permanent and total disability, and the 2026 act names the VA letter showing a 100% service-connected permanent and total rating as proof. Apply in person or by mail at your county Revenue Commissioner or Tax Assessor; file October 1 to December 31 for the current tax year (later filings apply to the next year). You must own and live in the home on October 1.
benefits.source_title: Alabama Department of Revenue - Homestead Exemptions (Code of Ala. 40-9-19, 40-9-21; Rule 810-4-1-.23)

benefits.benefit: Property tax exemption for homes bought with a VA Specially Adapted Housing grant
benefits.details: A home acquired under the VA Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) grant program is exempt from property tax regardless of its value for as long as the veteran, or the veteran's unremarried surviving spouse, owns and lives in it. Eligibility is tied to the SAH grant, not to a VA percentage. Claim it at your county Revenue Commissioner or Tax Assessor with proof of the SAH grant.
benefits.source_title: ADVA - Alabama Laws Affecting Veterans (May 2025), Homes of Veterans/Widows Acquired Under PL 702 (Code of Ala. 40-9-20)

benefits.benefit: 2026 changes: no annual re-verification for P&T veterans (HB155) and mortgage pre-approval certificate (HB77)
benefits.details: Effective October 1, 2026, a veteran the VA has found permanently and totally disabled who holds the homestead exemption no longer has to re-claim or re-verify it each year; the release ends at the veteran's death or when a new homestead is established. Also effective October 1, 2026, a veteran with a VA 100% service-connected P&T rating can get a tentative certificate of exemption from the county assessing official within 20 days, before buying a home, and lenders may not count homestead property tax in the debt-to-income ratio. Both bills passed the Legislature as enrolled; the act numbers and signing record were not confirmed on an official page.
benefits.source_title: Alabama Legislature - HB155 (2026 RS) Enrolled; see also HB77 (2026 RS) Enrolled, Disabled Veterans Property Tax Debt-To-Income Ratio Exemption Act

benefits.benefit: Vehicle registration fee exemption and Disabled Veteran license plate
benefits.details: An Alabama resident with a service-connected rating of 10% or higher pays no state registration fee or plate issuance fee on one vehicle; ad valorem (property) tax on the vehicle is still owed. Veterans rated above 50% (ALDOR says 51% and higher) or who need special mechanical controls can register additional vehicles for a $5 annual fee each and may use any weight pleasure vehicle. Bring your VA rating letter plus a DD214, military ID, or ADVA affidavit to the county license office, and claim the exemption when you register or renew because it is not refunded later. You do not have to buy the Disabled Veteran plate to get the fee break, and the plate cannot pass to a surviving spouse.
benefits.source_title: Alabama Department of Revenue - Disabled Veteran License Plate (Code of Ala. 40-12-244, 40-12-254, 32-6-130; Rule 810-5-1-.201)

benefits.benefit: No license fees or ad valorem tax on a vehicle paid for with a VA grant
benefits.details: A disabled veteran whose vehicle was paid for in whole or in part with VA funds (such as the VA automobile grant) owes no license or registration fees and no ad valorem tax on that vehicle, as long as it is kept for private use. This is limited to one plate. Eligibility is based on the VA grant, not a specific rating percentage. Show proof of the VA grant at your county license office when registering.
benefits.source_title: Alabama Department of Revenue - Disabled Veteran License Plate, vehicle paid for by U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (Code of Ala. 40-12-254)

benefits.benefit: Purple Heart, Medal of Honor, and POW plates; Honored Veteran Parking Permit
benefits.details: Purple Heart recipients get the first plate free of registration fees (ad valorem tax still applies); Medal of Honor, former POW, and Legion of Valor recipients get the first plate free of both registration fees and ad valorem tax. These plates are permanent, do not need yearly re-registration, and a surviving spouse may keep the plate (Purple Heart spouses pay the ad valorem tax). Apply at the county license office with a DD214 or VA certification. Anyone who qualifies for one of these plates can also get an Honored Veteran Parking Permit placard from an ADVA county veterans service office.
benefits.source_title: Alabama Department of Revenue - Purple Heart License Plate (Code of Ala. 32-6-250, 32-6-254); ADVA Laws Affecting Veterans (May 2025)

benefits.benefit: Disabled Military Veteran's Appreciation hunting licenses (50% and 100%) and lifetime hunting license (40%)
benefits.details: Alabama residents rated 50% or more can buy the annual Military Veteran's Appreciation all-game hunting license at about half price ($15.65 on the 2022 form), and residents rated 100% pay a nominal fee ($3.30 on the 2022 form; the statute sets $2 plus issuance fee, subject to adjustment). Residents rated 40% or more may instead buy a lifetime disabled veteran hunting license, priced by whether you are under or over 50 and whether you are 100% P&T. Buy at your county Probate Office or License Commissioner, or by mail to DCNR, with your VA rating letter; licenses run September 1 to August 31. Residency follows your driver license, and nonresident disabled veterans get no discount.
benefits.source_title: Alabama DCNR - 100% and 50% Disabled Military Veteran's Appreciation Hunting License forms (Code of Ala. 9-11-44, 9-11-65.3); DCNR License FAQs

benefits.benefit: Disabled Military Veteran's Appreciation fishing licenses (20%), freshwater and saltwater, annual and lifetime
benefits.details: Alabama residents with a VA rating of 20% or more can buy reduced-price annual freshwater and saltwater fishing licenses (the saltwater license is $3.15 on the current DCNR form) and may instead buy lifetime disabled veteran freshwater and/or saltwater licenses priced by whether you are under or over age 50. Show your VA rating letter at the county Probate Office or License Commissioner, a DCNR district office, or buy online. Licenses run September 1 to August 31. Nonresidents do not qualify.
benefits.source_title: Alabama DCNR Marine Resources - Disabled Military Veteran's Appreciation Annual Saltwater Fishing License (Code of Ala. 9-11-53.1, 9-11-65.3); DCNR License FAQs

benefits.benefit: Free state park admission for resident veterans and 15% lodging discount
benefits.details: Honorably discharged veterans who live in Alabama get free day-use admission to state parks that charge entrance fees (Parks for Patriots), by showing a military or retiree ID, an Alabama driver license with the veteran designation, or a DD214. Veterans, active military, and people with ADA-defined disabilities also get a 15% daily discount on park-run overnight lodging, which cannot be combined with other discounts; ID is required at check-in. This is not based on a disability rating. Some parks limit free entry to the veteran only, not dependents.
benefits.source_title: Alabama State Parks - Parks for Patriots (Code of Ala. 9-14-8); park discount pages

benefits.benefit: Alabama G.I. Dependents' Scholarship Program (children, stepchildren, spouses, unremarried widow(er)s)
benefits.details: Dependents of a veteran rated 40% or more (or a POW, MIA, or veteran who died from service-connected causes or in the line of duty) get tuition up to $400 per semester hour plus up to $1,000 per semester for books and fees at Alabama public colleges and listed private colleges, after other grants are applied. Children and stepchildren get 10 semesters (must start before age 26); spouses and widow(er)s get 10 semesters if the veteran is 100% P&T, or 6 semesters at 40% to 90%. The veteran must have been an Alabama resident for a year before entering service plus meet a current-residency test, or if 100% P&T have lived in Alabama for 5 years; the student must be an Alabama resident and file the FAFSA each year. Apply through the ADVA scholarship portal; benefits are not retroactive and end on divorce or the widow(er)'s remarriage.
benefits.source_title: ADVA - Alabama G.I. Dependent Scholarship Program pamphlet (November 2024) and Laws Affecting Veterans (May 2025) (Code of Ala. 31-6-1 to 31-6-17)

benefits.benefit: Purple Heart recipient tuition and fee waiver (discretionary)
benefits.details: Alabama public two-year and four-year colleges may waive tuition and fees for undergraduate study by Purple Heart recipients. The law says 'may,' so each school decides whether and how to grant it. Contact the financial aid or veterans office at the public college you plan to attend. There is no other state tuition waiver for the disabled veteran personally.
benefits.source_title: ADVA - Alabama Laws Affecting Veterans (May 2025), Tuition Waiver - Purple Heart Medal Recipients (Code of Ala. 16-1-43)

benefits.benefit: Military retirement pay and VA benefits exempt from state income tax
benefits.details: Alabama has a state income tax, but military retirement pay, survivor benefits derived from it, and disability and other benefits paid by the VA are fully exempt; combat-zone pay and military allowances are also exempt. You simply leave these amounts off your Alabama return. Active-duty base pay of Alabama residents is still taxable. No application is needed.
benefits.source_title: Alabama Department of Revenue - Income Exempt from Alabama Income Taxation (Code of Ala. 40-18-20, 40-18-3)

benefits.benefit: State classified employment preference points (5 or 10 points)
benefits.details: Honorably discharged veterans get 5 points added to their passing score on State Personnel Department open-competitive exams; veterans with a current service-connected disability receiving VA compensation get 10 points, as do certain spouses and unremarried widows of disabled or deceased veterans. Attach your DD214 and, for the 10 points, a VA rating letter dated within the last 6 months (keep it updated until the register is set or you drop to 5 points). Points are not given on promotional exams. Apply through personnel.alabama.gov.
benefits.source_title: State of Alabama Personnel Department - FAQ, Veteran Preference (Code of Ala. 36-26-15(b))

benefits.benefit: Business and occupational license tax exemption for disabled veterans
benefits.details: An honorably discharged wartime-era veteran who is a permanent Alabama resident with a physical disability of 25% or more (service-connected or not) can get state, county, and city business or occupational licenses for no more than $25 total, if the business is run by the veteran personally with no more than one employee. The exemption is lost if the veteran's total real and personal property is worth $5,000 or more or net income is $2,500 or more, so very few veterans qualify today. Apply at the county Probate Judge or License Commissioner that issues the license.
benefits.source_title: ADVA - Alabama Laws Affecting Veterans (May 2025), Business and Occupational License Exemptions for Disabled Veterans (Code of Ala. 40-12-340 to 40-12-352)

benefits.benefit: State Veterans Homes (skilled nursing and assisted living) and State Veterans Memorial Cemetery
benefits.details: ADVA runs five State Veterans Homes (Alexander City, Pell City, Bay Minette, Huntsville, and a fifth home) offering skilled nursing and some assisted living care to eligible Alabama veterans, and the Alabama State Veterans Memorial Cemetery at Spanish Fort. Apply through your county veterans service officer or directly with the home of your choice. Current admission rules (service, discharge, residency) and daily co-pay amounts were not available on a current ADVA page and should be confirmed with ADVA at 334-242-5077.
benefits.source_title: Alabama Department of Veterans Affairs - State Veterans Homes (Code of Ala. 31-5A-1 to 31-5A-11); Laws Affecting Veterans (May 2025)

states.name: Alaska

agency.name: Alaska Department of Military and Veterans Affairs, Office of Veterans Affairs

notes: Alaska has no state income tax, so there is nothing to exempt: military retired pay and VA compensation are not taxed by the state. There is also no statewide sales tax, but many cities and boroughs charge their own local sales tax.

The disabled veteran property tax exemption is run by your city or borough, not the state. Each one sets its own form and deadline. Anchorage is March 15. Fairbanks North Star Borough is February 14 and you must apply in person. Check with your local assessor. If you live outside a borough that levies property tax, there is no tax and no exemption.

The state test for the property tax break is a rating of 50% or more from the VA or your branch of service. It does not ask whether you are P&T, TDIU, or 100% schedular. If your rating letter shows 50% or higher and the disability was incurred or aggravated in the line of duty, you meet the state threshold. Some boroughs (for example Fairbanks North Star) require a new rating letter every year if the VA has not marked your rating permanent.

The property tax break covers only the first $150,000 of assessed value, and only your primary home that you own and live in. A borough can go above $150,000 only if its voters approve an ordinance. A bill to raise the state floor to $250,000 (HB 169) was introduced in 2025 but had not passed as of October 2026.

Surviving spouse rule: the widow or widower keeps the exemption only if they are at least 60 and have not remarried. A municipality may extend it to a younger surviving spouse by voter-approved ordinance, so ask locally.

The free Alaska State Parks pass is for camping only. There is no disabled veteran day-use, parking, or boat launch pass. A bill to create a lifetime camping and parking permit (SB 30) was still in committee as of October 2026. The pass is not based on a percentage: you need proof of a service-connected disability.

The free hunting, fishing, and trapping card requires a 50% or greater VA rating, an honorable discharge, and Alaska residency under Fish and Game rules. You must be physically in Alaska to apply, and the card is void the day you stop being an Alaska resident.

The disabled veteran license plate (50% or more combined rating) gets you one free vehicle registration, but it does not come with disability parking privileges unless you also file DMV Form 861 signed by a health practitioner.

The University of Alaska tuition waiver for spouses and children is only for families of Alaska residents who died in the line of duty or were listed as POW or MIA. It does not cover dependents of living 100% disabled veterans. A 2025 bill (HB 88) to add permanent total disability had not passed as of October 2026.

The state job preference adds 10 points only when the state uses a numerically scored exam, which it rarely does. In practice a disabled veteran who meets minimum qualifications must be offered an interview for jobs open to all Alaska residents; it does not apply to jobs limited to current state employees.

The veterans land discount is 25% under the statute, even though an older Office of Veterans Affairs page says 20%. You can use it once in your lifetime and you must have been an Alaska resident for one year before the sale.

Permanent Fund Dividend: active duty service outside Alaska is an allowable absence only if you were an Alaska resident for at least six consecutive months before you left, and you must return to Alaska for at least 72 consecutive hours every two years.

benefits.benefit: Disabled veteran property tax exemption (first $150,000)
benefits.details: The first $150,000 of assessed value of the home you own and occupy as your primary residence is exempt from municipal property tax. You qualify if you were separated under conditions other than dishonorable, are an Alaska resident, and your disability was incurred or aggravated in the line of duty and is rated 50% or more by the VA or your branch of service. Apply in writing to your city or borough assessor with your VA rating letter; each municipality sets its own deadline (Anchorage March 15; Fairbanks North Star Borough February 14, in person). A widow or widower age 60 or older who has not remarried keeps the exemption.
benefits.source_title: Alaska Statutes 2025, AS 29.45.030(e), (f), (i) Required exemptions

benefits.benefit: Optional municipal exemption above $150,000
benefits.details: A borough or city may, by an ordinance approved by its voters, exempt the assessed value above $150,000 of a disabled veteran's primary residence. This is optional and most places have not adopted it. Ask your local assessor whether your municipality offers any exemption beyond the state-required $150,000, and whether it has extended the exemption to surviving spouses under 60.
benefits.source_title: Alaska Statutes 2025, AS 29.45.050(i) Optional exemptions and exclusions

benefits.benefit: Disabled veteran license plate and one free vehicle registration
benefits.details: A veteran with a combined service-connected rating of 50% or more from the VA can register one vehicle free and get a Disabled Veteran plate at no charge ($0 initial, $0 renewal). The plate without parking privileges needs only your VA rating notice; the plate with parking privileges also requires DMV Form 861 signed by a health practitioner showing a permanent mobility disability. Apply online through the Alaska DMV. Additional vehicles with the plate pay normal fees.
benefits.source_title: Alaska DMV, Disability Parking Permits & Plates (implements AS 28.10.181(d))

benefits.benefit: Veteran designation on driver license or ID
benefits.details: A retired veteran or a veteran discharged under honorable conditions can have a veteran designation printed on an Alaska driver license or state ID card. Apply with Form D1 and a DD-214, DD-215, NGB-22, a VA letter, or a military retiree ID. There is no extra fee beyond the normal license or duplicate fee.
benefits.source_title: Alaska DMV, Military & Veteran Services

benefits.benefit: Free permanent hunting, sport fishing, and trapping ID card
benefits.details: Alaska residents who were discharged under honorable conditions and are certified by the VA as 50% or more disabled receive a complimentary permanent identification card that takes the place of resident hunting, sport fishing, and trapping licenses. Apply through the ADF&G online store and send your VA disability certification letter to the ADF&G Licensing Section (adfg.license@alaska.gov, fax 907-465-2440, or P.O. Box 115525, Juneau, AK 99811-5525). You must be physically present in Alaska to apply, and the card is void if you stop being a resident. A free Sport Fishing Harvest Record Card is still required for fisheries with annual limits.
benefits.source_title: ADF&G Military Licenses, Alaska Resident Disabled Veteran License (AS 16.05.400(b))

benefits.benefit: Free Alaska State Parks disabled veteran camping pass
benefits.details: Disabled veterans receive one free Alaska State Park camping pass good in all developed state park campgrounds (not group sites, day-use areas, or boat launches). Present proof of a service-connected disability (a VA card imprinted 'service connected' or a current-year VA letter) plus photo ID in person at the DNR Public Information Center in Anchorage (907-269-8400) or Fairbanks (907-451-2705); call if you cannot appear in person. The veteran must be present in the campsite each night and the decal is not transferable.
benefits.source_title: Alaska State Parks, Disabled Veteran's Annual Camping Pass (AS 41.21.026(d))

benefits.benefit: Alaska Marine Highway half-fare disability pass
benefits.details: Veterans with a service-connected disability can get a Disability Discount Pass worth 50% off the standard adult passenger fare on Alaska Marine Highway ferries between Alaska ports (not Bellingham or Prince Rupert, and not vehicles, cabins, or meals). An attendant may ride at the discount if a physician certifies the need. Submit the application with photo ID and a VA letter or VHIC marked 'service connected' to the AMHS Disability Pass Desk (dot.amhs.customer@alaska.gov, 907-465-3946). Passes last two years and must be renewed.
benefits.source_title: Alaska Office of Veterans Affairs, Recreational benefits; AMHS Disability Discount Pass Application

benefits.benefit: University of Alaska tuition and fee waiver for survivors
benefits.details: The spouse or dependent child of an Alaska-resident member of the armed services, Alaska National Guard, or Naval Militia who died in the line of duty, died of line-of-duty injuries, or was listed by DoD as a POW or MIA is entitled to a waiver of undergraduate tuition and fees at the University of Alaska. The member must have lived in Alaska one year before service and listed Alaska as home of record. This does not cover dependents of living disabled veterans. Apply through the UA campus financial aid or veterans office.
benefits.source_title: Alaska Statutes 2025, AS 14.43.085; UA Regents Policy P05.10.080

benefits.benefit: No state income tax on military retired pay or VA compensation
benefits.details: Alaska has no personal income tax. The state's Net Income Tax Act applies only to corporations and by statute 'does not apply to an individual,' so military retired pay, SBP, and VA disability compensation are not taxed by the state and no state return is filed. There is also no statewide sales tax; boroughs and cities may levy their own local sales taxes.
benefits.source_title: Alaska Statutes 2025, AS 43.20.012(a)(1) Limitation on application of chapter; AS 29.45.650 Sales and use tax

benefits.benefit: State employment preference (5 or 10 points / guaranteed interview)
benefits.details: For State of Alaska jobs open to all Alaska residents or all applicants, a disabled veteran (one entitled to VA compensation or discharged for a service-connected disability) or former POW gets 10% of available points added on a numerically scored exam and, in the usual unscored process, must be offered an interview if minimally qualified. Other honorably discharged veterans, Guard members, and reservists get 5% of points or 'consideration'; spouses and certain survivors also receive consideration. Workplace Alaska flags the preference automatically; provide your DD-214 or VA letter if selected. The preference does not apply to recruitments limited to current state employees.
benefits.source_title: Alaska Statutes 2025, AS 39.25.159 Employment preference for military, veterans, and their spouses and children

benefits.benefit: Veterans land discount (25%) and veterans preference land auction
benefits.details: An eligible veteran gets a 25% discount on the purchase price of state land classified for non-commercial, non-industrial use (residential or recreational), once in a lifetime. You must be 18 or older, an Alaska resident for one year before the sale, and have served 90 days on active duty (or in the Alaska Territorial Guard) with an honorable or general-under-honorable discharge; shortened service due to a service-connected disability still counts. Apply at the time of purchase through DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water (907-269-8400). A separate veterans preference sealed-bid auction exists for residential parcels of five acres or less; the two cannot be combined.
benefits.source_title: Alaska Statutes 2025, AS 38.05.940 Land purchase price discount for veterans; DNR Fact Sheet: Veteran's Programs (Sept. 2025)

benefits.benefit: AHFC Veterans Mortgage Program and veterans interest rate preference
benefits.details: Alaska Housing Finance Corporation offers a tax-exempt-bond-funded Veterans Mortgage Program with below-market fixed rates for owner-occupied homes (duplex to fourplex with restrictions). You must apply within 25 years of discharge from active duty, have completed your initial obligation if still serving, and have been separated under conditions other than dishonorable; a DD-214 and VA Certificate of Eligibility are required. A separate State Veteran's Interest Rate Preference gives a 1% rate reduction on the first $50,000 of the loan, subject to income limits, and cannot be combined with the Veterans Mortgage Program. Apply through an AHFC-approved lender.
benefits.source_title: Alaska Housing Finance Corporation, Veterans Programs

benefits.benefit: Alaska Veterans and Pioneers Home (Palmer)
benefits.details: The state's veterans home in Palmer is an assisted living facility where 75% of its 79 beds are reserved for veterans. To apply you must be 60 or older, an Alaska resident under 7 AAC 74.035 who has lived in the state continuously for one year before applying, and (for the active waitlist) in need of the home's care. Veterans also submit a DD-214, VA Form 10-10EZ, and the Pioneer Homes Veterans' Addendum. Applications go to the Division of Alaska Pioneer Homes in Juneau (907-465-4416) or any Pioneer Home; admission is by original application date.
benefits.source_title: Alaska Department of Family and Community Services, Alaska Pioneer Homes Admissions; Alaska Veterans & Pioneers Home page

benefits.benefit: Permanent Fund Dividend allowable absence for military service
benefits.details: Alaska residents normally lose the yearly Permanent Fund Dividend if they are outside the state more than 180 days, but active duty service in the U.S. uniformed services (and accompanying spouses and dependents) is an allowable absence with no day limit. You must have been an Alaska resident for at least six consecutive months before leaving, keep Alaska as your state of legal residence (shown on your LES), return to Alaska for at least 72 consecutive hours every two years, and report all absences over 90 days on your application. Apply online with the PFD Division each January 1 to March 31.
benefits.source_title: Alaska Department of Revenue, PFD Division, Absence Guidelines and Military Eligibility (AS 43.23.008(a)(3))

states.name: Arizona
notes: Arizona's property tax law changed twice in 2026. For tax year 2026, only a veteran with a 100% service-connected VA rating gets the full exemption on a primary residence. TDIU (paid at the 100% rate but rated below 100%) does not count until tax year 2027, when Laws 2026, Chapter 140 takes effect.

The 100% full exemption is based on your combined rating on the VA letter, not on how much the VA pays you. Maricopa County says this directly. P&T status is not required for the property tax exemption, but it is required for the free Game and Fish license.

For tax year 2026 the household income limit still applies to every veteran exemption, including the 100% full exemption (ADOR FAQ and Maricopa County). Starting tax year 2027 the income limit is removed for veterans and their surviving spouses. Social Security, military pensions and VA disability pay are not counted as income.

You must file an affidavit with your county assessor between the first Monday in January and March 1 (A.R.S. 42-11153). Maricopa County lists February 28, or September 1 with an Exemption Deadline Waiver. Miss the window and the exemption is waived for that year unless the county board of supervisors redeems it; taxes already due are not refunded. Check your own county's dates.
Only one property tax exemption per person. You cannot stack the veteran exemption with the widow/widower or total-disability exemption, even if you qualify for more than one.
The constitution limits the veteran property tax exemption to honorably discharged veterans who are Arizona residents. A general discharge may not qualify; ask the assessor.
A surviving spouse keeps the 100% full exemption only while the home stays their primary residence and they do not remarry. Remarriage ends the vehicle license tax exemption too.

The vehicle license tax exemption covers one vehicle only, and you must be rated 100% and drawing compensation on that basis. A veteran rated below 100% does not get it unless they are a Purple Heart recipient or received a VA grant for the vehicle.

Arizona has no free annual state park pass for disabled veterans as of this review. The official benefit is a free day-use pass for 100% service-connected veterans and 50% off day use for other service-disabled or retired veterans. A 2026 bill (SB 1050) for a free lifetime pass passed the Legislature in March 2026, but we could not confirm on an official page that it was signed.

Arizona Game and Fish requires one full year of Arizona residency before you apply, and the free license needs a VA letter showing 100% permanent and total. A 100% rating that will be re-evaluated gets a license that expires after three years.

Military retirement pay has been fully exempt from Arizona income tax since tax year 2021. VA disability compensation is not in federal adjusted gross income, so it is not taxed by Arizona either, but ADOR's military page does not say this in so many words.

The Purple Heart tuition waiver at state universities and community colleges requires a VA rating of 50% or more and that you were an Arizona resident or stationed in Arizona when injured. There is no general tuition waiver for 100% disabled veterans in Arizona.

benefits.benefit: Full property tax exemption on primary residence (100% service-connected)
benefits.details: Your primary residence is fully exempt from property tax if your VA service-connected disability rating is 100%. A home owned with your spouse is treated as owned by you alone, and a surviving spouse keeps the full exemption while living there and not remarried. For tax year 2026 the household income limit still applies (per ADOR and Maricopa County); it is removed for tax year 2027. File an affidavit (ADOR Form 82514 or the county form) with your county assessor between the first Monday in January and March 1; Maricopa lists Feb. 28, or Sept. 1 with a deadline waiver.
benefits.source_title: A.R.S. 42-11111 Exemption for property; widows and widowers; persons with a total and permanent disability; veterans with a disability

benefits.benefit: Partial property tax exemption prorated by disability percentage
benefits.details: A veteran with a service-connected rating below 100%, or a nonservice-connected disability rated 100% or less, gets an exemption off assessed value of $4,188 (statute base; $4,873 for 2026 after inflation adjustment per Maricopa County) multiplied by the VA disability percentage. Example from Maricopa: $4,873 x 60% = $2,924 off assessed limited property value. Household income must be under the limit ($39,865 with no minor children, $47,826 with minor or disabled children for 2026); the assessed-value cap no longer applies to veterans. Honorable discharge and Arizona residency required. Apply with the county assessor in the January to March 1 window; a surviving spouse of this veteran gets the same prorated amount starting tax year 2027.
benefits.source_title: Maricopa County Assessor: Personal Exemptions and Senior Valuation Relief

benefits.benefit: Full property tax exemption extended to TDIU and income limit removed (tax year 2027)
benefits.details: Laws 2026, Chapter 140 (HB 4168, approved June 13, 2026) adds veterans whose VA status is total disability based on individual unemployability (TDIU) to the full primary-residence exemption and removes the income limit for disabled veterans and their surviving spouses. Section 34(B) says the amended statute applies to tax years beginning from and after December 31, 2026, so TDIU veterans first qualify for tax year 2027. Apply with your county assessor in the January to March 1, 2027 window with your VA letter showing TDIU. A veteran who moves must file an exemption transfer form within 60 days.
benefits.source_title: Laws 2026, Chapter 140 (HB 4168) taxation; omnibus; 2026-2027

benefits.benefit: Vehicle license tax and registration fee exemption (100% disabled)
benefits.details: MVD will not collect the vehicle license tax or registration fee for one personally owned vehicle (or one you co-own) if the VA certifies you as 100% disabled and you are drawing compensation on that basis. The exemption continues for a surviving spouse until remarriage or death. Show a VA letter of eligibility, or a DoD/Uniformed Services ID with the 100% Disabled American Veteran affiliation, at an MVD office when you first register. A vehicle bought with a VA grant is also exempt.
benefits.source_title: ADOT MVD: Vehicle License Tax Exemptions (VA Disability); A.R.S. 28-5802

benefits.benefit: Purple Heart vehicle license tax and registration fee exemption
benefits.details: An honorably discharged Purple Heart recipient pays no vehicle license tax or registration fee on one vehicle. Submit proof of honorable discharge and the Purple Heart award to MVD at initial registration. No disability rating is required.
benefits.source_title: A.R.S. 28-5802 Vehicle license tax exemption; veterans

benefits.benefit: Disability (International Symbol of Access) plates and placard for 100% disabled veterans
benefits.details: A veteran with a 100% VA disability can get international symbol of access special plates or a removable windshield placard by submitting a copy of the VA certificate of 100% disability instead of a medical certificate. The placard is issued at no additional charge, ISA plates are exempt from the $25 special plate fee and the transfer fee, and the plate can be combined with an honored military plate. These plates or placard allow parking in designated accessible spaces (A.R.S. 28-884). Apply through ADOT MVD.
benefits.source_title: A.R.S. 28-2409 International symbol of access special plates; placard

benefits.benefit: Free or reduced-fee hunting and fishing license (Arizona Game and Fish)
benefits.details: A veteran who has lived in Arizona for at least one year and receives VA compensation for a permanent service-connected disability rated 100% gets a complimentary license (fee: none; a VA letter stating 100% permanent and total is required). Veterans with a service-connected rating under 100% and one year of residency get a reduced-fee license ($42), and Purple Heart recipients pay half price ($28). Apply in person at any Game and Fish office or by mail to the Phoenix office with the application form and your VA letter; a paper license is free, a plastic card is $4. If the VA says the 100% rating is permanent, no new certification is needed; if it will be re-evaluated, the license expires after three years.
benefits.source_title: Arizona Game and Fish Department: Disabled Veteran License; A.R.S. 17-333(C)

benefits.benefit: Arizona State Parks free day-use pass (100%) and 50% day-use discount
benefits.details: Veterans with a 100% service-connected disability get a free day-use pass; bring VA-certified proof of the 100% rating to a park visitor center. Retired military and service-disabled veterans rated below 100% get 50% off day-use entry, as do active duty, reserve and National Guard members. The discount covers the pass holder and up to three accompanying adults for day entry only, not camping, tours at Kartchner Caverns or Riordan Mansion, reservations or special events. There is no discounted veteran annual pass as of this review.
benefits.source_title: Arizona State Parks and Trails: Veteran and Military Discounts

benefits.benefit: Purple Heart tuition waiver at Arizona public universities and community colleges
benefits.details: A current or former service member who received the Purple Heart, was an Arizona resident or stationed in Arizona when injured, and has a VA disability rating of 50% or more gets a tuition waiver scholarship at any Arizona Board of Regents university (ASU, NAU, UA) or community college. The Arizona Department of Veterans' Services verifies eligibility; apply through the school's veterans office. A conviction for a class 1 through 5 felony disqualifies you. Arizona National Guard members with a post-9/11 Purple Heart or a medical discharge from state or training duty also qualify.
benefits.source_title: A.R.S. 15-1808 Tuition waiver scholarships; eligibility; definitions

benefits.benefit: Tuition waiver for spouses and children of service members killed in the line of duty
benefits.details: The child or spouse of a service member who was an Arizona resident or stationed in Arizona and was killed in the line of duty (or died from line-of-duty injuries) gets a tuition waiver at any ABOR university or Arizona community college. Children must be 30 or younger and a spouse must not have remarried; the waiver covers up to 64 community college credits and the credits required for a bachelor's degree. The same waiver covers the child or spouse of a veteran or service member who was an Arizona resident, suffered a post-traumatic stress injury in the line of duty and died by suicide. ADVS or the National Guard verifies eligibility.
benefits.source_title: A.R.S. 15-1808 Tuition waiver scholarships; eligibility; definitions

benefits.benefit: Immediate in-state tuition for honorably discharged veterans
benefits.details: An honorably discharged or retired veteran is classified as an in-state student right away at ABOR universities and community colleges if they show objective evidence of intent to live in Arizona (such as an Arizona driver license, voter registration, job or lease). Veterans and others using GI Bill benefits (chapters 30, 31, 33 or 35) who enroll after a discharge from 90 or more days of active duty also get in-state status, and so do service members stationed in Arizona and their spouses and dependents. Ask the school's residency office when you apply.
benefits.source_title: A.R.S. 15-1802 In-state student status

benefits.benefit: Military retirement pay and VA compensation exempt from state income tax
benefits.details: Arizona has an income tax, but for tax year 2021 and later you subtract the full amount of retired or retainer pay of the uniformed services, so military retirement is not taxed (A.R.S. 43-1022, paragraph 26). Active duty pay has not been taxed since 2006 and National Guard and reserve pay is also subtracted. Arizona gross income starts from federal adjusted gross income (A.R.S. 43-1001), so VA disability compensation, which is excluded federally, is not taxed by Arizona. Claim the subtraction on Form 140.
benefits.source_title: Arizona Department of Revenue: Military Tax Filing; A.R.S. 43-1022

benefits.benefit: State and local government hiring preference points
benefits.details: On a merit-system exam for state or local government jobs, a veteran separated under honorable conditions after more than six months of active duty gets 5 points added to a passing score. A veteran with a service-connected disability, or who receives VA compensation or disability retirement, gets 10 points. Certain spouses and surviving spouses (for example of a veteran who died of a service-connected disability or had a total permanent service-connected disability) get 5 points. The maximum is 10 points, and where applicants are not scored the agency applies preference codes. For state jobs upload your DD214 and VA letter to your azstatejobs.gov profile.
benefits.source_title: A.R.S. 38-492 Preferences

benefits.benefit: Arizona Military Family Relief Fund grants
benefits.details: The Military Family Relief Fund, run by the Arizona Department of Veterans' Services, gives financial hardship grants to service members, veterans and families with Arizona ties; the statute lets a subcommittee approve grants of up to $3,000 and the fund runs through December 31, 2031. ADVS materials describe deployment, Arizona residency and honorable-conditions discharge requirements and a $20,000 lifetime cap, but we could not open the ADVS program page to confirm current criteria. Apply online through ADVS (dvs.az.gov) with your DD214, bank statements, pay stubs and the bills you need help with.
benefits.source_title: A.R.S. 41-608.04 Military family relief fund; ADVS MFRF page

benefits.benefit: Arizona State Veteran Homes (Phoenix, Tucson, Yuma, Flagstaff)
benefits.details: ADVS operates skilled-nursing veteran homes in Phoenix, Tucson, Yuma and Flagstaff for veterans, spouses and Gold Star family members who need skilled nursing care. ADVS material indicates the VA pays the full cost for veterans rated 70% or more service-connected. We could not open the ADVS admissions pages during this review, so confirm eligibility, cost and the application packet with ADVS admissions (dvs.az.gov).
benefits.source_title: Arizona Department of Veterans' Services: Arizona State Veteran Homes

states.name: Arkansas
notes: The property tax exemption needs a service-connected 100% rating that the VA calls total AND permanent, or VA special monthly compensation for losing a limb (or its use) or for blindness. A temporary 100% rating does not clearly qualify.
TDIU (unemployability) is not named in the statute. One county says an unemployable veteran may qualify, but we found no statewide rule. Ask your county collector before you count on it.

Since 2025 state law says you send the VA letter to the county collector only once, but some counties (for example Saline County) still ask for it every year with an October 15 deadline. Follow your county's instructions or you may lose a year, because counties do not refund past years.
You must live in the home as your main residence. Rental property and land with no house do not qualify. Up to 160 acres next to the house counts if it is not used for business.
A surviving spouse keeps the property tax exemption only while unmarried. Minor dependent children are also covered.
You cannot stack the disabled veteran exemption with the Amendment 79 homestead credit or the over-65 assessment freeze, according to county collector pages.

Homes owned by a revocable trust, an irrevocable trust you benefit from, or an LLC owned only by you (or you and your spouse) qualify starting with the 2026 assessment year, but you must file trust papers with the collector.

The free Disabled Veteran plate is set by statute at 30% service-connected or totally and permanently disabled, but DFA's web page wording is confusing (it says '100% Non-Service Connected'). Bring your VA letter. Parking in disability spaces is allowed only when the vehicle is actually carrying the disabled veteran.

The $1.50 lifetime hunting or fishing license requires a 100% total and permanent VA rating plus ONE YEAR of Arkansas residency. The 60-day residency rule applies to the 3-year disability licenses, not the lifetime veteran licenses. The 70% (or 50% with Purple Heart) lifetime combo license costs $52.50 and is sold only at the AGFC Little Rock office.

We could not confirm the 50% state park camping discount on the current official parks website. Older official text said parks do NOT accept a DV plate or placard as proof; bring a VA letter dated within two years and call the park first.

There is no state tuition waiver for the veteran. The scholarship (now listed as the Arkansas Heroes Scholarship) is for spouses and children of 100% P&T, POW, MIA or KIA veterans, requires applying for VA Chapter 35 first, and has a July 1 deadline. The 2024 rules also say the veteran must be receiving special monthly compensation.

Arkansas has a state income tax. Military retirement pay and VA compensation are exempt, but if your military retirement exemption is over $6,000 you cannot also take the $6,000 exemption on other retirement income.

benefits.benefit: Homestead and personal property tax exemption
benefits.details: Full exemption from state property taxes on the homestead (home plus up to 160 contiguous non-commercial acres) and personal property registered to the veteran. Qualifies: VA special monthly compensation for loss or loss of use of one or more limbs, total blindness in one or both eyes, or a service-connected 100% total and permanent rating; TDIU is not named in the statute. Surviving spouse (while unmarried) and minor dependent children keep it, including when the member is killed in the line of duty or MIA. Apply at the county collector with your VA letter; since Act 876 of 2025 the letter is required only once, but report any change in status or property and re-file if you move. Many counties still key the letter to the October 15 tax deadline.
benefits.source_title: ADVA Guide to AR Property Taxes (A.C.A. 26-3-306); Acts 407, 876 and 880 of 2025

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran license plate (free)
benefits.details: First Disabled Veteran plate is free; one additional plate costs $4.00, and one plate can be reissued to a surviving spouse for $4.00. By statute (A.C.A. 27-24-203) a disabled veteran is an Arkansas resident rated at least 30% service-connected, or totally and permanently disabled, who owns a vehicle used by or for them (a 2023 bill to lower it to 10% died). DFA's page wording is inconsistent ('100% Non-Service Connected'), so bring your VA letter to the Specialty License Plate Office. Renewal fee not stated on the DFA page.
benefits.source_title: DFA Disabled Veteran License Plate - Free; HB1101 (2023) reprint of A.C.A. 27-24-203

benefits.benefit: Disability-space parking with DV plate
benefits.details: A vehicle displaying an Arkansas Disabled Veteran special plate (or another state's DV plate) may park in spaces reserved for persons with disabilities, but only while the vehicle is actually transporting the disabled veteran (A.C.A. 27-15-316(b)). No separate application; the plate itself is the permit. Threshold follows the plate (30% or P&T).
benefits.source_title: HB1086 (2023) reprint of A.C.A. 27-15-316(b) (bill died; existing text unchanged)

benefits.benefit: Sales tax exemption on VA-financed vehicle and adaptive equipment
benefits.details: Arkansas gross receipts tax rule GR-34 exempts a highway vehicle and adaptive equipment bought by a disabled veteran with VA financial aid under 38 U.S.C. 1901-1905 (the VA automobile grant), proven by a VA letter; a separate exemption covers one automobile every two years for a veteran blinded by service-connected injury. Claim it at the DFA revenue office when registering. We could not reach the official rule text on a DFA page.
benefits.source_title: DFA Sales and Use Tax (Gross Receipts Tax Rule GR-34, A.C.A. 26-52-401)

benefits.benefit: Resident Disabled Military Veteran lifetime hunting/fishing licenses ($1.50-$3.00)
benefits.details: Lifetime Fishing (VLF) $1.50, Lifetime Hunting (VLH) $1.50, or Lifetime Combination (VLC2) $3.00. Veterans must be 100 percent totally and permanently disabled with certification from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and show proof of one year of Arkansas residency. Trout permit, HIP registration and waterfowl stamps are still required where applicable. Buy through AGFC (833-345-0325 or a regional office).
benefits.source_title: AGFC Disability, Mobility-impaired, 65-Plus, Military Retiree, Lifetime Licenses

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran Lifetime Combination License and Permit (VLL2) $52.50
benefits.details: One-time $52.50 lifetime license covering hunting, fishing, trout permit and state duck stamp. Open to resident veterans with a service-connected disability rating of 70% or higher, or 50% or higher with a Purple Heart; requires a copy of your VA disability certification and one year of Arkansas residency. Created by Act 729 of 2019. Sold only at the AGFC Little Rock office.
benefits.source_title: AGFC Disability, Mobility-impaired, 65-Plus, Military Retiree, Lifetime Licenses

benefits.benefit: Resident 3-Year Disability hunting/fishing licenses
benefits.details: Reduced-price 3-year licenses: Fishing (RDF) $10.50, Hunting (RDH) $25, Combination $35.50. Requires a 100 percent total and permanent disability certification dated within the last three years from the Social Security Administration, Veterans Affairs or Railroad Retirement, plus proof of 60 days of Arkansas residency. Must recertify at each 3-year renewal. Not veteran-specific, but a VA 100% P&T letter qualifies.
benefits.source_title: AGFC Disability, Mobility-impaired, 65-Plus, Military Retiree, Lifetime Licenses

benefits.benefit: Arkansas State Parks 50% campsite discount
benefits.details: Older official parks text gave U.S. citizens with 100% total and permanent disability a 50% discount on campsite fees year-round (not on cabins, yurts or other rental facilities), with proof being a VA letter dated within the last two years; the parks FAQ said DV plates and placards are not accepted as proof. We could not find this language on the current arkansas.com/state-parks site, so call the park (888-287-2757) before relying on it. Arkansas state parks charge no general entrance fee.
benefits.source_title: Arkansas State Parks - Camping

benefits.benefit: Military Dependents' / Arkansas Heroes Scholarship (spouse and children)
benefits.details: Waives in-state tuition, mandatory fees and on-campus room and board at Arkansas public (and some private nonprofit) colleges for the spouse or dependent child of a veteran the VA has declared 100% totally and permanently disabled from service-connected conditions (the 2024 rules also require that the veteran be receiving special monthly compensation), or of a service member who was POW, MIA, KIA or killed on ordnance delivery after January 1, 1960. Veteran must have been an Arkansas resident at entry into service or be a current resident; student must be a current resident and must first apply for VA Chapter 35 (DEA), which pays first. Up to 8 semesters with a 2.0 GPA and 24 hours per year; children must be under 26; spouses lose it on remarriage. Apply through the ADHE SAMS portal; annual deadline July 1. The portal now lists it as the Arkansas Heroes Scholarship.
benefits.source_title: ADHE Rules Governing the Military Dependents' Scholarship Program (eff. 10/31/2024); SAMS Arkansas Heroes Scholarship

benefits.benefit: Military retirement pay exempt from state income tax
benefits.details: Beginning with tax year 2018 (Act 141 of 2017, A.C.A. 26-51-307), retirement benefits received by a member of the uniformed services, including survivor benefits, are fully exempt from Arkansas income tax with no cap or age limit. Report it on line 17 of Form AR1000F/AR1000NR. Retirees cannot also claim the $6,000 exemption on other retirement income if their military retirement exemption exceeds $6,000; if it is less, the remainder may be used.
benefits.source_title: DFA 2025 AR1000F and AR1000NR Instructions - Military Retirement Exemption (Act 141 of 2017)

benefits.benefit: VA disability compensation not taxed
benefits.details: Arkansas has a state income tax, but DFA's instructions list VA benefits among exempt income: Social Security benefits, VA benefits, Workers' Compensation and Railroad Retirement benefits are exempt from tax. Military disability retirement pay for service-connected injury is also excluded, and Act 238 of 2009 extends the refund deadline when the VA retroactively reclassifies retired pay as disability pay. Nothing to apply for; simply do not report VA compensation as income.
benefits.source_title: DFA 2025 AR1000F and AR1000NR Instructions - Exempt Income

benefits.benefit: State employment veterans preference (5 or 10 points)
benefits.details: State agencies must apply veterans preference in hiring, promotion and retention. With numerical scoring, a qualifying veteran who passes gets 5 points added; a disabled veteran (disability established by VA records), a disabled veteran over 55 entitled to pension or compensation, or the spouse of a disabled veteran whose disability disqualifies them gets 10 points, and 10-point candidates go to the top of the interview list among equal scores. You must be a citizen and resident of Arkansas with substantially equal qualifications, and you must voluntarily submit official proof (DD214, VA letter). Unmarried surviving spouses also qualify. Policy 13 effective May 26, 2026.
benefits.source_title: Arkansas OPM Policy 13: Veterans Preference and Reemployment (A.C.A. 21-3-301 et seq.)

benefits.benefit: Arkansas State Veterans Homes (skilled nursing)
benefits.details: ADVA operates two State Veterans Homes, in Fayetteville (479-444-7001) and North Little Rock (501-683-1406), offering skilled nursing, therapy and hospice. Applicants need an honorable discharge and a medical need for nursing home placement; veterans, veterans' spouses and Gold Star parents may apply. Submit the Inquiry for Admission form by email to the home you choose. Costs are not listed on the page; ask the home about VA per-diem and private pay.
benefits.source_title: ADVA Veteran Homes

benefits.benefit: Concealed handgun carry license fee waived for veterans
benefits.details: Under A.C.A. 5-73-311(a)(2)(B) as amended by Act 888 of 2021, there is no license fee for a concealed handgun carry license if the applicant is a U.S. Armed Forces veteran or currently serving. Submit a copy of your DD214 or similar document or valid military ID with the Arkansas State Police application. Training and background-check requirements still apply.

benefits.benefit: Veteran designation on driver's license or ID
benefits.details: Arkansas residents with an honorable or general-under-honorable-conditions discharge can add a veteran designation to their driver's license or state ID at any Driver Services/revenue office. Bring a DD214, NGB 22, VA Veteran ID card, DD256/257 or DD2 (retired). The regular license or ID fee applies; no disabled veteran fee waiver was found.
benefits.source_title: DFA Driver Services - Military & Veterans

states.name: California
notes: The property tax exemption needs a 100% rating OR pay at the 100% rate for unemployability (TDIU). P&T status is not required. You can also qualify with no rating at all if you are blind in both eyes or lost the use of two or more limbs.

For property tax, the veteran must also have served in wartime or in a campaign with a Congressional medal, or been released in peacetime for a service-connected disability, and must be eligible for VA health care. A peacetime-only veteran with no campaign medal can be turned down.

The low-income property tax exemption must be re-filed with the county assessor every year between January 1 and February 15. File late and you get 90% (through December 10) or 85% (after). The basic exemption is a one-time filing.
Only an UNMARRIED surviving spouse keeps the property tax exemption. Remarrying ends it.

A 100% rating alone does NOT get you Disabled Veteran license plates. The 100% rating must be for a condition that impairs mobility, or you must need an assistive device to move, have lost the use of a limb, or be permanently blind. TDIU is not listed. The fee waiver covers one vehicle only.

California taxes military retirement pay. Starting with tax year 2025 you can exclude up to $20,000 if your federal AGI is $125,000 or less ($250,000 joint). The exclusion ends after tax year 2029 unless extended. VA disability pay is never taxed.

State civil service no longer gives 10 or 15 preference points. Since 2014 any veteran who passes an open exam goes to the top rank. A disabled veteran gets the same preference as any other veteran; the spouse of a 100% disabled veteran also qualifies. It does not apply once you have permanent state civil service status.

The free State Parks pass needs a 50%+ rating AND wartime or foreign-operations service, California residency, and a VA letter dated within one year. Peacetime-only veterans at 50% do not qualify unless they were a POW or Medal of Honor recipient.
California has no free hunting or fishing license for disabled veterans, only a reduced-fee license (about $10) at 50% or higher. Tags and validations still cost extra.

The College Fee Waiver is for dependents, not the veteran. Plan A needs a 100% (totally disabled) wartime veteran and cannot be used with VA Chapter 35. Plan B works with any service-connected rating but the child's own income must be under $22,941 (AY 2026-27). Re-apply every school year at a County Veterans Service Office.
Business license and vendor fee waivers depend on your city or county. CalVet says eligibility differs by local jurisdiction.

Commonly believed but NOT found on an official source: a free DMV disabled parking placard based on rating alone, a free fishing license at 100%, and a full state income tax exemption for military retirement pay. None of these exist in California.

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veterans' Property Tax Exemption
benefits.details: Exempts part of the value of your primary home from property tax: $180,671 (basic) for the 2026 lien date, or $271,009 (low-income) if household income is $81,131 or less; 2027 amounts are $185,889 / $278,836 with an $83,474 income limit. You qualify if the VA rated you 100%, pays you at the 100% rate for unemployability (TDIU), or you are blind in both eyes or lost the use of two or more limbs; the home must be your principal residence and you must have wartime, campaign-medal, or disability-release service. File form BOE-261-G with the county assessor where the home is; first-year filing is due by the next January 1 or 90 days after you qualify, and the low-income level must be re-filed every year January 1 to February 15. Unmarried surviving spouses also qualify.
benefits.source_title: Revenue and Taxation Code 205.5; BOE Letter To Assessors 2026/019 (May 22, 2026); BOE Disabled Veterans' Exemption page

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran (DV) license plates and registration fee exemption
benefits.details: One vehicle (passenger car, motorcycle, or commercial vehicle 8,000 lbs or less, not for hire) is exempt from all DMV registration and license fees except duplicates, and gets DV plates with the wheelchair symbol that carry disabled-person parking privileges when the veteran is driving or riding. You must meet Vehicle Code 295.7: a 100% VA rating for a disease or disorder that substantially impairs mobility, OR being unable to move without an assistive device, OR loss or loss of use of one or more limbs, OR permanent blindness. Submit form REG 256A with a certification from a medical provider, County Veterans Service Officer, CalVet, or the VA, plus proof of identity, to DMV Special Processing Unit, P.O. Box 932345, Sacramento, CA 94232-0001. Plates renew every December 31 at no fee.
benefits.source_title: Vehicle Code 295.7 and 5007; DMV Vehicle Industry Registration Procedures Manual 21.095; DMV form REG 256A

benefits.benefit: Reduced-fee Disabled Veteran hunting license
benefits.details: Honorably discharged veterans with a service-connected rating of 50% or greater can buy the annual hunting license for $9.79 instead of the regular resident fee. Prequalify once by sending CDFW a VA benefit summary letter showing your discharge and rating, a copy of your driver license, and your GO ID (upload to your online customer record, mail to a CDFW license office, or fax 916-419-7585; do not email). After CDFW updates your record you can buy the license anywhere licenses are sold. Tags and validations are still full price.
benefits.source_title: CDFW Reduced-Fee Hunting License and Disabled Entitlements

benefits.benefit: Reduced-fee Disabled Veteran sport fishing license
benefits.details: Honorably discharged veterans with a 50 percent or greater service-connected disability can buy an annual sport fishing license for $10.04 at CDFW offices or $10.54 from license agents (2026 fees); residents and nonresidents both qualify. Prequalify by submitting a VA letter showing discharge and rating with a copy of your driver license and GO ID to CDFW (upload, mail, or fax). The license is valid 365 days from purchase.
benefits.source_title: CDFW Reduced-Fee Sport Fishing Licenses

benefits.benefit: State Parks Distinguished Veteran Pass
benefits.details: A free lifetime pass for free vehicle day use, family camping, and boat use at state park units run by California State Parks. You must be a California resident with an honorable discharge and either a combined rating of 50% or more with service during wartime or operations against a foreign power, former POW status, or the Medal of Honor. Apply online at ReserveCalifornia.com or mail form DPR 619 with your DD-214, a California driver license or ID, and a VA letter dated within one year showing the rating; allow 8 to 10 weeks. The card must be renewed every five years.
benefits.source_title: California State Parks - Distinguished Veteran Pass; DPR 619 application (Rev. 4/2026)

benefits.benefit: College Fee Waiver for Veteran Dependents - Plan A
benefits.details: Waives mandatory systemwide tuition and fees at any California Community College, CSU, or UC campus for the unmarried child (age 14 to 27, or 30 if the child is a veteran), spouse, or unmarried surviving spouse of a wartime veteran who is totally (100%) service-connected disabled or who died of service-connected causes. The veteran must have served at least one day of active duty in a Congress-declared war or earned a campaign or expeditionary medal, and the qualifying event must have happened before the child turned 21. There is no income limit, but Plan A cannot be used at the same time as VA Chapter 35. Apply with form DVS-40 at a County Veterans Service Office each academic year; books, parking, and housing are not covered.
benefits.source_title: CalVet - College Fee Waiver

benefits.benefit: College Fee Waiver for Veteran Dependents - Plan B
benefits.details: Waives mandatory systemwide tuition and fees at CCC, CSU, and UC campuses for the child of a veteran who has any service-connected disability rating (or had one at death, or died of service-related causes). No wartime service or age limit is required, but the child's own income (adjusted gross income plus the value of parental support) for the prior calendar year may not exceed the state poverty level, which is $22,941 for academic year 2026-27. Only children qualify under Plan B, and it may be combined with VA Chapter 35. Apply with form DVS-40 at a County Veterans Service Office every academic year; the student must meet the school's California residency rules.
benefits.source_title: CalVet - College Fee Waiver

benefits.benefit: Nonresident tuition exemption for veterans and GI Bill users
benefits.details: Veterans and dependents who live in California and are eligible for the Montgomery GI Bill, Veterans Readiness and Employment (Ch. 31), Post-9/11 GI Bill, or Chapter 35 DEA are exempt from nonresident tuition at California Community Colleges and CSU campuses, and keep the exemption while continuously enrolled. Separately, a veteran stationed in California on active duty for more than one year right before discharge is exempt from nonresident tuition for one year while establishing residency (must be used within two years of discharge). Apply through the campus admissions or residency office with your DD-214 and VA certificate of eligibility. The statute covers CCC and CSU; check UC campus policy separately.
benefits.source_title: Education Code 68075.7 and 68075.5

benefits.benefit: Military retirement pay exclusion (up to $20,000)
benefits.details: California taxes military retirement pay, but for tax years 2025 through 2029 you can exclude up to $20,000 of federal uniformed services retirement pay from state income if your federal adjusted gross income is $125,000 or less ($250,000 for joint filers or surviving spouses). A separate exclusion of up to $20,000 applies to DoD Survivor Benefit Plan annuity payments under the same income limits. Claim it on Schedule CA (540 or 540NR) when you file. The law (SB 132, 2025) repeals itself December 1, 2030 unless extended.
benefits.source_title: Revenue and Taxation Code 17132.9 and 17132.10; FTB Military page (updated 06/11/2026)

benefits.benefit: VA disability compensation not taxed
benefits.details: California follows federal law: VA disability compensation and lump-sum retroactive VA payments are tax-exempt, not included in income, and not reported on a 1099-R. Combat-Related Special Compensation (CRSC) is also exempt. Concurrent Retirement and Disability Pay (CRDP) is taxable even if you have a VA rating. Nothing to file; just do not report VA compensation as income.
benefits.source_title: Franchise Tax Board - Military (Retirement and disability), last updated 06/11/2026

benefits.benefit: State civil service Veterans' Preference (top rank)
benefits.details: Any veteran with an other-than-dishonorable discharge, the widow or widower of a veteran, or the spouse of a 100% disabled veteran who passes an open (entrance) state civil service exam with a score of 70 or higher is placed in rank 1 of the eligibility list regardless of score. It applies only to open exams, not promotional exams, and ends once you have permanent state civil service status. Apply by mailing form CalHR 1093 with your Member 4 DD-214 (spouses add marriage certificate and the VA 100% award letter) to CalHR Selection Division, 1515 S Street, North Building, Suite 500, Sacramento, CA 95811-7258. Service members within six months of separation can apply early with form CalHR 1094.
benefits.source_title: Government Code 18973.1 and 18973.5; CalHR form 1093 (Rev 07/2025); CalCareers Veterans' Information

benefits.benefit: CalVet Home Loans
benefits.details: State-run home loan program for buying an owner-occupied home in California; most loan products have no down payment requirement and you can use it more than once. You must have served at least 90 days of active duty (wartime or peacetime, not counting training), have a discharge under honorable conditions, and not currently hold a CalVet loan. There is no prior California residency rule and National Guard or reservists ordered to federal active duty qualify. Apply online at calvet.ca.gov/HomeLoans.
benefits.source_title: CalVet Home Loans - New Customer (Am I eligible?)

benefits.benefit: Veterans Homes of California (long-term care)
benefits.details: Eight state-run homes (Barstow, Chula Vista, Fresno, Lancaster, Redding, Ventura, West LA, Yountville) offer independent living, assisted living, skilled nursing, and memory care at affordable cost. You must be 55 or older, homeless, or disabled; a veteran who served on active duty; a California resident; discharged under other than dishonorable conditions; and have medical insurance. Priority admission goes to Medal of Honor recipients, former POWs, homeless veterans, and veterans rated 70% or more service-connected. Apply online through myCalVet or mail the Veterans Home Admission Application (Sections A, B, and physician Section C) to the home you choose; waitlists vary by home.
benefits.source_title: CalVet - Applying for a CalVet Veterans Home

benefits.benefit: Business license, tax and fee waiver for veteran vendors
benefits.details: Honorably discharged veterans who hawk, peddle, or sell goods they own (not services, and not alcohol) can get municipal, county, and state business license fees and taxes waived, and the county or city must issue the license at no cost. CalVet notes eligibility criteria differ by local jurisdiction, so check with your city or county business license office and bring proof of honorable discharge.
benefits.source_title: CalVet - Business License, Tax and Fee Waiver; Business and Professions Code 16102

states.name: Colorado
notes: Property tax: since Jan 1, 2024 you apply at your COUNTY ASSESSOR, not the Division of Veterans Affairs. The window is January 1 to July 1 each year (C.R.S. 39-3-205(1)(b)). Late applications are not held over; they are discarded.

Property tax: TDIU veterans became eligible starting with tax year 2025 (taxes paid in 2026) after voters passed Amendment G on Nov 5, 2024. A 100% rating that is NOT marked permanent does not qualify; the constitution says '100 percent permanent' or 'individual unemployability status.'

Property tax: the Division's FAQ says TDIU veterans must be 'rated at least 70%' and must have 'served on active duty for at least 24 months.' Neither statement appears in the constitution or statute. Needs verification; ask your assessor if it affects you.

Property tax, surviving spouses: a surviving spouse keeps the exemption on the same home if the veteran already had it (C.R.S. 39-3-203(1.5)(a.5)). Gold Star spouses (DIC recipients or line-of-duty death gratuity) qualify in their own right since tax year 2023 (Amendment E). The state page is inconsistent on whether remarriage disqualifies; the constitution is silent.
Property tax: you must own and occupy the home as your primary residence on January 1 of the application year. You cannot stack the senior and veteran exemptions on one home.
C.R.S. 28-5-104 (effective Jan 1, 2025) requires every Colorado state veterans benefit to treat a VA individual unemployability (TDIU) finding the same as a 100% permanent rating.

Vehicle: the 50% rule for DV plates and the ownership tax exemption reads '50% or more, service-connected, permanent disability' (C.R.S. 42-3-304(5)(a)) or loss of use of hands, feet, or vision. Only ONE vehicle per veteran is exempt, and sales tax is still owed. The plain DV plate does NOT allow accessible parking; you need the DV Handicap plate or a placard with a DR 2219 medical certification.

Recreation: the lifetime small game and fishing license threshold dropped from 60% to 50% for applications on or after Jan 1, 2025 (SB 24-161). Some older state pages still say 60%. You must have lived in Colorado six months, and the license is valid only while you remain a resident. The $14 Columbine Pass is NOT the veteran pass; the free Independence Pass (50%+) is.

Recreation: whether DV-plate vehicles are automatically exempt from the $29 Keep Colorado Wild Pass at registration is not addressed on CPW pages. Needs verification; you can decline the pass at registration either way.

Income tax: VA disability compensation is not in federal taxable income, and Colorado tax starts from federal taxable income (C.R.S. 39-22-104), so it is not taxed. No Colorado DOR page states this in so many words. Military retirement subtraction is capped at $15,000 for retirees under 55 through tax year 2028; at 55+ the general pension cap applies ($20,000 at 55 to 64, $24,000 at 65+). No 2026 change.

Education: Colorado has NO general tuition waiver for dependents of 100% P&T veterans. SB26-067 (2026) was postponed indefinitely. The free-tuition law (C.R.S. 23-3.3-205) covers only dependents of Colorado National Guard members killed or permanently disabled on duty, plus police, fire, and search-and-rescue.

Employment: 10 preference points require receiving VA compensation or disability retired pay for a line-of-duty disability (any rating); 5 points for wartime or campaign-badge service; 10 points maximum; no preference for promotions (Colo. Const. Art. XII Sec. 15).
NOT found on any official Colorado source, so not listed: a disabled-veteran business license fee waiver; a free driver's license for 100% veterans; veteran-specific big-game preference points.

benefits.benefit: Veteran with a Disability property tax exemption
benefits.details: Half of the first $200,000 of your home's actual value is exempt from property tax. You need an honorable discharge and a VA rating of 100% permanent and total, OR a VA individual unemployability (TDIU) finding (TDIU counts starting tax year 2025 under Amendment G). You must own and live in the home as your primary residence on January 1. File the state application (DOLA form 15-DPT-AR) with your VA Benefit Summary Letter at your COUNTY ASSESSOR between January 1 and July 1. Once approved you do not reapply unless you move or your VA status changes.
benefits.source_title: Property Tax Exemption, Colorado Division of Veterans Affairs (Colo. Const. Art. X Sec. 3.5; C.R.S. 39-3-203, 39-3-205)

benefits.benefit: Gold Star Spouse and surviving spouse property tax exemption
benefits.details: A surviving spouse can get the same 50%-of-the-first-$200,000 exemption on their primary home. Gold Star spouses qualify if the service member died in the line of duty (and the spouse received the DoD death gratuity) or the veteran died of a service-connected cause and the spouse receives VA DIC. A surviving spouse of a veteran who already had the disabled-veteran exemption keeps it on the same home. Apply at the county assessor between January 1 and July 1 with a VA letter or DD Form 1300.
benefits.source_title: Property Tax Exemption, Colorado Division of Veterans Affairs (Colo. Const. Art. X Sec. 3.5(1)(d), (1.7); C.R.S. 39-3-203(1.5)(a.5))

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran (DV) license plate with registration fee and ownership tax exemption
benefits.details: With an honorable discharge and a VA letter showing a 50% or greater service-connected disability (or loss of use of a hand or foot, or blindness) you get one set of D.V. plates free. That one vehicle is also exempt from Colorado's annual specific ownership tax and registration fees. Sales tax still applies, and extra DV sets cost $50 plus normal taxes and fees. Apply with Form DR 2002, your DD 214, VA letter, and title or registration at your county motor vehicle office. The plain DV plate does not give accessible parking rights, but it does give free entry to state parks.
benefits.source_title: License Plates - Military, Colorado DMV (Form DR 2002 rev. 08/04/25; C.R.S. 42-3-213(5), 42-3-304(5))

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran Handicap plate or accessible parking placard
benefits.details: If you need accessible parking, get the Disabled Veteran Handicap plate (the same 50% VA letter plus Form DR 2219 signed by a licensed medical provider) or a standard placard. Three-year placards are for permanent impairments; temporary placards for short-term ones. Submit the DR 2219 to your county motor vehicle office or through myDMV. The regular DV plate alone does not allow parking in accessible spaces.
benefits.source_title: Persons with Disabilities, Colorado DMV (Form DR 2219)

benefits.benefit: Purple Heart license plate
benefits.details: Any Purple Heart recipient can get Purple Heart plates. The first set is exempt from fees (C.R.S. 42-3-213(1)(b)(II)(D)) and Form DR 2002 lists it as exempt from ownership taxes and registration fees for one vehicle; additional sets cost $50 plus taxes and fees. Apply with Form DR 2002 and a DD 214 or orders showing the award. Purple Heart plates also give free entry to Colorado state parks.
benefits.source_title: License Plates - Military, Colorado DMV

benefits.benefit: VETERAN indicator and military identifier on driver license or ID
benefits.details: You can have the word VETERAN and/or your branch's military identifier printed on your Colorado driver license or ID card. Bring an original Member 4 copy of your DD-214 or a valid military ID to a driver license office appointment. Once added you do not show the documents again at renewal, and there is no added fee when done at renewal. The indicator is accepted as proof of veteran status for the free August state parks pass.
benefits.source_title: Active Duty Military and Veterans, Colorado DMV

benefits.benefit: Free lifetime small game hunting and fishing combination license
benefits.details: Colorado resident veterans with a VA combined service-connected rating of 50% or more (lowered from 60% for applications on or after January 1, 2025), and Purple Heart recipients, get a free lifetime resident small game and fishing combo license. You must have lived in Colorado at least six months, hold a Colorado DL or ID, and have hunter education if you want to hunt. Holders skip the annual Habitat Stamp, and the license counts as a qualifying license for big game draws. Apply with CPW's Veteran License application by email, through your cpwshop.com account, or by mail; allow 15 business days.
benefits.source_title: Hunters with Disabilities, Colorado Parks and Wildlife (C.R.S. 33-4-104(3) as amended by SB 24-161)

benefits.benefit: Independence Pass: free annual state parks pass for disabled veterans
benefits.details: The Independence Pass gives free vehicle entry to all Colorado state parks for 12 months at no cost. Colorado residents qualify with a VA letter showing a discharge other than dishonorable and compensation for a 50% or greater disability (combined ratings count), or loss of use of hands or feet or blindness; Purple Heart recipients also qualify. Apply with CPW's Veteran's License and Pass Application by email, mail, or in person at CPW headquarters in Denver; allow 15 business days. Residents with DV or Purple Heart plates can enter free without any pass when the veteran is in the vehicle.
benefits.source_title: Park Specialty Passes, Colorado Parks and Wildlife

benefits.benefit: Free state park entry in August (Military Parks Pass)
benefits.details: Every August, active-duty military, veterans, and National Guard members get a free pass for entry to any Colorado state park.
