benefits.source_title: GDVS - State War Veterans Homes: Eligibility Criteria

benefits.benefit: Georgia VECTR Center (Veterans Education Career Transition Resource Center)
benefits.details: A state-backed center in Warner Robins run with Central Georgia Technical College that offers accelerated career training at little or no cost to Georgia residents, service members stationed in Georgia, and transitioning military, plus a testing center, employment connections, a Veterans Business Outreach Center, and on-site GDVS claims officers. Open to the public. Contact the center at 1001 S. Armed Forces Blvd, Warner Robins, GA 31088.
benefits.source_title: Georgia VECTR Center

states.name: Hawaii

agency.name: Hawaii Office of Veterans' Services (State Department of Defense)

notes: Hawaii has no state property tax. Each of the four counties (City and County of Honolulu, Maui, Hawaii, Kauai) sets its own disabled veteran exemption, threshold, deadline and minimum tax. Check your own county's real property office. The Office of Veterans' Services only links to the counties; it does not run the program.

None of the four county rules name TDIU (total disability based on individual unemployability) or permanent and total (P&T). Honolulu and Hawaii County use the words 'totally disabled' from active duty injuries; Honolulu's 2026 guide says '100% totally disabled.' Kauai starts at 80 percent and Maui at 70 percent, so a TDIU veteran rated 70 percent or more clears those two counties on the schedular rating alone. For Honolulu and Hawaii County, ask the county whether a TDIU letter counts before you rely on it.

County deadlines differ. Honolulu now has no annual deadline for the totally disabled veteran claim; file before the Aug. 19 or Feb. 19 tax payment date. Hawaii County: June 30 or December 31. Maui: December 31. Kauai: September 30, and you must already hold the regular home exemption. The home must be your owner occupied principal residence in every county, and a minimum tax still applies ($300 Honolulu, $150 Kauai, half of the minimum tax in Maui and Hawaii County).
A surviving spouse keeps the county exemption only while unmarried and, in most counties, only while living in the same home. The exemption does not move to a new house.

The state waives the $46 annual state vehicle registration fee for one non-commercial vehicle if you are a Hawaii resident with a VA 100 percent service-connected rating (P&T is not required). You must get a new letter from the Office of Veterans' Services every year; the county DMV will not take last year's letter. County weight tax and county fees still apply unless you were furnished a car by the VA (then the county weight tax is also waived on that one car under HRS 249-6).

Bills to replace the $46 fee waiver with a full vehicle weight tax exemption for 100 percent disabled veterans (HB 657 of 2025, SB 607 of 2025 and 2026) did not pass. As of October 2026 the law is unchanged.

Hawaii has no disabled veteran or veteran discount on hunting or freshwater fishing licenses and no veteran park pass. The good news is that resident rates are low ($10 hunting, $5 freshwater fishing, free at age 65), Hawaii residents never need a license for ocean fishing, and residents pay nothing to enter or park at state parks. You must have lived in Hawaii one year to be a resident for hunting.

Hawaii has no state tuition waiver for veterans or for the children or spouses of disabled veterans. Bills to create one (SB 951 and HB 426 in 2021 and 2022) did not pass. What you do get is the resident tuition rate at every University of Hawaii campus if you use GI Bill, VR&E, Fry or DEA benefits and live in Hawaii.

Hawaii does not tax military retired pay, VA disability compensation, or other federal benefits that are tax free under federal law. There is no age limit or dollar cap on the military pension exclusion. Reserve and National Guard drill pay is excluded up to $8,636 for 2025.

State civil service preference is 5 points for honorable service and 10 points if a VA or service letter dated within the past 12 months confirms you qualify for the 10 point preference. The statute (HRS 76-103) leaves the details to rules, and the state's job notice does not list a disability percentage. Points apply only to open competitive recruitments.

The state special housing grant is a one time payment of up to $5,000 and only tops up a VA Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) grant. You must have been a bona fide Hawaii resident before you entered the service, and the money depends on the Legislature funding it. Ask the Office of Veterans' Services whether funds are available before you plan on it.

benefits.benefit: City and County of Honolulu: totally disabled veteran real property tax exemption (ROH 8-10.5)
benefits.details: Honolulu exempts real property owned and occupied by a veteran who is '100% totally disabled due to service related injuries while on active duty with U.S. Armed Forces.' You still pay the minimum real property tax, currently $300 a year. The exemption passes to a widow or widower who remains unmarried and keeps owning and living in the home. There is no annual filing deadline; file Form BFS-RP-E-8-10.5 with the Real Property Assessment Division and the exemption starts with the next tax payment date (Aug. 19 or Feb. 19) after you file. The county's words are 'totally disabled,' not permanent and total, and TDIU is not mentioned, so ask the county if you are rated under TDIU.
benefits.source_title: City and County of Honolulu Real Property Assessment Division - Totally Disabled Veterans (Revised Ordinances of Honolulu 8-10.5); RPAD Information Guide rev. 2026-06-26

benefits.benefit: Maui County: severely disabled (70%+) and totally disabled veteran property tax exemptions (MCC 3.48.475)
benefits.details: Maui County Code section 3.48.475 defines 'severely disabled' as 'a 70 percent or higher disability rating by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs.' A severely disabled veteran who owns and occupies a home pays only 50 percent of the minimum real property tax instead of the normal bill (the county reported the minimum tax at $350 when the rule passed in 2022). File the Claim for Disability Exemption, Severely Disabled Veteran, with the Real Property Assessment Division by December 31 for the next tax year; the county verifies your rating with the VA. The county also has an older totally disabled veteran exemption, but the county web pages blocked our review, so confirm the current amounts, the 100 percent rule and surviving spouse terms with the division at (808) 270-7297.
benefits.source_title: County of Maui Real Property Assessment Division - Claim for Disability Exemption, Severely Disabled Veteran (Maui County Code 3.48.475); Maui County Council press release July 13, 2022 (Bill 110, CD1)

benefits.benefit: Hawaii County: totally disabled veteran real property tax exemption (Form 19-73)
benefits.details: Hawaii County exempts the principal home of a veteran who is totally disabled from injuries received on active duty, except for special assessments and half of the annual minimum tax (the county lists the minimum tax at $200). The county says the program requires 100 percent disability and that you must already have the homeowner exemption. File Form 19-73 with the Real Property Tax Division by June 30 for the first half payment or December 31 for the second half. The exemption continues while you stay totally disabled or while your surviving spouse stays unmarried. Any part of the home used for business is not covered. The county website blocked automated review, so confirm the current rules with the division (Hilo 808-961-8201, Kona 808-323-4880).
benefits.source_title: County of Hawaii Real Property Tax Division - Exemptions/Programs (Hawaii County Code ch. 19; Form 19-73)

benefits.benefit: Kauai County: disabled veteran property tax exemption (80%+ full; under 80% up to $50,000)
benefits.details: Kauai gives two tiers. A veteran who is '80% to totally disabled due to injuries sustained while on duty as a member of the United States Armed Forces' and who holds the county home exemption is 'exempt from all property tax (with the exclusion of multi-unit properties) except the minimum tax of $150' ($75 if you also qualify for the income based additional exemption). A disabled veteran who is 'less than 80% disabled' gets an exemption of up to $50,000 of value on top of the home exemption. File RP Form P-6 and the Claim for Home Exemption (P-3) with the Real Property Assessment Division on or before September 30 for the next tax year. After the veteran dies, the surviving spouse, civil union partner or reciprocal beneficiary keeps the benefit on the same home while unmarried and living there.
benefits.source_title: County of Kauai Department of Finance, Real Property Assessment - Exemption/Tax Relief Information (Kauai County Code 5A-11.4); Understanding Your Real Property Taxes, rev. 1/22/2026

benefits.benefit: State vehicle registration fee ($46) exemption for 100% service-connected veterans (HRS 249-31.5)
benefits.details: If you are a Hawaii resident, were discharged other than dishonorably, and the VA rates you with 'a service-connected one hundred per cent disability rating for compensation or a service-connected disability rating of one hundred per cent,' you do not pay the $46 annual state registration fee on one non-commercial vehicle. Permanent and total status is not required. You still pay the county weight tax, county registration fee and other charges. Request an original eligibility letter from the Office of Veterans' Services each year (it is mailed to you) and present it to your county DMV when you renew; the DMV will not accept a prior year's letter. The vehicle must have a current registration and safety check.
benefits.source_title: Hawaii Revised Statutes 249-31.5 Exemptions from registration fees for certain vehicles; disabled veterans; Office of Veterans' Services - Benefits and Services

benefits.benefit: County vehicle weight tax exemption for a car furnished by the VA (HRS 249-6)
benefits.details: Passenger cars 'owned by persons who, by reason of their service disability, have been furnished such cars by the federal government and have been so certified by the Department of Veterans Affairs' are exempt from the county vehicle weight tax. This covers a car bought with a VA automobile grant, which the VA gives for specific service-connected disabilities such as loss of use of a hand or foot or certain vision loss, not for a rating percentage. The exemption covers only one vehicle and not a vehicle used for business. Bring the VA certification to your county motor vehicle office.
benefits.source_title: Hawaii Revised Statutes 249-6 Exemptions for certain cars furnished to disabled veterans

benefits.benefit: Veteran, Combat Wounded (Purple Heart), war era and Gold Star special license plates (HRS 249-9.2)
benefits.details: Your county finance director issues, for a fee, one set of special plates marked VETERAN, COMBAT WOUNDED (Purple Heart), COMBAT VETERAN, PEARL HARBOR SURVIVOR, FORMER PRISONER OF WAR, WORLD WAR II, KOREA, VIETNAM, PERSIAN GULF, IRAQ or AFGHANISTAN VETERAN, or GOLD STAR FAMILY. You need proof of the award or VA or Office of Veterans' Services certification of your service, plus a discharge paper showing an honorable or general (under honorable conditions) discharge. The Office of Veterans' Services says the cost is the same as a regular plate; there is no free plate for disabled veterans. Plates go on a non-commercial car, motorcycle or scooter registered in your name and cannot be transferred; a survivor may keep the front plate as a memorial.
benefits.source_title: Hawaii Revised Statutes 249-9.2 Special number plates; military service (am. L 2024, c 83)

benefits.benefit: Honolulu: $20 county vehicle registration fee exemption for veterans age 65 and older (from July 1, 2026)
benefits.details: Starting July 1, 2026, veterans 'of the U.S. armed forces 65 and older who were not dishonorably discharged' living on Oahu can have the $20 City and County of Honolulu registration fee waived on one non-commercial vehicle each year. It does not waive the $46 state fee, state or county weight tax, the $7 beautification fee or plate fees. Apply once in person at a satellite city hall (schedule an AlohaQ appointment) with form CS-L(MVR)50B, proof of veteran status, age and vehicle ownership; the exemption stays with the vehicle until you remove it. The City Council passed Bill 62 (2024) in October 2025 and the mayor signed it in November 2025. Other counties do not offer this.
benefits.source_title: City and County of Honolulu Department of Customer Services - Veterans Benefit (Bill 62 (2024), CD2)

benefits.benefit: Hunting, fishing and state parks: no veteran discount; resident rates and free resident park entry
benefits.details: Hawaii has no veteran or disabled veteran discount on hunting or fishing licenses and no veteran park pass; the only free licenses are for residents age 65 and older. A resident hunting license is $10 after one year of Hawaii residency (active duty members and families count as residents), plus a $10 Wildlife Conservation Stamp and hunter education proof; non-residents pay $95. A freshwater game fishing license is $5 for residents and military. Hawaii residents need no license to fish in the ocean; only non-residents age 15 and over must buy a marine license ($20 one day, $40 seven days, $70 annual), and active duty members stationed in Hawaii and their families are exempt. State parks that charge (such as Diamond Head and Haena) list 'Residents = Free with Hawaii DL or ID' for entry and parking, while non-residents pay $5 per person and $10 per vehicle; resident tent camping is $20 a night and non-resident $30. Show your Hawaii driver license or state ID.
benefits.source_title: Hawaii Revised Statutes 183D-22 Hunting licenses; fees; HRS 188-72 Nonresident recreational marine fishing license; DLNR Freshwater Game Fishing License; DLNR Division of State Parks Haena fees

benefits.benefit: University of Hawaii resident tuition for GI Bill, VR&E, Fry and DEA users (Regents Policy 6.208)
benefits.details: Board of Regents Policy RP 6.208 (effective Aug. 15, 2024) exempts from non-resident tuition at every UH campus: veterans using Post-9/11 or Montgomery GI Bill benefits, people using transferred Post-9/11 benefits, Fry Scholarship and Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance (DEA) users, and 'veterans with service-connected disabilities' using the VR&E (chapter 31) program, as long as they live in Hawaii, or move away but stay continuously enrolled. Dependents of active duty members transferred out of Hawaii also keep the resident rate. Hawaii has no state tuition waiver or scholarship for veterans or for children and spouses of disabled veterans; proposals in 2021 and 2022 did not pass. Apply through your campus Residency Officer.
benefits.source_title: University of Hawaii Board of Regents Policy RP 6.208 Board Exemptions to Non-Resident Tuition (eff. Aug. 15, 2024); UH Student Affairs - Veterans and Military Connected

benefits.benefit: No state income tax on military retired pay or VA disability pay; reserve and Guard pay exclusion (HRS 235-7)
benefits.details: Hawaii excludes from taxable income 'any compensation received in the form of a pension for past services' and any income the United States exempts from federal tax. The Department of Taxation's Form N-11 instructions say Hawaii 'does not tax qualifying distributions ... from a government retirement system (e.g., federal civil service, military pension, state or county retirement system)' paid by reason of retirement, disability or death; subtract the amount on the pension line. There is no age limit or cap. VA disability compensation and DIC are federally tax free and are not taxed by Hawaii. Reserve and Hawaii National Guard duty pay is excluded up to $8,636 for tax year 2025. Hawaii does tax active duty pay of residents.
benefits.source_title: Hawaii Revised Statutes 235-7(a) Other provisions as to gross income; Hawaii Department of Taxation 2025 Form N-11 Instructions (Pensions; National Guard Duty Pay Exclusion)

benefits.benefit: State civil service veterans preference points, 5 or 10 points (HRS 76-103)
benefits.details: On open competitive state recruitments, you get 5 veterans preference points added to your passing score by submitting your DD-214 (Member 4) showing honorable service. You get 10 points if you submit 'an official statement/letter from the U.S. Department of Veteran Affairs or armed service dated within the past 12 months which confirms your qualification to receive 10 points preference.' The statute says preference for veterans, disabled veterans, spouses of disabled veterans and unremarried surviving spouses 'shall be provided by rules and regulations,' and the state notice does not list a disability percentage for the 10 point tier. Claim the points when you apply through the Department of Human Resources Development. Counties run their own systems with similar 5 and 10 point rules.
benefits.source_title: Hawaii Revised Statutes 76-103 Veteran's preference; DHRD Important Information for job announcements (Veterans Preference Points)

benefits.benefit: State special housing grant up to $5,000 for VA Specially Adapted Housing grant recipients (HRS 363-11)
benefits.details: The Office of Veterans' Services may pay 'a grant not to exceed $5,000 to remodel or purchase a home for a disabled veteran.' You must be approved for a federal VA Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) grant, have been 'a bona fide resident of the State before entering active service,' live in Hawaii when the VA grant is approved and when you apply, and the home must be in Hawaii and be your permanent residence. The state cannot pay more than the VA pays, the grant is made only once, and it depends on money being appropriated. The state sends the money to the VA regional office escrow once the VA grant is ready to close. Apply on the office's form; call OVS at (808) 433-0420.
benefits.source_title: Hawaii Revised Statutes 363-11 Special housing for disabled veterans; Hawaii Administrative Rules 7-31-4.1 (State Department of Defense)

benefits.benefit: Hawaii State Veterans Cemetery (Kaneohe) and county veterans cemeteries; no cost gravesite and marker
benefits.details: The state cemetery in Kaneohe, Oahu buries veterans of the U.S. Armed Forces and their eligible dependents: spouses, children under 21 (under 23 if in school), and unmarried adult children disabled before age 21. The state provides the gravesite, flat granite or bronze marker, grave opening and closing, a vault liner for casket burials (subject to funds) and perpetual care at no charge; the VA pays the plot allowance for the veteran. Families pay the funeral home and transportation, and an urn vault if needed. Gravesites cannot be reserved; your funeral director contacts the cemetery (808-369-3575) with the veteran's DD-214 or other discharge record. County run veterans cemeteries serve Hawaii Island (Hilo and Kona), Maui, Molokai, Lanai and Kauai.
benefits.source_title: Hawaii Office of Veterans' Services - Arranging for Burial in the Hawaii State Veterans Cemetery (Kaneohe), revised 2/12/2024; OVS Veteran Cemeteries

benefits.benefit: State veterans homes: Yukio Okutsu (Hilo) and Daniel K. Akaka (Kapolei) State Veterans Homes
benefits.details: Hawaii runs two skilled nursing homes for veterans, overseen by the Office of Veterans' Services: the Yukio Okutsu State Veterans Home in Hilo (808-961-1500) and the Daniel K. Akaka State Veterans Home in Kapolei, Oahu (apply through the online form on the OVS page). Earlier OVS material said residents must be veterans in good standing who meet general VA eligibility and were Hawaii residents before entering the military or have lived in Hawaii more than a year before applying, but the current OVS page lists no criteria and says to contact the home or your primary care doctor. Confirm eligibility, cost share and any waiting list with the home.
benefits.source_title: Hawaii Office of Veterans' Services - State Veteran Homes

states.name: Idaho
notes: Idaho does not fully exempt a disabled veteran's home from property tax. The main benefit is a reduction of up to $1,500 a year on your home and up to one acre. The law (Idaho Code 63-705A) covers a veteran with 'a service-connected disability of one hundred percent (100%)' or 'a disability rating based on individual unemployability rating that is compensated at the one hundred percent (100%) disability rate.' So a 100% schedular rating and TDIU both count. You do not need a permanent and total (P&T) rating to get the money. P&T only matters for one thing: if you are 100% P&T you do not have to reapply every year.

Property tax deadlines are strict. You must own and live in the home as your primary residence by April 15, the home must already have an Idaho homeowner's exemption, and you must apply between January 1 and April 15 each year (online through the Tax Commission's TAP portal or on paper with your county assessor). Most veterans must reapply every year. If you buy a new home after April 15 but before October 1, tell the Tax Commission before October 1 and the benefit can move with you. The benefit does not reduce solid waste, irrigation or other fees.

Surviving spouse: if the veteran applied and then died, the spouse keeps the $1,500 reduction for that year and future years 'until such time as the surviving spouse remarries, dies, or no longer has property tax levied on the homestead.' The Tax Commission says the benefit is not transferable to a new property after the veteran dies. Any widow or widower, with or without a veteran connection, can also apply for the income-tested Property Tax Reduction (circuit breaker).

The Property Tax Reduction (circuit breaker) is a separate, income-tested program. A veteran with a service-connected rating of 10% or more (or a VA pension for a non-service-connected disability) is an eligible claimant. For 2027 taxes your 2026 income after medical expenses must be $40,030 or less. VA disability compensation counts as income unless your rating is 40% or more; DIC does not count. The reduction is $250 to $1,500. Homes valued above the greater of $400,000 or 200% of your county's median are not eligible. You can get both the circuit breaker and the $1,500 veteran reduction, but the total cannot exceed your actual tax bill.

The free Disabled Veteran (DV) license plate waives registration fees on one vehicle at a time. The statute keys on receiving VA compensation 'for one hundred percent (100%) service-connected disability' or loss of use of a hand, foot or both eyes. The ITD application form says '100% service-connected permanent disability' and asks for a 100% rating letter; it does not mention TDIU. If you are TDIU or 100% without a P&T letter, confirm with ITD Special Plates before you count on it. The DV plate comes with a disability placard and lets you park free at meters and without time limits in time-restricted zones.

Idaho has no vehicle sales tax exemption for disabled veterans and no driver license fee waiver. Adding the 'VETERAN' designation to your license is free only when you get a new or renewed license; at any other time you pay the duplicate license fee. The Purple Heart plate waives only the plate fee (you still pay registration) unless you also qualify for the DV fee exemption. The Medal of Honor plate is free but regular registration fees apply.

Hunting and fishing: Idaho does not give free licenses to disabled veterans. Resident veterans with a VA rating of 40% or more get a $5 Disabled American Veteran (DAV) license and sharply reduced tags and permits; nonresident veterans at 40% or more get a reduced-fee hunting license and a limited pool of DAV deer and elk tags. You must send your VA 'Benefits Summary' percentage letter to Fish and Game once. The Idaho State Parks Veteran Pass is stricter: you must be an Idaho resident rated 100% permanent and total. The Parks application says 'Being compensated at 100% does not qualify,' so TDIU and non-permanent 100% ratings are excluded.

Education: Idaho has no state tuition waiver for veterans themselves. In-state tuition for GI Bill users comes from federal law, not Idaho law. The Armed Forces and Public Safety Officer Dependent Scholarship (Idaho Code 33-4302) pays tuition and fees, up to $750 per term for books, and on-campus housing for the spouse or child of an Idaho resident service member who is a POW or MIA, died of wounds from active duty, or is 'determined to be unemployable due to' such injuries (VA individual unemployability or an SSA finding). A 100% rating alone does not meet the statute's wording. Operation Education at the University of Idaho is a scholarship, not an entitlement, and is limited to post-9/11 veterans with a permanent service-connected disability.

Income tax: Idaho taxes military retired pay but allows a deduction. Since the 2025 law change (House Bill 40, retroactive to January 1, 2025), a retired service member qualifies if 'classified as disabled' at any age, is 62 or older, or is under 62 and worked enough to have to file a federal return. 'Disabled' includes 'a veteran of a U.S. war with a service-connected disability rating of 10% or more.' The 2025 cap is $48,216 (single) or $72,324 (married filing jointly), reduced by any Social Security or Railroad Retirement you and your spouse receive. VA disability compensation is not in federal adjusted gross income, so Idaho does not tax it.

State hiring preference adds 5 points to a passing score for any veteran (90 days of active duty, honorable or general discharge) and 10 points for a veteran with a 10% or higher service-connected rating or a Purple Heart. Veterans rated 30% or more must be offered an interview if they are among the qualified applicants. Points apply only to your first hire, not promotions. Unremarried widows and widowers get the same points, and the spouse of a disabled veteran who cannot work in public employment gets 10 points.

2025 and 2026 law changes: the $1,500 property tax benefit itself was last changed in 2023 (House Bill 258); nothing in the 2025 or 2026 sessions changed it or the DV plate law. The 2025 session broadened the military retirement deduction (H0040, ch. 13, and trailer H0479, ch. 302). The 2026 session passed only a veterans code cleanup (S1273, ch. 44) and a veterans benefits consumer protection law (S1286, ch. 145); neither changes benefit eligibility described here.

benefits.benefit: Special property tax reduction of up to $1,500 for 100% or TDIU veterans (Idaho Code 63-705A)
benefits.details: Your property tax (or occupancy tax) on your Idaho home and up to one acre is cut by $1,500 or your whole bill, whichever is less. You qualify with a VA 'service-connected disability of one hundred percent (100%)' or a 'disability rating based on individual unemployability rating that is compensated at the one hundred percent (100%) disability rate' as of January 1. A 100% schedular rating does not need to be permanent; TDIU counts. The home must be your primary residence by April 15 and already have the homeowner's exemption; a mobile home counts. There is no income limit. Apply between January 1 and April 15 online (Tax Commission TAP portal) or on paper with your county assessor, with your current VA rating letter. If you are 100% permanent and total you do not have to reapply each year; everyone else reapplies annually. If you move after April 15 but before October 1, notify the Tax Commission before October 1 to transfer the benefit. Fees such as solid waste and irrigation are not reduced.
benefits.source_title: Idaho Legislature - Idaho Code 63-705A Special property tax or occupancy tax reduction for disabled veterans; Idaho State Tax Commission - Property Tax Benefit for Veterans with Disabilities (updated Sept. 22, 2026)

benefits.benefit: Property Tax Reduction (circuit breaker) for veterans rated 10% or more, income-tested
benefits.details: A separate program reduces property tax on your home and up to one acre by $250 to $1,500 depending on income. You are an eligible claimant if on January 1 you are 'a disabled veteran of any war engaged in by the United States, whose disability is recognized as a service-connected disability of a degree of ten percent (10%) or more, or who has a pension for nonservice-connected disabilities.' You must own and live in the home as your primary residence by April 15 and have the homeowner's exemption. For 2027 taxes, your 2026 household income after medical expenses must be $40,030 or less. VA disability compensation counts as income unless your rating is 40% or more; DIC does not count. Homes assessed above the greater of $400,000 or 200% of the county median are not eligible (they are referred to the deferral program). Apply January 1 to April 15 online or with your county assessor every year. You can stack this with the $1,500 veteran reduction, but the total cannot exceed your actual tax.
benefits.source_title: Idaho Legislature - Idaho Code 63-701 Definitions (claimant, homestead, income) and 63-705 Amount of reduction; Idaho State Tax Commission - Property Tax Reduction page (updated Sept. 23, 2026)

benefits.benefit: Surviving spouse keeps the $1,500 veteran reduction; widows and widowers eligible for circuit breaker
benefits.details: If a qualified veteran applied for the $1,500 reduction and then died, 'the veteran's surviving spouse is entitled to receive the special tax reduction in that year and subsequent years, until such time as the surviving spouse remarries, dies, or no longer has property tax levied on the homestead.' The spouse must keep living in the same home; the Tax Commission says the benefit is not transferable to a new property after the veteran's death. Separately, any widow or widower (no veteran link needed) is an eligible claimant for the income-tested Property Tax Reduction of $250 to $1,500, with the same April 15 deadline and $40,030 income limit for 2027. DIC and death benefits from the VA do not count as income for that program.
benefits.source_title: Idaho State Tax Commission - Property Tax Benefit for Veterans with Disabilities (updated Sept. 22, 2026); Idaho Code 63-705A(3) and 63-701(1)(c)

benefits.benefit: Free Disabled Veteran (DV) license plate, registration fee waiver, and disability parking privileges
benefits.details: No registration fee is charged on one vehicle at a time owned by a veteran 'receiving compensation from the veterans administration ... for one hundred percent (100%) service-connected disability' or for loss or loss of use of a hand or foot, or blindness in both eyes. ITD issues the DV plate (counties cannot) with a disability placard, and the plate gives the parking privileges of Idaho Code 49-410(7): free parking at meters, unlimited time in time-restricted zones, and use of accessible spaces. The ITD form (ITD 3397, rev. 7/24) says applicants 'must be a veteran with a 100% service-connected permanent disability' and must send a 100% VA rating letter; it does not mention TDIU, so TDIU veterans should confirm with ITD Special Plates first. A Purple Heart recipient who qualifies may choose a fee-free Service-Connected Disabled Purple Heart plate instead. Apply by mail (ITD Special Plates, PO Box 7129, Boise ID 83707-1129) or email specialplates@itd.idaho.gov; vehicles over 26,000 pounds are excluded. Limited to one set.
benefits.source_title: Idaho Legislature - Idaho Code 49-403 Disabled veteran license plates (am. 2023, ch. 16); Idaho Code 49-410(7); ITD Form 3397 Disabled Veteran Plates Application (Rev. 7/24)

benefits.benefit: Purple Heart and Medal of Honor plates; free VETERAN designation on driver license at renewal
benefits.details: Purple Heart plates (Idaho Code 49-403A) are open to any veteran or service member with a DD-214, medal certificate or orders showing the award; you pay regular registration but 'shall not be charged the plate fee,' may put them on several vehicles, and a surviving spouse may keep or reapply for them within 5 years of the death. Medal of Honor plates (49-415A) are free, cover up to two vehicles, and need VA certification; regular registration fees still apply. Idaho does not waive driver license fees for veterans. Any honorably discharged veteran can add the word VETERAN to a driver license or ID card by showing a DD-214 (copy 4), VA ID card, 100% disabled veteran letter or other listed proof; there is 'no additional charge' when done with a new or renewed license, but 'a duplicate fee' applies at any other time. Apply for Purple Heart plates with ITD Form 3398; for Medal of Honor plates call ITD Special Plates at (208) 334-8649.
benefits.source_title: Idaho Legislature - Idaho Code 49-403A Purple heart recipient license plates; 49-415A Congressional medal of honor license plates; ITD Veteran Designation flyer (Revised 11-16-23)

benefits.benefit: Reduced-fee Disabled American Veteran (DAV) hunting and fishing licenses and tags (40% or more)
benefits.details: Idaho Fish and Game sells a $5 DAV license to resident veterans whose VA letter shows 'a service-connected disability rating of 40% or greater.' DAV holders then buy reduced tags: deer $10.75, elk $16.50, bear $6.75, turkey $10.75, and archery or muzzleloader permits $3.75 each. Nonresident veterans at 40% or more can buy a $31.75 DAV hunting license with 3-day fishing, and reduced deer ($23.75) and elk ($39.75) tags from a yearly pool of 500 deer and 300 elk DAV tags. Send your one-page VA Benefits Summary percentage letter once by email (licenses@idfg.idaho.gov), mail (Licensing Section, PO Box 25, Boise ID 83707) or at any regional office; you do not resend it later. Fish and Game also offers 5 free Disabled Veterans Special Big Game Tags each year (deer, elk, pronghorn, bear or mountain lion) through a sponsoring nonprofit; apply January 2 to 31. Licenses are not free in Idaho.
benefits.source_title: Idaho Department of Fish and Game - Disabled Veterans Programs (DAV reduced fees; Disabled Veterans Special Big Game Tag Program)

benefits.benefit: Idaho State Parks Veteran Pass: free vehicle entry and free campsite for 100% P&T Idaho residents
benefits.details: A lifetime, non-transferable pass that 'Waives the Motor Vehicle Entrance Fee for one personal vehicle' for day use and 'Waives the Usage Fees for one campsite per eligible veteran' (not cabins, yurts or lodges; reservation and transaction fees still apply; 14-night limit in 30 days per park). You must meet all three: 'A Resident of Idaho,' 'Service-connected disability,' and 'VA evaluation of 100% Permanent & Total.' The application states 'Being compensated at 100% does not qualify,' so TDIU and non-permanent 100% ratings are excluded. Apply online at parksandrecreation.idaho.gov, or email IDPRVeteran@idpr.idaho.gov or mail the Veteran Pass application with your VA letter (or your Idaho DV plate number) to Idaho Department of Parks and Recreation, Attn: Veteran Pass Program, PO Box 83720, Boise ID 83720-0065. Processing can take up to 90 days and you need the card in hand to get the discount.
benefits.source_title: Idaho Department of Parks and Recreation - Idaho State Parks Veteran Pass Program application and brochure (2025); IDPR Discounts and Fees page

benefits.benefit: Armed Forces and Public Safety Officer Dependent Scholarship: tuition, fees, books, housing (33-4302)
benefits.details: The spouse or child of an Idaho resident who entered active service as an Idaho resident (shown on the DD-214) qualifies if the service member 'has been determined by the federal government to be a prisoner of war or missing in action' or 'died of, or is determined to be unemployable due to, injuries or wounds sustained during active duty or inactive duty training.' Unemployable means the VA found individual unemployability or the SSA found total and permanent disability from service injuries; a 100% rating alone is not the statutory test. The student attends an Idaho public college or career technical college 'without the necessity of paying tuition and fees,' gets up to $750 per academic period for books and supplies, and on-campus housing and subsistence while living on campus, for up to 36 months. A child must be an Idaho resident who finished high school in Idaho; a spouse must have been married at the time of the event and still married if the veteran is living. Benefits can be used for 19 years after high school or 10 years after the event, whichever is longer. Apply through the State Board of Education and the school's financial aid office.
benefits.source_title: Idaho Legislature - Idaho Code 33-4302 Armed forces and public safety officer scholarships (am. 2025, ch. 94)

benefits.benefit: Operation Education scholarship at the University of Idaho for post-9/11 veterans with permanent disabilities
benefits.details: The University of Idaho's Operation Education program is 'available to military personnel who sustained permanent disability while serving our nation since Sept. 11, 2001,' and their spouses may also apply. It is a donor-funded scholarship, not a state entitlement, and the committee gives priority to Idaho residents and to combat-zone injuries. Depending on need it can cover tuition, books and fees, on-campus housing, transportation, adaptive equipment, medical assistance, child care, tutoring and career help. You must be honorably separated, admitted as a degree-seeking student, and generally enroll full time; you must also apply for VA benefits such as Veteran Readiness and Employment. Download the application from the program page and send your DD-214 and disability documentation; questions go to operationeducation@uidaho.edu or (208) 885-6229.
benefits.source_title: University of Idaho - Operation Education, Eligibility Requirements

benefits.benefit: Idaho income tax: military retirement deduction (disabled any age, 62+, or working); VA pay untaxed
benefits.details: Idaho taxes military retired pay but lets you deduct it under Idaho Code 63-3022A, as broadened in 2025 (House Bill 40, retroactive to January 1, 2025). A retired service member or unremarried surviving spouse qualifies if the retiree 'is classified as disabled,' 'has attained the age of sixty-two (62) years by the end of the tax year,' or 'was employed during the tax year and received sufficient income from such employment to be required to file a federal return.' The Tax Commission's 2025 instructions say 'classified as disabled' includes 'a veteran of a U.S. war with a service-connected disability rating of 10% or more.' The 2025 maximum is $48,216 (single) or $72,324 (married filing jointly), reduced by Social Security and Railroad Retirement benefits you and your spouse receive, and never more than the retired pay in your federal income. Claim it on Form 39R, Part B, line 8. VA disability compensation is excluded from federal adjusted gross income, which is where Idaho starts, so Idaho does not tax it. The Idaho income tax rate dropped to 5.3% for 2025.
benefits.source_title: Idaho Legislature - Idaho Code 63-3022A Deduction of certain retirement benefits (am. 2025, ch. 13 and ch. 302); Idaho State Tax Commission - 2025 Form 39R instructions (EIN00046, 03-02-2026)

benefits.benefit: Veterans preference in state and local government hiring: 5 or 10 points, guaranteed interview at 30%
benefits.details: Idaho public employers (state, counties, cities, school districts) must give preference at initial hire. 'Five (5) points shall be added to the earned rating of any veteran and the widow or widower of any veteran as long as he or she remains unmarried.' 'Ten (10) points shall be added to the earned rating of veterans discharged under honorable conditions who ... have a current service-connected disability of ten percent (10%) or more,' and the same 10 points go to Purple Heart recipients, the unremarried widow or widower of a disabled veteran, and the spouse of a disabled veteran who cannot work in public employment because of the disability. Veterans with 'a current service-connected disability of thirty percent (30%) or more shall be offered an interview if they are one (1) of the qualified applicants.' A veteran means 90 days of continuous active duty (or less if separated for a service-connected disability) with an honorable or general discharge. Points apply 'only for the purpose of initial appointment,' not promotions. Claim preference on the state application and be ready to show your DD-214 and VA rating letter.
benefits.source_title: Idaho Legislature - Idaho Code 65-504 Basic preference and addition of points to competitive examination ratings; 65-502 Definitions; 65-203 Veteran defined

benefits.benefit: Idaho State Veterans Homes in Boise, Lewiston, Pocatello and Post Falls
benefits.details: The Division of Veterans Services runs four skilled nursing homes (Boise also has residential and special care units). To be admitted you must be a veteran with at least 90 days of service and an honorable (other than dishonorable) discharge, 'a resident of the State of Idaho at the time of application,' and 'unemployable as a result of age, illness, or disability.' Wartime veterans get priority. Spouses and widows of veterans are eligible for nursing care only and must show proof of marriage. You must apply for (or already receive) VA pension with Aid and Attendance, and either apply for Medicaid or pay the current maximum monthly charge; veterans are admitted regardless of financial status. Apply with the Idaho State Veterans Home Application for Admission and your DD-214; call (208) 780-1300. The admission page was last updated in 2021, so confirm current rules with the home.
benefits.source_title: Idaho Division of Veterans Services - Idaho State Veterans Home Application for Admission (eligibility; page updated June 23, 2021)

benefits.benefit: Idaho State Veterans Cemeteries in Boise and Blackfoot (no Idaho residency required)
benefits.details: Idaho operates state veterans cemeteries in Boise (10100 N Horseshoe Bend Rd) and Blackfoot; the Snake River Canyon National Cemetery near Buhl is federal. Eligibility follows National Cemetery Administration rules and Idaho law: generally an honorably discharged veteran who served before September 7, 1980, or who later completed 24 months of active duty or a federally ordered deployment. 'There is no requirement to be a resident of the state of Idaho.' Interment fees for eligible veterans are paid by the VA; the family pays funeral costs. Guard and reserve members who do not meet federal rules, and spouses and dependents, pay a fee that the cemetery quotes case by case. Pre-registration is free and not binding: send discharge papers (and a marriage certificate for a spouse) to the cemetery. Burials are scheduled by the family or funeral home with a Request for Burial.
benefits.source_title: Idaho Division of Veterans Services - Cemeteries; Idaho State Veterans Cemetery Boise page

benefits.benefit: Emergency financial relief grant for Idaho veterans (Joining Forces Idaho)
benefits.details: The Division of Veterans Services offers one-time emergency help with bills such as an electric bill, rent or car repairs. The 2026 Joining Forces Idaho application says the 'Applicant must be a resident of Idaho,' must show veteran status (DD-214 member copy 4 showing character of discharge), and the need must be 'current and NOT ongoing.' The Division's state benefits page describes the older Emergency Relief program as 'up to a $1,500 grant, in cases of extreme emergency' for veterans who 'entered the military from Idaho, or lived within the state for at least 5 years,' with the event within 90 days of the request; the policy document behind that page could not be retrieved, so treat the $1,500 cap and the 5-year rule as unconfirmed. Send the signed application, bills or past-due notices, and proof of Idaho residency to JFIdaho@veterans.idaho.gov, or call (208) 780-1300.
benefits.source_title: Idaho Division of Veterans Services - Joining Forces Idaho Grant Application (Emergency Assistance and Financial Relief), posted Feb. 11, 2026; IDVS State Benefits and Services page

states.name: Illinois
notes: Illinois property tax relief for veterans is tiered by your VA rating, not all-or-nothing. The Standard Homestead Exemption for Veterans with Disabilities (SHEVD) takes $2,500 off the equalized assessed value (EAV) at 30% to 49%, $5,000 at 50% to 69%, and exempts the first $250,000 of EAV at 70% or more. Since tax year 2023 there is no longer a rule that your home's EAV must be under $250,000 to qualify; instead, EAV above $250,000 stays taxable. The law says 'service connected disability of 70% or more ... as certified by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs' and does not mention individual unemployability (TDIU). If your schedular rating is below 70% and you are paid at the 100% rate through TDIU, no official Illinois source says you qualify for the 70% tier. Ask your Chief County Assessment Office before you count on it.

You must reapply for SHEVD every year unless the VA certifies you have 'a combined service connected disability rating of 100%' and are 'permanently and totally disabled' (P&T). That no-reapply rule comes from Public Act 102-895 (May 23, 2022). By its words it needs a 100% combined rating plus P&T, so a 60% rating with TDIU P&T does not match the text. World War II veterans also do not reapply. Cook County says all other applicants, including the 70% to 99% tier, must reapply each year.

Illinois property tax deadlines are set county by county. The statute says to apply 'during the application period in effect for the county of his or her residence,' and you file with the Chief County Assessment Office (in Cook County, the Cook County Assessor). Cook County processes late applications as Certificates of Error, which can reach back several tax years. Illinois taxes are paid a year behind, so the 2025 exemption shows on bills paid in 2026. The home must be your primary residence, and any part used for business is excluded. A home rented out for more than 6 months is presumed commercial. You must be an Illinois resident with a service-connected disability certified by the VA and receiving VA disability compensation. If you move in after January 1, the exemption is prorated by month. If you move into a nursing home or VA facility, the exemption continues while your spouse lives there or the home sits empty but you still own it.

A surviving spouse keeps the SHEVD as long as he or she holds title, lives in the home, and does not remarry. If the spouse sells, an amount up to the last exemption granted can move to a new primary residence. Since tax year 2023, a spouse can also qualify if the veteran never applied but would have qualified (the spouse must have lived in Illinois since the veteran's death), or if the spouse receives VA Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) for a service-connected death; DIC spouses get the first $250,000 of EAV exempt. Spouses of veterans killed in the line of duty get a full exemption on the home.

You cannot stack the veteran exemptions. A taxpayer who takes the Specially Adapted Housing exemption (15-165) or the general Homestead Exemption for Persons with Disabilities (15-168, $2,000 EAV) cannot also take SHEVD in the same year. The Returning Veterans' Homestead Exemption ($5,000 for the year you return from an armed conflict and the next year) is in addition to the others. Cook County says it cannot be combined with SHEVD; the statute says it is 'in addition to any other homestead exemption,' so ask your county.

The free veterans-with-disabilities license plate has two doors. Any veteran with a VA service-connected disability whose doctor certifies it meets the disability-plate standard gets the plate with the wheelchair symbol free of the registration fee. A veteran rated 50% or more who does not meet that medical standard gets a plate without the symbol, also free. Right now the fee waiver covers one vehicle; Public Act 104-603 raises that to 2 sets of plates on July 1, 2027. Renewals need fresh proof unless your disability is permanent. The Illinois Secretary of State website could not be reached during this research, so fee details come from the statute and IDVA.

Illinois has no state income tax on military retired pay, military disability retired pay, Survivor Benefit Plan payments from a government plan, or active duty and Guard pay. All are subtracted on Form IL-1040 (Line 5 retirement income, or Schedule M for military pay). VA disability compensation and DIC are not in federal adjusted gross income, which is where the Illinois return starts, so they are not taxed either. No 2025 or 2026 change to these rules was found.

Illinois does not require a fishing license for veterans 'at least 10% disabled with service-related disabilities or in receipt of total disability pensions.' IDVA says the same 10% rule covers hunting licenses and issues the Disability Affidavit for Illinois Hunting and Fishing Privilege card through its Veteran Service Officers; the hunting side was not found in the Wildlife Code text, so confirm with IDVA or IDNR. Free camping at Illinois state parks is a narrower benefit: permanent loss of use of a leg or arm, wheelchair or crutch dependence, 100% service-connected compensation, or former POW status, with a $10 utility fee still due at electric sites.

The MIA/POW Scholarship for dependents is the one Illinois benefit that clearly counts TDIU: IDVA accepts a veteran rated '100% permanent and totally disabled from service-connected causes due to unemployability.' The Illinois Veteran Grant (IVG) is for the veteran and needs Illinois residency when you entered service (or within 6 months) and a return to Illinois within 6 months of discharge, or 15 consecutive years of Illinois residency after service. The ISAC website blocked automated access, so IVG details come from the statute and IDVA.

State hiring preference is points, not absolute preference: 10 points for a VA service-connected disability or a Purple Heart, 5 points for qualifying wartime service, 3 points for other honorable service. Claim it by checking the box on the careers.illinois.gov application and providing a certified DD-214 to the CMS Veterans Outreach Program. Spouses of veterans with a service-connected disability and some surviving spouses and parents can also get points.

Things that are NOT available or were not found: no vehicle sales tax exemption for disabled veterans, no free Illinois ID card or driver's license just for being a veteran (free ID cards go only to residents of veterans homes or hospitals and people 65 and older; the 'veteran' designation is free at renewal, $5 for an early license update), no state veterans cemetery was named on the IDVA burial page, and Veterans Cash lottery grants go to nonprofits and government agencies, not to individual veterans. The War Participation Bonus is a one-time $100 (more for WWII) for Illinois residents with qualifying campaign medals, not a disability benefit.

2025 and 2026 law changes checked: Public Act 104-234 (Aug. 15, 2025) only renamed the agency to 'Department of Veterans Affairs' in many statutes. Public Act 104-238 (Jan. 1, 2026) lets IDVA set MIA/POW Scholarship eligibility by rule. Public Act 104-603 (July 1, 2027) doubles the free plates for veterans with disabilities, Purple Heart, Medal of Honor and POW plates to 2 sets. Bills to change SHEVD (HB 2809 percentage tiers, SB 99 surviving spouse $250,000, HB 3136 caregivers, HB 4405 nonresident killed in line of duty) had not become law as of this research; HB 4405 was re-referred to Rules.

benefits.benefit: Standard Homestead Exemption for Veterans with Disabilities (SHEVD): $2,500 to first $250,000 EAV exempt
benefits.details: If you are an Illinois resident veteran with a VA-certified service-connected disability and receive VA disability compensation, your primary home gets a reduction in equalized assessed value (EAV): $2,500 at 30% to 49%, $5,000 at 50% to 69%, and the first $250,000 of EAV exempt at 70% or more (EAV above $250,000 is still taxed). World War II veterans get a full exemption at any rating. The law counts your rating 'as of the date the application is submitted' and does not mention TDIU, so a TDIU veteran rated under 70% should ask the county. Apply with your Chief County Assessment Office during your county's application period, with your VA rating letter and DD-214 (Cook County requires a certified DD-214 for first-time filers). You must reapply every year unless the VA certifies a 100% combined rating that is permanent and total; then it renews on its own.
benefits.source_title: Illinois General Assembly - 35 ILCS 200/15-169 Homestead exemption for veterans with disabilities and veterans of World War II (P.A. 103-596); IDOR PIO-74 (R-07/25)

benefits.benefit: SHEVD for surviving spouses, including DIC recipients and spouses of veterans killed in the line of duty
benefits.details: If your veteran spouse dies, the exemption carries over as long as you hold title, live in the home, and do not remarry. If you sell, you can move an amount up to the last exemption granted to a new primary residence. Since tax year 2023 you can also qualify if the veteran never applied but would have qualified (you must have lived in Illinois since the death), or if the VA certifies you receive Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) for a service-connected death; DIC spouses get the first $250,000 of EAV exempt. Spouses of veterans killed in the line of duty get a full exemption. File with your Chief County Assessment Office with the death certificate and proof of ownership; IDOR says Form PTAX-342 is used to transfer the exemption.
benefits.source_title: Illinois General Assembly - 35 ILCS 200/15-169(c) surviving spouse provisions; Cook County Assessor - Veterans with Disabilities Exemption

benefits.benefit: Specially Adapted Housing property tax exemption: up to $100,000 of assessed value
benefits.details: If the federal government approved you for a VA Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) grant under 38 U.S.C. 2101, up to $100,000 of your home's assessed value is exempt. The home must be owned and used only as your home (or your spouse's or unmarried surviving spouse's). It covers homes bought or adapted with federal SAH funds, later homes bought with the proceeds of a prior SAH home, and since 2015 homes adapted or donated by a charity when you have SAH approval and a licensed inspector certifies VA design standards. Mobile homes qualify under a parallel law. IDVA must certify the exemption each year to the Department of Revenue, so start with your IDVA Veteran Service Officer. You cannot take SHEVD or the persons-with-disabilities exemption in the same year.
benefits.source_title: Illinois General Assembly - 35 ILCS 200/15-165 Veterans with disabilities (specially adapted housing) (P.A. 104-234)

benefits.benefit: Returning Veterans' Homestead Exemption: $5,000 EAV reduction for two years after an armed conflict deployment
benefits.details: An Illinois resident who served in the U.S. Armed Forces, Illinois National Guard, or Reserves and returns from active duty in an armed conflict gets a $5,000 reduction in EAV on the principal residence for the year of return and the following year. You must own (or hold a legal or equitable interest in) and live in the home and be liable for the taxes. If you buy the home after January 1 of the return year, you can use the exemption the next year only. You can get it again after another qualifying deployment. File Form PTAX-341 with your Chief County Assessment Office during the county application period with your DD-214 or military orders; it is not renewed automatically. The statute says it is in addition to other homestead exemptions.
benefits.source_title: Illinois General Assembly - 35 ILCS 200/15-167 Returning Veterans' Homestead Exemption; IDOR PIO-74

benefits.benefit: Free license plates for veterans with disabilities (with or without the wheelchair symbol)
benefits.details: You pay no registration fee for veterans-with-disabilities plates on one car, motorcycle, or truck up to 8,000 pounds if you hold VA proof of a service-connected disability and a physician, physician assistant, or advanced practice nurse certifies that the disability meets the standard for disability plates (Section 3-616); these plates carry the international symbol of access. If your VA rating is 50% or more but you do not meet that medical standard, you get a plate without the symbol, also free. Renewals need new proof of eligibility unless your disability is permanent; IDVA can help with documentation. Public Act 104-603 raises the free allowance to up to 2 sets of plates on July 1, 2027. Apply at a Secretary of State facility.
benefits.source_title: Illinois General Assembly - 625 ILCS 5/3-609 Plates for veterans with disabilities (P.A. 104-603; P.A. 104-682)

benefits.benefit: Purple Heart plates free of registration fees; free 'veteran' designation on driver's license at renewal
benefits.details: An Illinois resident awarded the Purple Heart (or the surviving spouse of one) can display Purple Heart plates on one vehicle 'without the payment of any registration or registration renewal fee'; this rises to 2 vehicles on July 1, 2027 under Public Act 104-603. Separately, any honorably discharged veteran can have the word 'veteran' printed on an Illinois driver's license or state ID by showing a DD-214 or other proof at any Secretary of State facility; it is free when added at renewal, or $5 for an early license update and $10 for an early ID update (free for veterans 65 and older). Illinois does not waive the regular license or ID fee for veterans; free ID cards go only to people 65 and older and residents of veterans homes or hospitals.
benefits.source_title: Illinois General Assembly - 625 ILCS 5/3-623 Purple Heart Plates; 625 ILCS 5/6-110(e-5); IDVA - Veteran Driver's License page

benefits.benefit: No fishing license needed and free hunting license for veterans 10%+ service-connected or on VA pension
benefits.details: Under the Fish Code, veterans the VA certifies as 'at least 10% disabled with service-related disabilities or in receipt of total disability pensions' may fish with sport fishing devices without a license, as long as the disability does not make fishing unsafe. IDVA says the same 10% rule gives free hunting licenses and that this applies regardless of your state of residence. You need a DD-214 and a Disability Affidavit for Illinois Hunting and Fishing Privilege card, which IDVA issues through its Veteran Service Officers using VA proof of compensation dated within the last year; carry it while hunting or fishing. The hunting exemption was not found in the Wildlife Code text, and IDVA does not say whether stamps and permits (habitat, waterfowl, deer) are also free, so confirm with IDVA or IDNR.
benefits.source_title: Illinois General Assembly - 515 ILCS 5/20-5(d) Fish and Aquatic Life Code, necessity of license; exemptions; IDVA - Fishing and Hunting Permits page

benefits.benefit: Free camping and shelter reservations at Illinois state parks for severely disabled veterans and former POWs
benefits.details: An Illinois resident veteran who has permanent loss of use of a leg or arm (or both), cannot move without crutches or a wheelchair, or 'is receiving 100% service connected disability compensation benefits' from the VA or military disability retired pay (not Temporary Disability Retired List), and any former prisoner of war, camps free at IDNR state parks any day of the week. At Class AA, A, A-P, B/E and B/E-P sites you still pay the $10 utility fee; at Class B/S, B/S-P, C and D sites there is no fee. Shelter reservation fees are also waived, and your spouse, minor children and grandchildren under 18 are covered when camping with you. Get the Department of Veterans Affairs Disability Certification Card at any IDVA field office with federal proof, and show it to park staff when you get your camping permit. Whether TDIU counts as '100% compensation' is not stated.
benefits.source_title: Illinois Department of Natural Resources - Camping Fee Discounts (Senior Citizens, Persons with Disabilities, Veterans and Former POWs)

benefits.benefit: Illinois Veteran Grant (IVG): 4 years of tuition and mandatory fees at Illinois public colleges
benefits.details: The IVG pays all tuition and mandatory fees for the equivalent of 4 years of full-time study (120 eligibility units) at any Illinois state university or public community college. You qualify if you were an Illinois resident when you entered federal active duty (or within 6 months, or were enrolled at an Illinois public college), served at least 1 year of federal active duty (less if discharged for a service-connected medical reason or served in a hostile area), were honorably discharged, and returned to Illinois within 6 months of leaving service. If you do not meet the entry-residency test, you can still qualify after 15 consecutive years of Illinois residency after service. Current service members with 1 year of honorable service also qualify. The grant never expires while federal GI Bill benefits exist. Apply through the Illinois Student Assistance Commission (ISAC) with your DD-214. The separate Illinois National Guard Grant gives active Guard members with 1 year of service up to 4 years (6 after 10 years of service) of tuition and fees at the same schools.
benefits.source_title: Illinois General Assembly - 110 ILCS 947/40 Illinois Veteran grant program; 110 ILCS 947/45 Illinois National Guard and Naval Militia grant program

benefits.benefit: MIA/POW Scholarship and $250 Educational Opportunity Grant for dependents of 100% P&T or deceased veterans
benefits.details: A spouse or child (natural, adopted or step-child under 18 at adoption or marriage, or a court-ordered ward for 2 years) of a veteran who is MIA or a POW, died of a service-connected cause, or 'has become a person with a permanent disability from service-connected causes with 100% disability' pays no tuition or mandatory fees for the equivalent of 4 years at any Illinois state university or public community college. IDVA states a veteran rated 100% permanent and total 'due to unemployability' qualifies. The veteran must have been an Illinois resident at entry into service, within 6 months after, or for 15 consecutive years after entering service. A spouse loses the benefit at the end of the term if he or she remarries or divorces. Benefits expire 12 years after first use. Apply through the ISAC student portal with the DD-214 or casualty report and VA award letter; IDVA decides eligibility by rule (Public Act 104-238, effective January 1, 2026). Children aged 10 to 18 of the same veterans can also get a $250 Educational Opportunity Grant each school year through IDVA.
benefits.source_title: Illinois Department of Veterans Affairs - MIA/POW Scholarship (105 ILCS 5/30-14.2; 95 Ill. Adm. Code 116)

benefits.benefit: No Illinois income tax on military retired pay, military disability retirement, SBP, or active duty pay
benefits.details: Illinois lets you subtract all federally taxed retirement income from 'a government retirement and government disability plan, including military plans' on Form IL-1040, Line 5, so military retired pay and military disability retired pay are not taxed. Survivor Benefit Plan payments from a government plan fall under the same subtraction. Active duty, Reserve and National Guard pay is subtracted on Schedule M; IDOR says 'Illinois does not tax military pay earned by service persons.' VA disability compensation and DIC are not in federal adjusted gross income, which is the starting point for the Illinois return, so they are not taxed. Attach your 1099-R or W-2 when you claim the subtraction. Illinois Publication 120 (R-12/25) and Publication 102 (R-12/25) are current.
benefits.source_title: Illinois Department of Revenue - Publication 120, Retirement Income (R-12/25); Publication 102, Illinois Filing Requirements for Military Personnel (R-12/25); 35 ILCS 5/203(a)(2)(E) and (F)

benefits.benefit: State hiring preference points: 10 for service-connected disability or Purple Heart, 5 wartime, 3 other
benefits.details: Under the Personnel Code, points are added to your passing score for State of Illinois jobs: 10 points if you hold VA proof of a service-connected disability or received the Purple Heart; 5 points for wartime service of at least 6 months, for the duration of hostilities, or ending in a hardship or service-connected discharge; and 3 points for other honorable service of 6 months or more, or 4 years in the Guard or Reserves. The augmented score sets your rank order. A spouse of a veteran whose service-connected disability keeps the veteran from civil service work, an unremarried surviving spouse of a veteran who died of a service-connected cause, and one parent of such an unmarried veteran can claim the same points. Check the veteran box on your careers.illinois.gov application and send a certified DD-214 or NGB-22 to the CMS Veterans Outreach Program (800-643-8138). This is a points preference, not an absolute hiring preference.
benefits.source_title: Illinois General Assembly - 20 ILCS 415/8b.7 Personnel Code, Veteran preference (P.A. 103-746); CMS Veterans Outreach Program

benefits.benefit: Illinois Veterans Homes in Anna, LaSalle, Manteno, Quincy and Chicago
benefits.details: IDVA runs five homes offering nursing and domiciliary care. You must be an honorably discharged veteran with qualifying service (wartime or campaign medal service, retirement for a service-connected disability, 24 months of continuous active duty after September 7, 1980, or certain Guard and Reserve service; peacetime veterans with 1 year of service may also qualify), be 'disabled by disease, wounds, or otherwise' and unable to earn a living, and have entered service from Illinois or lived in Illinois for the year before applying. Widows and widowers can be admitted at Anna and Quincy when beds are open, and eligible Gold Star family members may also apply. The cost of care is $1,720 per month (as of June 2025), charged as a maintenance fee based on your and your spouse's income; the inability to pay does not bar admission. Apply through the Adjutant's office at the home you choose.
benefits.source_title: Illinois Department of Veterans Affairs - Veterans' Homes (20 ILCS 2805/2.01)

benefits.benefit: Illinois War Participation Bonus ($100), POW compensation, and $125 headstone-setting reimbursement
benefits.details: Illinois pays a one-time $100 bonus to honorably discharged veterans who lived in Illinois for 12 months before entering service and earned the Korean Service Medal, Vietnam Service or Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal (Vietnam), Southwest Asia Service Medal, or a Global War on Terrorism Expeditionary or Service Medal, Iraq Campaign Medal or Afghanistan Campaign Medal with 30 consecutive or 60 nonconsecutive days of foreign or sea service. World War II veterans get $10 per month of domestic service and $15 per month of foreign service. Survivors of veterans whose deaths were service-connected from hostile action (WWII) or Agent Orange (Vietnam) get $1,000. Former POWs held in Southeast Asia on or after January 1, 1961 get $50 per month of captivity. Apply through IDVA's online form or a Veteran Service Officer. Separately, IDVA pays up to $125 toward setting a government headstone, and county Veterans Assistance Commissions bury indigent veterans and spouses. No state veterans cemetery is listed by IDVA.
benefits.source_title: Illinois Department of Veterans Affairs - War Participation Bonus and Compensation Benefits; IDVA - Survivor and Burial Benefits

states.name: Indiana
notes: Indiana rewrote its veteran property tax benefits in 2026. House Enrolled Act 1210 (2026) replaced the old $14,000 deduction with a deduction of 100 percent of the assessed value of a totally disabled veteran's principal residence, with no assessed value cap (the old $240,000 cap is gone). The old $24,960 wartime deduction became a $350 credit, and the old age 62 deduction became a $250 credit. The changes start with the 2026 assessment date (taxes paid in 2027).

The 100 percent deduction requires a 'total disability' shown by a VA pension certificate, a VA award of compensation, or an IDVA certificate of eligibility. The law does not say 'permanent,' and the Department of Local Government Finance (DLGF) says the total disability does not have to be service connected. Total disability based on individual unemployability (TDIU) is not named anywhere. Ask your county auditor or IDVA before you count on it if your 100 percent pay comes from TDIU.

If you got the old $14,000 deduction, the county auditor will automatically switch you to the $250 credit for taxes paid in 2027. You will NOT get the new 100 percent deduction unless you file a new State Form 12662 with your county auditor by January 15, 2027. Late applications cannot be made retroactive.

You cannot have both the 100 percent deduction and any credit under IC 6-1.1-51.3 (the $350, $250, Over 65, or Blind/Disabled credits). The $350 and $250 credits can be stacked with each other. Nothing renews each year; once approved, the benefit continues while you stay eligible.

Residency: the 100 percent deduction requires at least one year living in Indiana before the assessment date (January 1) and the home must be your principal place of residence. The $350 and $250 credits have no Indiana residency rule; you just need to own (or buy under a recorded contract) the Indiana property. Property held in a trust or LLC cannot get the 100 percent deduction, but a trust can get the credits.

Surviving spouses: a surviving spouse keeps the 100 percent deduction if the veteran qualified at death and the spouse owns the home, but loses it on remarriage. The $350 and $250 credits also pass to a surviving spouse who owns the property; the $250 credit also goes to the spouse of a member killed in action or who died on active duty or inactive duty training.

If you qualify for a veteran property tax benefit but own no taxable property, you can get a vehicle excise tax credit of up to $70 per vehicle on up to two vehicles. You need an affidavit from the county auditor and State Form 52870 at the BMV. The BMV form still cites the pre-2026 statute numbers, so confirm with your auditor.

The Disabled Hoosier Veteran (DHV) license plate and placard are based on the type of disability, not just the rating: loss or loss of use of a hand or foot, blindness, a VA rated condition that keeps you from walking without pain or difficulty, or a 50 percent or higher rating with at least 60 percent of it from a mobility disability. IDVA, not the BMV, approves the application (State Form 32584). The plate or placard lets the veteran park free at Indiana meters, but only when the veteran is in the vehicle. DHV eligibility also unlocks the $25 state park pass.

The $2.75 disabled veteran hunting and fishing license covers fishing and small game only. It does not cover deer, turkey, or any stamps (gamebird, waterfowl, trout and salmon). You must get DNR approval once before you can buy it. Indiana also waives DNR property entry fees for all veterans and active duty members on Veterans Day (November 11); the last official listing we found was for 2024.

For children of disabled veterans, the percentage of tuition covered depends on when the veteran enlisted. Before July 1, 2011: 100 percent. On or after July 1, 2011: 20 percent plus the veteran's VA rating (so a 40 percent rating means 60 percent of tuition). The child must apply before age 33, and the exemption lasts 124 credit hours or eight academic years. Wartime service (or a campaign medal) by the parent is required.

Indiana does not tax military retired pay or military survivor benefits (100 percent deductible since tax year 2022). VA disability compensation is excluded from federal adjusted gross income, which is where the Indiana return starts, so it is not taxed. Active duty pay gets a $5,000 Military Service Deduction; National Guard and reserve pay is fully deductible.

State hiring preference: IDVA's page says only that the State Merit System adds points for veterans applying for state merit jobs or promotions (citing IC 4-15-2-18). We could not find the current statute text or point values on an official page, so treat this as unverified. Indiana also has a no fee peddler, vendor, or hawker license for honorably discharged veterans where a local ordinance requires one.

benefits.benefit: 100% property tax deduction on principal residence for totally disabled veterans (new 2026 law)
benefits.details: Starting with the 2026 assessment date (taxes paid in 2027), a veteran with a 'total disability' can deduct 100 percent of the assessed value of the home used as the principal place of residence, with no assessed value cap. You must have served at least 90 days (wartime not required), been honorably discharged, lived in Indiana at least one year before January 1 of the assessment year, and prove the total disability with a VA pension certificate, VA award of compensation, or IDVA certificate of eligibility. DLGF says the disability does not have to be service connected; the law does not say 'permanent' and does not mention TDIU. A surviving spouse keeps it if the veteran qualified at death and the spouse owns the home and has not remarried. File State Form 12662 with your county auditor by January 15 of the year the tax is first due; if you had the old $14,000 deduction you must file again to get this one. You cannot also take any IC 6-1.1-51.3 credit.
benefits.source_title: Indiana DLGF - Frequently Asked Questions, 2026 Legislative Update: Veterans Deductions and Credits (IC 6-1.1-12-14, as amended by HEA 1210-2026; FAQ dated June 17, 2026, posted Aug. 12, 2026)

benefits.benefit: $350 property tax credit for wartime veterans with 10%+ service-connected disability
benefits.details: A credit of up to $350 against your local property tax bill if you served during a U.S. war, were honorably discharged, and have a service-connected disability of at least 10 percent. Proof is a VA award of compensation, VA pension certificate, VA disability compensation check, or IDVA certificate. There is no Indiana residency rule and no wartime period test beyond serving during a war; you must own the Indiana property or be buying it under a recorded contract. The credit can be split across more than one property but the total stays $350, and any unused amount is lost. A surviving spouse qualifies if the veteran met the tests at death. This replaces the old $24,960 deduction starting with 2026 pay 2027; DLGF recommends counties move old recipients over automatically, but the law requires an application, so file State Form 12662 with your county auditor by January 15 if you are not sure.
benefits.source_title: Indiana DLGF - FAQ 2026 Legislative Update: Veterans Deductions and Credits (IC 6-1.1-51.3-6; State Form 12662 R20 6-26)

benefits.benefit: $250 property tax credit for veterans age 62+ with 10%+ disability
benefits.details: A credit of up to $250 against local property tax if you served at least 90 days, were honorably discharged, are at least 62 years old, and have a disability of at least 10 percent (VA or IDVA proof). Wartime service is not required. You can stack it with the $350 credit and with the Over 65 or Blind/Disabled credits, but not with the 100 percent deduction. A surviving spouse qualifies if the veteran met the tests at death, or if the member was killed in action, died on active duty, or died during inactive duty training. For taxes paid in 2027, counties automatically convert anyone who had the old $14,000 deduction to this credit. Otherwise file State Form 12662 with the county auditor by January 15.
benefits.source_title: Indiana DLGF - State Form 12662 (R20 / 6-26), Application for Property Tax Benefits for Disabled Veterans and Surviving Spouses (IC 6-1.1-51.3-5)

benefits.benefit: Property tax deduction for a homestead donated to a disabled veteran (50% to 100% of value)
benefits.details: If a tax-exempt organization (for example a 501(c)(3) homebuilder) gave you your home at no charge, and you served at least 90 days, were honorably discharged, and have a disability of at least 50 percent, you may deduct a share of the home's assessed value equal to your rating tier: 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, or 100 percent. You must own the home (no contract purchase). You cannot take this and the 100 percent deduction for the same year, and no unused part can be used against vehicle excise tax. File State Form 12662, Section V, with your county auditor by January 15.
benefits.source_title: Indiana Department of Veterans Affairs - Disabled Veteran Property Tax Deductions and Credits (IC 6-1.1-12-14.5; State Form 12662)

benefits.benefit: Disabled Hoosier Veteran (DHV) license plate and placard with free metered parking
benefits.details: You can get a DHV plate for each vehicle you own, and a placard, if your service-connected condition is one of these: loss of sight or permanent vision impairment in both eyes; loss or permanent loss of use of one or both feet or hands; a VA rating for a physical condition that keeps you from walking without pain or difficulty; or a VA rating of at least 50 percent where at least 60 percent of the rating is for a mobility disability. Apply through IDVA (State Form 32584 with a VA certificate and your VA claim number; most approvals take about two days), then take the stamped form to a BMV branch. The plate and placard let you park in accessible spaces and at any Indiana meter for free, but the privilege belongs to the veteran, not the car. You pay normal registration fees and excise tax. Purple Heart recipients can get a modified Purple Heart plate with the accessibility symbol.
benefits.source_title: Indiana Department of Veterans Affairs - Veteran License Plates (IC 9-18.5-5-1; IC 9-18.5-6); IDVA DHV approval letter; BMV Drivers with Disabilities page

benefits.benefit: Vehicle excise tax credit (up to $70 per vehicle, two vehicles) for disabled veterans who own no property
benefits.details: If you qualify for a veteran property tax deduction or credit but do not own property the deduction can be applied to, Indiana gives you a credit against the annual vehicle excise tax equal to the lesser of the excise tax due or $70 per vehicle, for up to two vehicles per registration year. Get an affidavit from your county auditor stating you own no qualifying property, then file State Form 52870 at the BMV with the affidavit. Under the old law, any unused part of a property tax deduction could also be applied to excise tax; DLGF says the new 100 percent deduction usually leaves nothing unused. The BMV form (revised 12-24) still names the pre-2026 statutes, so confirm current eligibility with your auditor.
benefits.source_title: Indiana BMV - State Form 52870 (R3 / 12-24), Qualified Veteran Excise Tax Credit (IC 6-6-5-5.2); DLGF Veterans FAQ 2026

benefits.benefit: Hoosier Veteran plate ($15) and Purple Heart plate
benefits.details: Any Indiana resident honorably separated from the active armed forces can buy a Hoosier Veteran plate for $15 (plus $45 if personalized) by bringing a DD-214 or discharge certificate to a BMV branch; no application form is needed.
