Purple Heart recipients, or an unremarried surviving spouse, can get a Purple Heart plate by applying through IDVA with proof of the award. These plates do not waive registration fees or excise tax. Indiana has no veteran discount on driver's license fees that we could find.
benefits.source_title: Indiana Department of Veterans Affairs - Veteran License Plates (IC 9-18.5-6)

benefits.benefit: Reduced fee disabled veteran hunting and fishing license ($2.75 per year or $27.50 for 10 years)
benefits.details: Indiana residents who served in the armed forces and have a VA service-connected disability (or military disability retirement) can buy a license to fish and hunt small game for $2.75 a year, or $27.50 for a 10-year license. It does not cover deer or turkey, and gamebird, waterfowl, and trout and salmon stamps cost regular price. First send DNR the application (State Form 50833) with proof of your disability by email (INHuntFish@dnr.IN.gov), fax, or mail; after DNR approves you once, buy the license at GoOutdoorsIN.com, at a DNR property, or from a license vendor. IDVA's page says DNR will not process a faxed copy, while DNR's page lists a fax number, so use email or mail to be safe.
benefits.source_title: Indiana Department of Natural Resources - Disabled Veterans license (IC 14-22-12-1.5)

benefits.benefit: $25 Disabled Hoosier Veteran annual state park pass; free DNR entry on Veterans Day
benefits.details: Veterans eligible for the Disabled Hoosier Veteran license plate (see the plate row for the mobility-based tests) can buy an annual entrance pass for $25 instead of the $50 resident price. It covers unlimited entry to state parks, recreation areas, reservoirs, and state forests for the calendar year, but not historic sites or museums. Buy it at any DNR property with your DHV registration or approved State Form 32584, or online. Former POWs and their surviving spouses get a free Golden Hoosier Passport mailed each year. Indiana resident Gold Star family members get a free annual pass. All veterans and active duty members, with everyone in their vehicle, are admitted free to DNR properties on Veterans Day; just tell the gate attendant.
benefits.source_title: Indiana Department of Natural Resources - Entrance Fees (Disabled Hoosier Veteran pass, IC 9-18.5-5); events.in.gov Veterans Day free admission listing

benefits.benefit: Tuition and fee exemption for children of disabled veterans (up to 124 credit hours)
benefits.details: The biological or adopted child of a veteran who served during a war (or in duty that earned a service or campaign medal), has a VA service-connected disability or died from service, and was discharged other than dishonorably gets tuition and regularly assessed fees waived at Indiana public colleges for up to 124 credit hours or eight academic years. If the veteran enlisted before July 1, 2011, 100 percent is covered; if on or after that date, 20 percent plus the veteran's VA disability percentage. The veteran must have listed Indiana as home of record at enlistment or lived in Indiana five years before the child first applies, and the child must qualify for in-state tuition and apply before turning 33. Students who graduated high school on or after January 1, 2023 may use up to $5,000 a year at Indiana private nonprofit colleges. Apply once at ScholarTrack.IN.gov and file the FAFSA every year; IDVA reviews the application.
benefits.source_title: Indiana Commission for Higher Education - Tuition and Fee Exemption for Children of Disabled Veterans (IC 21-14-4)

benefits.benefit: Purple Heart recipient tuition and fee exemption; National Guard Tuition Supplement Grant
benefits.details: A veteran who received the Purple Heart or was wounded by enemy action, entered active duty from a permanent Indiana home address, and was discharged other than dishonorably gets up to 100 percent of tuition and regularly assessed fees waived at Indiana public colleges for up to 124 credit hours (eight academic years) at the undergraduate resident rate. Apply once at ScholarTrack.IN.gov and file the FAFSA each year. Separately, Indiana National Guard members in active drilling status seeking a first degree can get the National Guard Tuition Supplement Grant covering tuition and fees at public colleges (up to $5,000 a year at private nonprofits), certified by the unit each semester.
benefits.source_title: Indiana Commission for Higher Education - Tuition and Fee Exemption for Indiana Purple Heart Recipients; National Guard Tuition Supplement Grant page

benefits.benefit: Military retired pay and survivor benefits 100% deductible; $5,000 active duty pay deduction
benefits.details: Indiana lets you deduct all military retirement pay and military survivor's benefits (phased in from 2019 and 100 percent since tax year 2022), with no age requirement, on IT-40 Schedule 2. The surviving spouse gets the same deduction; a divorced spouse receiving a share under a divorce decree does not. You did not have to live in Indiana while serving. Active duty members can deduct up to $5,000 of military pay, and National Guard and reserve pay is fully deductible. VA disability compensation is not in federal adjusted gross income, which is where the Indiana return starts, so Indiana does not tax it. Enclose your 1099-R or W-2 with the return.
benefits.source_title: Indiana Department of Revenue - Income Tax Information Bulletin #27, Indiana Adjusted Gross Income Tax Applicable to Military Personnel (June 2025; IC 6-3-2-4); Bulletin #6 (June 2025)

benefits.benefit: Veterans preference points for state merit jobs; no fee peddler or vendor license
benefits.details: IDVA states that the State Merit System adds points to the scores of veterans applying for merit positions or promotions in Indiana state government (IDVA cites IC 4-15-2-18). We could not find the current statute text, point values, or any extra points for disabled veterans or spouses on an official page, so ask the State Personnel Department when you apply through WorkForIndiana. Department of Workforce Development offices have Disabled Veterans' Outreach Program specialists who focus on job placement for veterans with service-connected disabilities. Separately, any veteran with an honorable discharge can get a license to vend, hawk, or peddle in any Indiana county, city, or town without paying the license fee where a local ordinance requires one (IC 25-25-2-1); apply through the county auditor or local licensing authority with your DD-214.
benefits.source_title: Indiana Department of Veterans Affairs - Employment Assistance (cites IC 4-15-2-18); IDVA No Fee Vendor, Hawker, or Peddler License fact sheet (IC 25-25-2-1)

benefits.benefit: Military Family Relief Fund emergency grants
benefits.details: IDVA's Military Family Relief Fund gives hardship grants to Indiana resident veterans and their families for rent or mortgage, utilities, food, medical and dental bills, basic transportation, education, child care, and funeral costs. You must be an Indiana resident, the veteran must have an eligible discharge code, household income cannot exceed two times the federal poverty guidelines, and you must show genuine financial hardship in your income, spending, and statement letter. The fund will not reimburse bills already paid or pay bills more than 10 days in advance. Apply online, by email (MFRF@dva.in.gov), fax, mail, or in person at IDVA; incomplete applications close after 30 days. Grant maximums are set in 915 IAC 3 and were not shown on the web pages.
benefits.source_title: Indiana Department of Veterans Affairs - Military Family Relief Fund Eligibility Criteria (IC 10-17-12; 915 IAC 3)

benefits.benefit: Indiana Veterans' Home (West Lafayette) and Indiana Veterans Memorial Cemetery (Madison)
benefits.details: The Indiana Veterans' Home in West Lafayette offers long-term skilled nursing, short-term rehabilitation, and memory care to honorably discharged veterans of any service period, their spouses and surviving spouses, and Gold Star parents. You need one year of Indiana residency right before applying (waivers for those who enlisted in or were discharged to Indiana) and must pass a background check. Apply by sending the application packet to Admissions (765-497-8072). The Indiana Veterans Memorial Cemetery in Madison buries veterans separated under conditions other than dishonorable, their spouses, and dependent children; for eligible veterans and spouses there is no cost for the plot opening and closing, outer burial container, monument, or chapel. No Indiana residency rule is stated for the cemetery.
benefits.source_title: Indiana Veterans' Home - Who is Eligible for IVH; IDVA - Indiana Veterans Memorial Cemetery

states.name: Iowa
notes: Iowa's full property tax credit needs a 'permanent' 100% service-connected rating, or a permanent and total (P&T) rating based on individual unemployability (TDIU) paid at the 100% rate. The law names TDIU directly, so TDIU counts if the VA rates you permanently and totally disabled. A 100% rating that the VA has not marked permanent does not match the law's words.

2026 change: Senate File 2472 repealed Iowa Code 425.15 and moved the same credit to Iowa Code 425.1(2)(b), retroactive to the 2026 assessment year. If you first apply on or after July 1, 2026, the credit covers only one-half acre and no outbuildings. People who applied before that date keep the old homestead definition and do not need to refile.

File property tax claims with your city or county assessor by July 1. A claim filed after July 1 counts for the next year. Bring your DD-214 and a current VA Benefit Summary letter. You do not refile each year. You cannot take both the full disabled veteran credit and the $4,000 military exemption; pick one.

Surviving spouse: the full credit continues to the estate or the surviving spouse 'so long as the surviving spouse remains unmarried' and they stay in the home. A surviving spouse or child who receives Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) qualifies on their own, and the Department of Revenue says a DIC spouse stays eligible even after remarriage. The credit ends if DIC ends.

Residency: most Iowa veteran benefits use the Iowa Code 35.1 definition of 'veteran,' which requires you to be an Iowa resident with an honorable discharge. The homestead must be the home you own and occupy on July 1 and live in at least six months of the year. The military exemption requires you to be 'a resident of and domiciled in the state of Iowa.' Amounts do not vary by county.

There is no partial property tax credit for ratings below 100%. Bills to add tiers (HF 912, HF 910, HF 469 in 2025) were introduced but never passed. Any veteran with wartime service, 20 years of Guard or Reserve, 18 months of active duty, or an early discharge for a service injury can get the $4,000 military exemption instead.

Vehicles: Iowa's free DV plate and registration fee exemption apply only to a vehicle bought with the VA automobile grant (38 U.S.C. 3901-3904), not to a disability rating. DV plates park free in city lots and metered spaces. Bills to waive registration fees for 100% rated veterans (HF 291, HF 912 in 2025) did not pass. Any honorably discharged veteran gets one free set of Veteran plates but pays a $5 yearly fee plus normal registration.

Driver license: operator and motorcycle license fees are waived only for a 'permanent service-connected disability rating of one hundred percent.' The law does not mention TDIU, so ask Iowa DOT before you count on it. Honorably discharged veterans get chauffeur and CDL fees waived. The 'Veteran' designation costs $10 to add to a current card.

Hunting and fishing: any service-connected rating (even 0%) or ex-POW status gets you a $7 lifetime hunting and fishing license after 90 days of Iowa residency. You still pay yearly habitat and other fees. A $5 annual license is open to any veteran with federal active duty. A $65 lifetime trout license is for 100% rated veterans or those with the disabled veteran homestead credit.

Income tax: Iowa has a flat 3.8% income tax (tax year 2025 on). Military retirement pay and military survivor benefits are fully excluded, back to tax year 2014. Active duty pay is excluded. VA disability pay and DIC are not in federal income, so Iowa does not tax them.

Education: a new 2026 law (HF 2491, effective July 1, 2026) waives all tuition and mandatory fees at the three Regents universities for Iowa veterans with a permanent 100% service-connected rating, after Pell and GI Bill money is used up. It does not name TDIU and does not cover community colleges. Veterans with 90 days of Title 10 service get in-state tuition at Regents schools. Iowa has no tuition waiver for children or spouses of living disabled veterans.

Veterans preference in Iowa is a preference 'over other applicants of no greater qualifications' for state, county, city and school jobs, and the hiring officer must put the reasons for a refusal in writing. Point bonuses (5 points, plus 5 more for a service-connected disability) apply to city civil service and point-rated exams in local governments. Apply through your county veterans service officer for Trust Fund grants (income cap 300% of poverty, $20,000 liquid asset cap).

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran Homestead Tax Credit: full credit of all property tax on your homestead
benefits.details: Your whole homestead property tax bill is credited if you are an Iowa resident veteran with an honorable discharge and either a 'permanent service-connected disability rating of one hundred percent' or 'a permanent and total disability rating based on individual unemployability that is compensated at the one hundred percent disability rate.' Veterans who bought the home with a VA specially adapted housing grant also qualify. The credit continues to your unmarried surviving spouse. File Form 54-049 and the homestead form 54-028 with your city or county assessor by July 1, with your DD-214 and VA Benefit Summary letter; no yearly refiling. If you first apply on or after July 1, 2026, the credit covers only one-half acre and no outbuildings (SF 2472, 2026, which moved the law from Iowa Code 425.15 to 425.1(2)(b)).
benefits.source_title: Iowa Legislature - Iowa Code 2026 section 425.15 Disabled veteran tax credit (re-enacted as 425.1(2)(b) by SF 2472, 2026); Iowa Department of Revenue - Disabled Veteran Homestead Property Tax Credit

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran Homestead Tax Credit for surviving spouses and children receiving DIC
benefits.details: A surviving spouse or child who receives VA Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) gets the same full property tax credit on the homestead they own and occupy, in their own right. The Department of Revenue says a DIC surviving spouse 'is eligible for the credit even upon remarriage.' The credit ends when DIC ends. A surviving spouse of a veteran who already had the credit keeps it 'so long as the surviving spouse remains unmarried' and stays in the home. File Form 54-049 with the assessor by July 1 with the VA letter showing DIC.
benefits.source_title: Iowa Department of Revenue - Disabled Veteran Homestead Property Tax Credit (Iowa Code 425.15(1)(d), (2); 425.1(2)(b) as amended by SF 2472, 2026)

benefits.benefit: Military Service Property Tax Exemption: $4,000 of taxable value
benefits.details: Iowa takes $4,000 of taxable value off property owned by an honorably discharged veteran who is 'a resident of and domiciled in the state of Iowa.' You qualify with wartime service under Iowa Code 35.1, 20 years of Guard or Reserve service, 90 days of federal active duty in the Guard or Reserve, 18 months of active duty, or a shorter tour ended by a service-related injury. No disability rating is needed. If the veteran does not claim it, the spouse, unmarried surviving spouse, widowed dependent parent, or minor child may. File Form 54-146 with your city or county assessor by July 1 after recording your DD-214 with the county recorder; it renews automatically while you own the property on July 1. You cannot combine it with the full disabled veteran credit.
benefits.source_title: Iowa Legislature - Iowa Code 2026 chapter 426A Military Service Tax Credit and Exemptions (426A.11, 426A.12, 426A.13); Iowa Department of Revenue Form 54-146

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran (DV) plates with no registration fee for a VA auto-grant vehicle; free parking
benefits.details: If the VA paid for your vehicle under the automobile grant (38 U.S.C. 3901-3904) and you live in Iowa, that vehicle is exempt from the annual registration fee and you get one free set of DV plates or free military special plates. The benefit follows the grant vehicle, not your rating; a replacement vehicle needs new proof. DV plates may park free in any city-owned lot or metered space in Iowa, and the plates carry persons-with-disabilities parking rights (a PWD sticker can be added). Apply at your county treasurer with your DD-214 and VA documents showing the grant. Iowa has no registration fee waiver based on a disability percentage alone.
benefits.source_title: Iowa Legislature - Iowa Code 2026 section 321.105(5); 321.166(6); 321L.2(5); Iowa DOT - Disabled Veteran Plate

benefits.benefit: Veteran, Purple Heart, Ex-POW and Medal of Honor license plates
benefits.details: Any honorably discharged Iowa veteran can get one set of Veteran plates (or branch, Purple Heart, or other armed-forces plates) at no charge, then pay a $5 yearly fee to the Veterans License Fee Fund plus normal registration; a second set is $25 and personalized plates are $25. Ex-POW plates are free with a flat $15 annual registration fee. Medal of Honor plates are free and exempt from all registration fees. A surviving spouse may keep the plates until remarriage. Show your DD-214 (Guard and Reserve need 90 days of active duty other than training, or 20 years). Mail the Special Plate Application to Iowa DOT Vehicle & Motor Carrier Services and pick up the plates at your county treasurer.
benefits.source_title: Iowa Legislature - Iowa Code 2026 section 321.34(8), (8A), (12A), (18); Iowa DOT - Veteran Plate

benefits.benefit: Driver license fee waiver for 100% permanent service-connected veterans; Veteran designation
benefits.details: Iowa DOT does not charge the operator license fee or the motorcycle fee to 'a veteran with a permanent service-connected disability rating of one hundred percent, as certified by the United States department of veterans affairs.' Bring your VA Summary of Benefits letter when you get or renew a license; the waiver is not applied after the fact. The law does not mention TDIU. Honorably discharged veterans of any rating get chauffeur (Class D) and commercial license fees waived with a DD-214. Any honorably discharged veteran with 90 days of active duty can add a 'Veteran' designation; adding it to a current card costs $10.
benefits.source_title: Iowa Legislature - Iowa Code 2026 section 321.191(10); Iowa DOT - Military Fee Waiver; Iowa DOT - Driver's License Designations

benefits.benefit: Lifetime hunting and fishing license ($7), lifetime fur harvester license, and deer tag for disabled veterans
benefits.details: Iowa DNR issues a lifetime hunting and fishing combined license to an Iowa resident who served on federal active duty and 'was disabled or was a prisoner of war' in service; 'disabled' means 'entitled to a service connected rating under 38 U.S.C. ch. 11,' with no minimum percentage. The DNR fee is $7 (optional hard card $6). You must have lived in Iowa at least 90 days and still buy yearly habitat and other fees. The same application gets you a lifetime fur harvester license ($7 on the 7/2026 form; a 2026 law set it at $5 plus processing) and a $33 extra any-deer tag. Send DNR Form 542-1412 with your DD-214 and a current VA rating letter by mail, email, or upload at GoOutdoorsIowa.com. Any veteran with federal active duty can instead buy a $5 annual license, and 100% rated veterans can buy a $65 lifetime trout license.
benefits.source_title: Iowa Legislature - Iowa Code 2026 section 483A.24(16), (17), (20), (21); Iowa DNR Form 542-1412 (7/2026); SF 2471 (2026)

benefits.benefit: Regents university tuition and mandatory fee waiver for 100% permanent service-connected veterans (new 2026)
benefits.details: Starting July 1, 2026, the University of Iowa, Iowa State and the University of Northern Iowa must 'waive all tuition and mandatory fees for a veteran, as defined in section 35.1, who has a permanent service-connected disability rating of one hundred percent' and is admitted. It is a last-dollar benefit: you must first use or be ineligible for Pell grants, GI Bill and other federal or state aid, and the school prorates the waiver each semester to cover the gap. TDIU is not named in the law. Community colleges and private schools are not covered. Ask the university's veterans services office how to apply; implementation details were not yet posted when checked.
benefits.source_title: Iowa Legislature - House File 2491 (2026), enrolled and signed April 30, 2026; Iowa Code 262.9(43)

benefits.benefit: In-state tuition at Regents universities for veterans, Guard and Reserve, active duty and dependents
benefits.details: Board of Regents rules give resident tuition status to 'Honorably discharged veterans who have served an aggregate of 90 days or more on Title 10 orders, other than for training'; other discharges are reviewed case by case. Active duty Title 10 members and their dependents, Iowa Guard and Reserve members assigned to an Iowa unit after initial training or one year of service, retired Iowa Guard members, and people moved to Iowa by military orders (with spouse, domestic partner and children) also qualify. The rule follows Section 702 of the federal Choice Act. Ask the university registrar; documentation may be required.
benefits.source_title: Iowa Administrative Code 681-1.4(2)(b) Board of Regents resident classification (Iowa Code 262.9(3)); ARC 0417D effective 8/12/26

benefits.benefit: Educational assistance for children of Iowa service members who died on active duty (War Orphans fund)
benefits.details: The Iowa Commission of Veterans Affairs pays tuition for a child under 31 whose parent died on or after September 11, 2001 while on active federal military service and had lived in Iowa at least six months before entering service. The award is up to the highest Regents resident undergraduate tuition rate per year, minus other state and federal grants, or the child's financial need if less, with a lifetime cap of five times that rate; the child must start college before age 26. Children of members who died before September 11, 2001 get up to $600 a year ($3,000 lifetime) after two years of Iowa residency. IDVA also runs the Branstad-Reynolds Children of the Fallen scholarship (apply by December 31). Apply through IDVA.
benefits.source_title: Iowa Legislature - Iowa Code 2026 section 35A.13(9) War orphans educational assistance account; IDVA - Children of Fallen Iowa Service Members Scholarship

benefits.benefit: No Iowa income tax on military retired pay, SBP survivor benefits, or active duty pay; flat 3.8% rate
benefits.details: Iowa lets you subtract all 'retirement pay received by a taxpayer from the federal government for military service performed in the armed forces, the armed forces military reserve, or national guard,' plus military survivor benefits under 10 U.S.C. 1447, back to tax year 2014, at any age. Active duty military pay is also subtracted. VA disability compensation and DIC are not in federal adjusted gross income, so Iowa does not tax them. Iowa's income tax is a flat 3.8% starting with tax year 2025. Claim the subtraction on your Iowa return; no separate application.
benefits.source_title: Iowa Legislature - Iowa Code 2026 section 422.7(20), (21), (29); 422.5(1)(a); Iowa Department of Revenue - Military Tax Information

benefits.benefit: Veterans preference in state, county, city and school district hiring
benefits.details: Iowa veterans (honorable discharge; Iowa residency is not required for this benefit) 'are entitled to preference in appointment and employment over other applicants of no greater qualifications' for all state, county, city and school jobs. If you are of good moral character and can do the job, the hiring officer 'shall appoint the applicant' and must file written reasons for any refusal; you can demand the reasons and appeal to district court within 20 days, arbitrate within 60 days, or sue within 300 days. In city civil service and point-rated local exams you get 5 percentage points, plus 5 more if you have any service-connected disability, receive VA compensation or pension, or earned a Purple Heart. Preferred employees can be removed only for incompetency or misconduct after a hearing. Claim it on the job application and attach your DD-214 and VA rating letter.
benefits.source_title: Iowa Legislature - Iowa Code 2026 chapter 35C Veterans Preference (35C.1, 35C.3, 35C.6); Iowa Code 400.10 Veterans preferences (civil service points)

benefits.benefit: Iowa Veterans Trust Fund grants (dental, vision, hearing, medical equipment, repairs, housing, unemployment)
benefits.details: The Iowa Commission of Veterans Affairs pays for needs that other sources will not cover: dental, vision, hearing and prescription costs; durable medical equipment; travel for wounded veterans' follow-up care; job retraining; counseling; emergency vehicle repair, home repair and temporary housing (up to $10,000 lifetime each for repairs, $1,000 per year for transitional housing); up to $500 a month ($3,000 per year, $6,000 lifetime) during unemployment caused by a service-connected illness; and one-time homelessness prevention up to $1,000. Household income, counting VA disability pay, must be at or below 300% of the federal poverty guidelines and liquid assets under $20,000. Veterans, spouses and dependents qualify; a veteran must be an Iowa resident with 90 days of active federal service and an honorable discharge. The rules say a veteran rated 100% TDIU permanent and total does not qualify for the unemployment payments. Apply through your county veterans service officer.
benefits.source_title: Iowa Legislature - Iowa Code 2026 section 35A.13 Veterans trust fund; Iowa Administrative Code 801-14; IDVA - State Benefits

benefits.benefit: Injured Veterans Grant: up to $10,000 for serious injuries in a hazardous duty area after 9/11
benefits.details: Iowa pays a grant 'up to $10,000' in $2,500 steps to service members or veterans 'seriously injured in the line of duty in a hazardous area after September 11, 2001' while receiving combat or hazardous duty pay. The grant is not taxed by Iowa. The amount depends on the severity of the injury under Iowa Administrative Code 801-11. Apply to the Iowa Department of Veterans Affairs with your DD-214 and medical evacuation or injury records, or through your county veterans service officer.
benefits.source_title: Iowa Department of Veterans Affairs - Injured Veterans Grant (Iowa Code 35A.14; IAC 801-11)

benefits.benefit: Iowa Veterans Home (Marshalltown), Iowa Veterans Cemetery (Van Meter), and county veterans service officers
benefits.details: The Iowa Veterans Home in Marshalltown admits honorably discharged veterans who meet Iowa residency on the admission date and need residential or nursing care, plus spouses married at least one year, surviving spouses, and Gold Star parents; a veteran rated 70% or higher who needs nursing care has 'no out of pocket expense.' Get an application at any county Commission of Veterans Affairs office or VA medical center. The Iowa Veterans Cemetery near Van Meter buries honorably separated veterans free; spouses and dependent children pay $300; Iowa residency is not required and pre-need determination is free. Every Iowa county employs an accredited veterans service officer under Iowa Code chapter 35B who files claims and explains state benefits at no charge.
benefits.source_title: Iowa Department of Veterans Affairs - Iowa Veterans Home Admissions; IDVA - Iowa Veterans Cemetery Eligibility for Burial; Iowa Code 35B.6

states.name: Kansas
notes: Kansas has no property tax exemption for disabled veterans. It has two refund programs instead, and both use a 50% or higher VA service-connected evaluation. Bills to create a full or partial exemption or credit (HB 2036 in 2023, HB 2635 in 2024, HB 2005 'Veterans' Valor' in 2025-2026, and the 2026 House Substitute for SB 434) all died. Nothing changed for the 2025 or 2026 tax years.

Both refund programs define 'disabled veteran' by a 'service-connected evaluation percentage equal to or greater than 50%.' TDIU (total disability based on individual unemployability), 100% schedular, and 100% P&T all clear that bar as long as your combined evaluation is at least 50%. Permanence is not required by the statute, but the Department of Revenue asks for documentation of permanent disability and the Kansas Office of Veterans Services describes it as a 50% or greater permanent rating. Send your VA rating letter with the claim.

You can file only one property tax refund claim per household each year: K-40H (Homestead), K-40PT (SAFESR, seniors only), or K-40SVR (Senior or Disabled Veteran). Claims are filed with the Kansas Department of Revenue, not the county. The deadline is April 15 of the year after the tax year (April 15, 2026 for 2025 taxes). Late claims may be accepted for good cause within four years.

For every refund you must have lived in Kansas the entire prior year, must own and occupy the home as your homestead, and the home's appraised value must be $350,000 or less. Income limits apply: $43,389 for K-40H and $58,041 for K-40SVR for the 2025 tax year (indexed each year). VA disability pay, Social Security disability, SSI and Railroad Retirement are not counted as household income.

A surviving spouse who has not remarried can keep the refund if the veteran was receiving it at death. For K-40H the unremarried surviving spouse of a disabled veteran, or of a service member who died in the line of duty, qualifies on his or her own. A surviving spouse who remarries loses the benefit.

New for July 1, 2026: a state and local sales tax exemption for veterans the VA certifies as 100% permanent and total or TDIU (the Kansas Office of Veterans Services names TDIU directly). It covers up to $24,000 of personal purchases per year, but not motor vehicles, alcohol, tobacco or e-cigarettes. You must get a Disabled Veteran Exemption Certificate Card from the Department of Revenue first. A surviving spouse keeps it until remarriage.

The free Disabled Veteran license plate needs a 50% or higher service-connected evaluation and an honorable or general (under honorable conditions) discharge. Registration is free for the first plate, but Kansas still charges personal property tax on the vehicle. Kansas has no vehicle property tax exemption for disabled veterans; the only exemption is for current military and Guard members. There is no driver's license fee waiver for disabled veterans.

The free hunting and fishing license starts at a 30% service-connected evaluation and is permanent, but the Kansas Office of Veterans Services notes it is issued 'based on state funding.' Kansas state parks give no veteran discount; the only reduced-price park permit is the Senior/Disabled permit, and park fees rise on November 1, 2026.

Kansas does not tax military retired pay or VA disability pay. Veterans paid at the 100% rate for a permanent disability also get an extra $2,320 personal exemption on the Kansas return (K.S.A. 79-32,121). No official Kansas source we found addresses SBP or DIC by name.

The Kansas Hero's Scholarship (tuition and required fees for dependents and spouses) uses an 80% rating threshold, or a service-connected disability that ended the member's service, or death in service. The servicemember must be a current Kansas resident (or was one at death). Funding is first come, first served.

In 2024 and 2025 Kansas rewrote most veteran definitions to require an honorable discharge or a general discharge under honorable conditions (L. 2024 ch. 84 and L. 2025 ch. 97). Veterans with other-than-honorable discharges do not qualify for the state benefits listed here. Veteran homes and cemeteries use the VA's 'other than dishonorable' standard instead.

The state veterans agency was renamed in 2024 from the Kansas Commission on Veterans Affairs Office to the Kansas Office of Veterans Services (kovs.ks.gov). Its web pages block automated tools, so some application details below come from statute and Department of Revenue pages. Call KOVS at 785-296-3976 or 800-513-7731 for help.

benefits.benefit: Senior or Disabled Veteran property tax refund (K-40SVR) for 50%+ service-connected veterans
benefits.details: Kansas refunds the increase in your homestead property tax over your base year (the first year you qualified, no earlier than 2021). You qualify if you lived in Kansas all of the prior year, own and occupy the home, have a 'service-connected evaluation percentage equal to or greater than 50%' with an honorable or general (under honorable conditions) discharge, the home's base-year appraised value is $350,000 or less, and household income is $58,041 or less for 2025 claims. A surviving spouse who has not remarried keeps the refund if the veteran was receiving it at death. File Form K-40SVR with the Kansas Department of Revenue after December 31 and by April 15 (April 15, 2026 for 2025 taxes) with a copy of your VA rating letter showing 50% or more. You cannot also file K-40H or K-40PT. This is a refund, not an exemption, and processing takes 20 to 24 weeks.
benefits.source_title: Kansas Office of Revisor of Statutes - K.S.A. 79-4508a Property tax refund for seniors and disabled veterans (L. 2025 ch. 123); KDOR Form K-40SVR (2025)

benefits.benefit: Homestead Refund (K-40H) for 50%+ disabled veterans and surviving spouses
benefits.details: The Homestead Refund pays back part of the property tax on your home, up to $700, scaled down as income rises. You qualify as a disabled veteran if you were a Kansas resident all of 2025, own your home (contract for deed counts, rent-to-own does not), were a disabled veteran (50% or higher service-connected evaluation, honorable or general under honorable conditions discharge) all year, and household income was $43,389 or less. Homes valued at $350,000 or more do not qualify. The unremarried surviving spouse of a disabled veteran, or of a service member who died in the line of duty, also qualifies. File Form K-40H with the Kansas Department of Revenue by April 15, 2026 with your VA rating letter. Only one claim (K-40H, K-40PT or K-40SVR) is allowed per household.
benefits.source_title: Kansas Department of Revenue - 2025 Homestead or Property Tax Refund for Homeowners instructions (K-40H, K-40PT, K-40SVR); K.S.A. 79-4502

benefits.benefit: Sales tax exemption for 100% P&T or TDIU veterans (effective July 1, 2026, up to $24,000 per year)
benefits.details: Starting July 1, 2026, a Kansas resident veteran with an honorable or general (under honorable conditions) discharge who is certified by the VA 'to have a 100% disability or be deemed totally disabled or unemployable,' with a permanent disability from military action, accident or disease in service, pays no state or local sales tax on up to $24,000 of personal-use purchases per year. The Kansas Office of Veterans Services says TDIU counts. Motor vehicles, alcohol, tobacco and e-cigarettes are excluded, and purchases to produce income do not qualify. Your spouse or an authorized household member may buy for you. A surviving spouse keeps the exemption until remarriage. Apply first to the Department of Revenue (online or paper Form K-97) with your DD-214 and VA award letter; you get a wallet-size Disabled Veteran Exemption Certificate Card to show retailers. Created by 2024 HB 2098 (K.S.A. 79-3606h).
benefits.source_title: Kansas Department of Revenue - Disabled Veteran Tax Exemption (K.S.A. 79-3606h); KDOR Notice 26-01 (May 15, 2026)

benefits.benefit: Free Disabled Veteran license plate and registration, plus free metered and attended-lot parking
benefits.details: A Kansas resident with an honorable or general (under honorable conditions) discharge and a 'service-connected evaluation percentage equal to or greater than 50%' gets one Disabled Veteran plate with no registration fee, for a car, motorcycle or truck of 20,000 pounds or less that you own or lease. You still pay the vehicle's personal property tax. Extra DV plates for other vehicles carry the regular registration fee. With the plate you may park free in metered zones without time limits and free in reserved accessible spaces in attended public lots; the version with the wheelchair symbol (needs a medical certification under K.S.A. 8-1,124) also allows parking in accessible spaces. Complete Form TR-103, signed by you and the VA regional office, and apply at your county treasurer's motor vehicle office with proof of insurance. Carry the state ID card when using accessible parking.
benefits.source_title: Kansas Department of Revenue, Division of Vehicles - Kansas Disabled Veteran Plate (K.S.A. 8-160 and 8-161, L. 2025 ch. 97)

benefits.benefit: Purple Heart and other military plates (regular fee) and free VETERAN designation on driver's license
benefits.details: Kansas issues a Purple Heart plate to a resident who proves the award for wounds 'in military or naval combat against an armed enemy of the United States,' for each car, truck under 20,000 pounds or motorcycle. You pay the regular registration fee; there is no fee waiver. Other military plates (branch, Vietnam, Korea, Desert Storm, Iraqi Freedom, Enduring Freedom, Bronze Star, Silver Star, Gold Star Mother, Families of the Fallen, POW) work the same way. Any veteran with a DD-214 showing an honorable or general (under honorable conditions) discharge may ask the Division of Vehicles to print VETERAN on a driver's license or ID card; no extra fee for the designation is listed, but regular license fees apply. Apply at your county treasurer (plates) or driver's license office (designation).
benefits.source_title: Kansas Office of Revisor of Statutes - K.S.A. 8-1,140 Purple Heart license plates; K.S.A. 8-243 (VETERAN designation); KOVS State Veterans Benefits page

benefits.benefit: Free permanent hunting and fishing license for 30%+ disabled resident veterans
benefits.details: The Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks issues a free permanent hunting and fishing license to any Kansas resident who was discharged honorably or with a general discharge under honorable conditions, whose disability was incurred or aggravated in the line of duty, and who has a service-connected evaluation of 30% or more. Apply online through Go Outdoors Kansas (Customer Applications) or mail the Disabled Veterans Hunt and Fish License Application to KDWP Licensing, 512 SE 25th Ave, Pratt, KS 67124, with your Kansas driver's license or ID, your VA letter showing at least 30%, and your hunter education card if born on or after July 1, 1957. Allow two weeks. The license covers the hunting and fishing license itself; the official pages do not say it covers big game permits, stamps or park permits. The Kansas Office of Veterans Services notes the licenses are issued 'based on state funding.'
benefits.source_title: Kansas Office of Revisor of Statutes - K.S.A. 32-934 Disabled veterans hunting and fishing licenses (L. 2025 ch. 97); KDWP Special Licenses and Permits page

benefits.benefit: State park vehicle permits: no veteran discount; reduced Senior/Disabled permit only
benefits.details: Kansas state parks charge a vehicle permit and offer no veteran or disabled veteran discount. The only reduced permit is the Senior/Disabled annual vehicle permit, $13.75 for 2025 versus $25.00 regular (rising to $20.25 versus $39.00 on November 1, 2026), and a Senior/Disabled daily permit of $3.25 ($4.25 after November 1, 2026). KDWP describes it as for residents 65 or older or persons with disabilities who display a disability plate or placard; whether a Disabled Veteran plate without the wheelchair symbol qualifies is not stated, so ask at the park office. Free park permits go only to active Kansas National Guard members. A State Park Passport ($15.50, $30.50 after November 1, 2026) can be added when you register your vehicle at the county treasurer.
benefits.source_title: Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks - Kansas State Park Entrance and Camping Fees (2025 fees and fees beginning 11/1/2026)

benefits.benefit: Kansas Hero's Scholarship: tuition and fees for dependents and spouses of 80%+ disabled veterans
benefits.details: Dependents and spouses attend any public Kansas college, university, technical college or Washburn without paying tuition and required fees for up to 10 undergraduate semesters. The servicemember must be a current Kansas resident (or was one at death) and must have died in service, or sustained a service-connected injury or disability that made the member 'incapable of continuing military service,' or be 'entitled to compensation for a service-connected disability of at least 80%.' Dependents and spouses of Kansas public safety officers and former POWs also qualify. A spouse must not have remarried. Funding is limited and first come, first served. Apply at sfa.kansasregents.gov with the DD-214, VA letter and residency proof; 2026-27 deadlines are July 1, 2026 (summer), September 1, 2026 (fall) and February 1, 2027 (spring). Post-9/11 GI Bill users should check how this restricted aid affects VA tuition payments.
benefits.source_title: Kansas Board of Regents - Kansas Hero's Scholarship 2026-2027 information and required documentation (K.S.A. 75-4364)

benefits.benefit: In-state tuition for veterans and families; Kansas Military Service Scholarship
benefits.details: A veteran with an honorable or general (under honorable conditions) discharge who was stationed in Kansas at least 11 months or lived in Kansas before service, and lives in Kansas when enrolling, pays in-state tuition at Kansas public colleges no matter how long he or she has been in the state; the spouse and dependent children get the same. Current service members and their families, and anyone using federal GI Bill benefits who lives in Kansas and files a letter of intent to stay, are also treated as residents. Separately, the Kansas Military Service Scholarship pays tuition and fees for up to 8 undergraduate semesters for a Kansas resident who received hostile fire pay for at least 90 days after September 11, 2001 (or fewer days because of injury), is honorably discharged or still serving, and files a FAFSA; priority date May 1. Contact the school registrar for tuition status and the Board of Regents (785-430-4300) for the scholarship.
benefits.source_title: Kansas Office of Revisor of Statutes - K.S.A. 48-3601 Residency for tuition purposes; veterans and families (L. 2025 ch. 97); KOVS State Veterans Benefits page (Kansas Military Service Scholarship)

benefits.benefit: Military retired pay and VA disability pay not taxed by Kansas
benefits.details: Kansas lets you subtract all military retirement benefits (and federal civil service retirement) from Kansas income on Schedule S, line A14, with no age or income limit. VA disability compensation is not in federal adjusted gross income and is not taxed by Kansas; the Kansas Office of Veterans Services lists 'Department of Veterans Affairs Disability Payments' as not taxed. Military recruitment and retention bonuses and certain military student loan repayments are also subtracted (line A17). Active duty pay is taxed only by your state of legal residence. No official Kansas page addresses Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP) or DIC by name.
benefits.source_title: Kansas Department of Revenue - 2025 Individual Income Tax Booklet, Schedule S line A14 (K.S.A. 79-32,117(c)(vii)); KOVS State Veterans Benefits page

benefits.benefit: Additional $2,320 Kansas income tax exemption for 100% permanently disabled veterans
benefits.details: An honorably discharged veteran 'certified by the United States department of veterans affairs ... to be in receipt of disability compensation at the 100% rate, if the disability is permanent and was sustained through military action or accident or resulted from disease contracted while in such active service' gets an extra Kansas personal exemption of $2,320 for tax year 2025 and later ($2,250 for 2023 and 2024). The Kansas Office of Veterans Services describes this as 100% permanent and total. The law does not mention TDIU. Claim it in the exemptions section of Form K-40; keep your VA letter. For 2025 the standard exemptions are $18,320 (joint) or $9,160 (other filers) plus $2,320 per dependent.
benefits.source_title: Kansas Office of Revisor of Statutes - K.S.A. 79-32,121 Kansas personal exemption; additional exemption for disabled veterans (L. 2025 ch. 112)

benefits.benefit: Veterans' preference in state, county and city hiring (guaranteed interview; hire if competent)
benefits.details: Kansas gives veterans preference for initial hire and first promotion if they are 'competent' for the job, in state government and in Kansas counties and cities. For state classified jobs marked Veterans Preference Eligible, every qualifying veteran who meets the requirements must be offered an interview (unless a Kansas Employee Preference Program applicant applied). You qualify with an honorable or general (under honorable conditions) discharge and wartime or campaign service, any VA service-connected disability, a Purple Heart, or release with a service-connected disability. Spouses of veterans rated 100% or unemployable, unremarried spouses of members who died in service, and POW spouses also qualify. Officers who retired at O-4 or above are excluded unless retired for combat wounds or rated 10% or more. Claim it on the application with your DD-214; you must be notified within 30 days if not hired and may appeal. There are no preference points.
benefits.source_title: Kansas Department of Administration, Office of Personnel Services - Veterans Preference: How do I Determine if I am Eligible? (K.S.A. 73-201, L. 2025 ch. 97)

benefits.benefit: Disabled veteran business contract preference (30%+) and military spouse license fee exemption
benefits.details: State agencies must give preference to Kansas disabled veteran businesses (at least 51% owned and controlled by veterans with a 'service-connected evaluation percentage equal to or greater than 30%' and an honorable or general under honorable conditions discharge), with a goal of 3% of contracts. A disabled veteran business that is a responsible bidder wins the contract if its bid is not more than 10% above the lowest bid. Register with the Department of Administration, Procurement and Contracts. Separately, since July 1, 2025 the spouse of a current member, or of a former member with an honorable discharge, pays no application, licensing, renewal or background check fees to any Kansas occupational licensing body (K.S.A. 48-3406).
benefits.source_title: Kansas Office of Veterans Services - State Veterans Benefits (K.S.A. 73-230, 75-3740 Disabled Owned Veteran Business; K.S.A. 48-3406 Spouses Application Fees Exemption)

benefits.benefit: Kansas Soldiers' Home (Fort Dodge) and Kansas Veterans' Home (Winfield) long-term care
benefits.details: Kansas runs two veterans homes with skilled nursing, dementia care and domiciliary units: the Kansas Soldiers' Home at Fort Dodge and the Kansas Veterans' Home at Winfield (a third home in Topeka is awaiting federal construction funds). You must meet VA veteran status with a discharge 'under conditions other than dishonorable,' need 24-hour skilled nursing care documented by a physician, and have no felony record or sex offender registration. Spouses, surviving spouses and Gold Star Parents may be admitted as space allows. Kansas residency is not required, but Kansas residents get preference, and veterans without adequate means of support get first priority. Charges depend on ability to pay; the Legislative Research Department reports veterans rated 70% or higher pay no resident fees, which we could not confirm on the KOVS site. Apply through KOVS with VA Form 10-10EZ and the Application for Admission.
benefits.source_title: Kansas Office of Veterans Services - Veteran Homes: Eligibility and Admissions (K.S.A. 76-1908, 76-1954)

benefits.benefit: Free burial in Kansas Veterans' Cemeteries (Fort Dodge, Fort Riley, WaKeeney, Winfield)
benefits.details: Kansas operates four state veterans cemeteries. Eligibility follows VA National Cemetery Administration rules: discharge from active duty under other than dishonorable conditions, death on active duty, or 20 qualifying years of Guard or Reserve service with retired pay eligibility. There is no Kansas residency requirement and no fee for the veteran or eligible dependents; the state provides the grave, liner, opening and closing, marker and perpetual care (a fee can apply only if you decline the standard liner or need an oversized one). Spouses, surviving spouses (even if remarried to a non-veteran, for deaths on or after January 1, 2000), unmarried children under 21 (23 if full-time students) and permanently disabled adult children may be buried there even if the veteran is not. Pre-register with KVCP Form 200 and your DD-214.
benefits.source_title: Kansas Office of Veterans Services - Kansas Veterans' Cemetery Program

states.name: Kentucky
notes: Kentucky has no veteran-specific property tax exemption. The only break is the general homestead exemption in Section 170 of the Kentucky Constitution and KRS 132.810 for owners who are 65 or older or 'totally disabled.' It takes $49,100 off the assessed value of your home for the 2025 and 2026 tax years (the Department of Revenue resets the amount every two years). It is not a full exemption. The same amount applies in every county.

The homestead law does not say '100 percent,' 'permanent and total,' or 'individual unemployability.' It says you must be 'classified as totally disabled under a program authorized or administered by an agency of the United States government' and must 'have received disability payments pursuant to the disability.' A VA 100% rating is a total disability rating, so it fits. TDIU is also a total rating for pay purposes, but no official Kentucky source names TDIU, so ask your county PVA. P&T is not required, but you must keep the total classification for the whole tax year, and the PVA can ask for proof of continuing disability at any time. A veteran rated 'service-connected totally disabled' does not have to reapply every year; other disabled owners under 65 do.

To get the homestead exemption, file Form 62A350 with the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) in your county by December 31 of the tax year. You must own and live in the home as your personal residence on January 1. Only one exemption per home, even if you are both 65 and disabled. There is no surviving spouse carryover; a spouse qualifies only on his or her own age or disability. If you no longer meet the disability classification, you must tell the PVA, or you can be billed for up to five years of back taxes.

Bills to create a real disabled veteran property tax exemption have been filed in Kentucky for years but none has passed. In 2025, HB 639 (new homestead exemption for veterans with a service-connected disability) died in committee. In 2026, HB 285 (up to $100,000 for veterans rated 50% or more), HB 587, HB 242 and SB 169 (constitutional amendments for disabled veterans) all died in committee. Kentucky needs a constitutional amendment approved by voters before the legislature can give disabled veterans more than the regular homestead amount.

The free Disabled Veteran license plate needs a VA rating of exactly 100% service-connected (or a VA grant to buy or adapt a vehicle, or the Medal of Honor). Veterans rated 50% to 99% can get a Disabled Veteran plate but pay $23 to get it and $23 to renew. A 2025 bill (HB 157) that would have made all veteran plates free was changed in the Senate and that part was dropped. A 2026 law (Acts ch. 161) rewrites the fee list effective January 1, 2027; the 100% plate stays at $0. Kentucky does not waive driver license fees for disabled veterans. The accessible parking placard is free to anyone with a qualifying mobility impairment, veteran or not.

The Disabled Sportsman's hunting and fishing license needs a 50% or higher service-connected rating and Kentucky residency. You first get a disability authorization from Kentucky Fish and Wildlife (good for 3 years), then buy the license each year. The regulation sets the price at $12; the Fish and Wildlife fee page shows $12.68 after a 2026 cost-of-living adjustment. The regular Resident Sportsman's License is $100.42, so this is a large discount.

Kentucky State Parks give veterans rated 100% service-connected who live in Kentucky up to three free overnight stays a year (three nights each) in a lodge room, cottage or campsite. You must call the park no more than 10 days ahead and bring your VA letter and proof of Kentucky residency. In summer and October, stays must fall Sunday through Thursday. There is no free pass for veterans rated below 100%; active and retired military get 15% off lodging.

The Kentucky Tuition Waiver is for your spouse and children, not for you. The veteran must be rated 100% service-connected for compensation (or P&T for VA pension), be a POW or MIA, or have died on active duty or from a service-connected cause, and must be a current Kentucky resident (or a resident at death). Children must start before age 26 and get up to 45 months; spouses have no age limit. It waives tuition only, not fees, books or housing, at Kentucky public schools. TDIU is not named in KRS 164.515. A 2026 bill to turn the waiver into a last-dollar scholarship with a 128-credit-hour cap (HB 497) passed the House but died in the Senate, so the rules above still apply.

Kentucky taxes income at a flat rate: 4% for 2025 and 3.5% for 2026 (KRS 141.020, as changed by 2025 HB 1). Active duty military pay is fully exempt. Military retired pay gets the general pension exclusion of up to $31,110 per person; if you retired before January 1, 1998, your military pension is fully exempt, and if you retired later, the part earned before 1998 is exempt on Schedule P. VA disability compensation is not in federal adjusted gross income, which is where the Kentucky return starts, so Kentucky does not tax it.

Kentucky state hiring preference is an interview preference, not points. Since June 27, 2019 (HB 338), any veteran with an honorable, under honorable conditions, or general discharge, their spouse, unremarried surviving spouse, current service members and their spouses, and a dependent parent of a member who died or became permanently and totally disabled from service, must be offered an interview for a competitive classified job they are minimally qualified for (at least five such applicants, or all if fewer). A disability rating does not add anything extra.

Kentucky runs five state veterans nursing homes (Wilmore, Hazard, Hanson, Radcliff and Bowling Green). You must be a veteran with a discharge that is not dishonorable, need nursing care, and be a Kentucky resident on the day you are admitted. Spouses are not eligible. Kentucky's five state veterans cemeteries do not require Kentucky residency; burial is free for the veteran and the KDVA page lists a $500 spousal fee. Starting January 1, 2026, Guard and Reserve members who finished their initial service obligation are also eligible.

benefits.benefit: Homestead exemption for totally disabled owners ($49,100 off assessed value, 2025-2026)
benefits.details: Kentucky has no veteran-only property tax exemption. If a federal agency classifies you as totally disabled and you get disability payments for it, or you are 65 or older, you can take $49,100 off the assessed value of the home you own and live in as your residence on January 1. The Department of Revenue's PVA manual accepts a VA 100% combined rating, and also accepts a rating below 100% if your VA award letter shows Individual Unemployability (TDIU). File Form 62A350 with your county Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) by December 31 of the tax year with your VA award letter. A service-connected totally disabled veteran does not have to reapply each year. Only one exemption per home, and no surviving spouse carryover.
benefits.source_title: Guidelines for Administering the Homestead Exemption, Commonwealth of Kentucky Department of Revenue (2024), Situation #22

benefits.benefit: Free Disabled Veteran license plate (100%); $23 plate for 50% to 99%; local vehicle fee exemption
benefits.details: If the VA has declared you 'one hundred percent (100%) service-connected disabled,' or you received VA help to buy a vehicle, or you hold the Medal of Honor, the Disabled Veteran plate costs $0 to get and $0 to renew, with no limit on the number of vehicles you own or lease. Veterans rated 'between fifty percent (50%) and ninety-nine percent (99%)' pay $23 initial and $23 renewal. Apply at your county clerk with Form TC 96-217 (notarized) and your VA rating letter; the clerk collects usage tax but no registration fee. Disabled Veteran plates expire July 31. With the plate, no city or county may charge you a local vehicle license or fee, and you may park two hours past posted limits. Fees are restructured January 1, 2027 under 2026 Acts ch. 161; the 100% plate stays free.
benefits.source_title: Kentucky Legislature - KRS 186.162(2)(a) and (2)(d) Special license plates fees (effective until Jan. 1, 2027); KRS 186.041; KRS 189.4595; Transportation Cabinet Form TC 96-217 (rev. 10/2025)

benefits.benefit: Purple Heart license plate ($23 initial, $11 renewal) with surviving spouse retention
benefits.details: Purple Heart recipients, former POWs and Pearl Harbor survivors can get a special plate for $23 initial and $11 renewal; $5 of each fee goes to the Kentucky Veterans' Program Trust Fund. Show your DD-214 or VA ID card plus proof of the award at the county clerk. A surviving spouse may keep the Purple Heart plate on the same or a replacement vehicle and renew it as long as the registration fee is paid. A 2026 law changes the fee split effective January 1, 2027 ($17 initial, $5 renewal plus clerk fee).
benefits.source_title: Kentucky Legislature - KRS 186.041 Special military-related license plates (effective July 15, 2026); KRS 186.162(2)(b)

benefits.benefit: 'Veteran' designation on driver license or ID card (no disabled veteran license fee waiver)
benefits.details: Any veteran can ask that the word 'veteran' be printed on a Kentucky driver license or personal ID card when first applying, renewing or getting a duplicate. Show an unexpired VA Veteran ID Card or Veteran Health ID Card, a DD-2, DD-214, DD-256, DD-257 or NGB-22, or a Geneva Conventions ID card at a Driver Licensing Regional Office. Kentucky does not waive driver license or ID card fees for disabled veterans; KRS 186.531 has no veteran exemption. The free accessible parking placard (KRS 189.456) is available to any person with a qualifying mobility impairment through the county clerk.
benefits.source_title: Kentucky Legislature - KRS 186.416(4) Veteran's designation on operator's license or personal ID card (effective July 15, 2026); KRS 186.531; KRS 189.456

benefits.benefit: Resident Disabled Sportsman's hunting and fishing license ($12 base fee) for 50%+ service-connected veterans
benefits.details: A Kentucky resident who is 'an American veteran at least fifty percent (50%) disabled as a result of a service-connected disability' can buy the Disabled Sportsman's License. It includes the combination hunting and fishing license, all deer permits, spring and fall turkey permits, the Kentucky migratory bird and waterfowl permit and the trout permit (the same package as the $100.42 Resident Sportsman's License). The regulation sets the fee at $12; the Fish and Wildlife fee page shows $12.68 after the 2026 adjustment. First get a disability authorization (valid 3 years) by sending a VA letter showing at least 50% to Kentucky Fish and Wildlife online through My Profile, by mail, fax or in person in Frankfort. Then buy the license each year; it runs March 1 to the end of February. You still need the federal duck stamp and HIP survey for waterfowl.
benefits.source_title: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources - Senior and Disabled Licenses (KRS 150.175(27); 301 KAR 5:022; fw.ky.gov Fees page)

benefits.benefit: Free Kentucky State Parks lodging or camping for 100% service-connected veterans (3 stays per year)
benefits.details: Kentucky State Parks give a free lodge room, cottage or campsite to a veteran who is '100% disabled as a direct result of a service-connected incident and is a current Kentucky resident.' Kentucky National Guard or Reserve members disabled the same way also qualify. You get up to three overnight stays per calendar year, three nights maximum per visit, subject to availability. From Memorial Day to Labor Day and in October, stays must start and end Sunday through Thursday. The free room covers only the veteran's own accommodation; pet fees still apply. Call the park no more than 10 days before arrival and bring your VA disability letter and proof of Kentucky residency. Active and retired military get 15% off lodging and 10% off campsites; former POWs camp free.
benefits.source_title: Kentucky State Parks - Deals and Discounts: Kentucky Disabled Veterans Lodging Guidelines

benefits.benefit: Kentucky Tuition Waiver for spouse and children of 100% disabled, P&T, POW or MIA veterans (KRS 164.515)
benefits.details: Your spouse (any age) and your children, stepchildren or orphans under 26 pay no tuition at Kentucky state-supported colleges, universities and vocational schools for up to 45 months or until they earn a degree. You must be 'a permanently and totally disabled war veteran, or a one hundred percent (100%) service-connected disabled veteran regardless of wartime service,' rated 'permanently and totally disabled for pension purposes or one hundred percent (100%) disabled for compensation purposes' by the VA or Defense Department, or a POW or MIA. You must have an honorable-conditions discharge and be a current Kentucky resident (or a Kentucky resident at death). The waiver covers tuition only, not fees, books or housing, and does not work at private or out-of-state schools. Apply to KDVA (KDVA.TuitionWaiver@ky.gov, 502-503-7911) after the student is accepted, with birth or marriage certificate, VA award letter and DD-214; allow 30 days.
benefits.source_title: Kentucky Legislature - KRS 164.515 Exemption from tuition for spouse or child under age 26 of permanently disabled member of the National Guard, war veteran, prisoner of war, or MIA; KDVA Education for Veterans in Kentucky page

benefits.benefit: Tuition waiver for spouse and children of veterans who died in service or of a service-connected cause
benefits.details: If a Kentucky veteran died on active duty, was killed in action, or died from a service-connected disability, the unremarried spouse and children or stepchildren pay no matriculation or tuition fees at Kentucky state-supported schools. Under KRS 164.505 (killed in service or died of a service-connected disability during a war, national emergency or UN action, with Kentucky as home of record) there is no age or time limit and graduate degrees count. Under KRS 164.507 (any wartime veteran who was a Kentucky resident at death, or who died on active duty or from a service-connected disability) children under 26 get up to 45 months. Proof is a death certificate, VA or Defense Department records, and birth or marriage certificates. Apply through KDVA.
benefits.source_title: Kentucky Legislature - KRS 164.505 Exemption from matriculation or tuition fee of dependents, widow, or widower of members killed while in service or having died as a result of service-connected disability; KRS 164.507

benefits.benefit: Income tax: $31,110 pension exclusion, pre-1998 military retirement fully exempt, 3.5% rate for 2026
benefits.details: Kentucky's flat income tax is 4% for 2025 and 3.5% for tax years starting January 1, 2026. Active duty military pay is fully exempt. Military retired pay is treated like any pension: you exclude up to $31,110 per person. If you retired before January 1, 1998, your entire military pension is exempt; if you retired after December 31, 1997, the part earned before 1998 is exempt based on an 'exempt percentage' you figure on Schedule P. VA disability compensation is excluded from federal adjusted gross income, which is the starting point for the Kentucky return, so it is not taxed. Kentucky National Guard members get a $20 credit.
benefits.source_title: Kentucky Legislature - KRS 141.019(1)(g) and (l) Calculation of adjusted gross income (pension exclusion, military pay); KRS 141.020(2)(e)-(f) tax rate; DOR Military Tax Issues page; DOR Schedule P

benefits.benefit: Interview preference for state classified jobs (veterans, spouses, surviving spouses, dependent parents)
benefits.details: If you served in the Armed Forces, Reserves or National Guard and were discharged with an honorable, under honorable conditions, or general discharge, you get interview preference for any competitive classified state job you meet the minimum qualifications for. The same goes for your spouse, your unremarried widow or widower, current service members and their spouses, and a parent dependent on a member who died in service or 'became permanently and totally disabled as a result of a service-connected disability.' The agency must interview at least five preference applicants, or all of them if fewer than five. It applies only to initial appointment, not promotions. Kentucky dropped the old 5 and 10 point system in 2019. Claim it when you apply on the Personnel Cabinet careers site and upload your DD-214.
benefits.source_title: Kentucky Legislature - KRS 18A.150 Interview preference for current service members, honorably or generally discharged former service members, and members' spouses, surviving spouses, and dependent parents (effective June 27, 2019); Personnel Memo 19-07

benefits.benefit: Kentucky Veterans Centers (five state veterans nursing homes)
benefits.details: KDVA runs skilled nursing homes at Wilmore (Thomson-Hood), Hazard (Paul E. Patton Eastern Kentucky), Hanson (Joseph Eddie Ballard Western Kentucky), Radcliff (Carl M. Brashear) and Bowling Green (Robert E. Spiller). To be admitted you must 'be a veteran,' 'be disabled by reason of disease, wounds, age, or otherwise is in need of nursing care,' 'be a Kentucky resident as of the date of admission,' and have a discharge 'that is not of a dishonorable nature.' Spouses are not eligible. Bring your DD-214, proof of Kentucky residency, insurance cards, and your VA award letter if you are rated 70% or higher. Contact the admissions coordinator at the center you want; an admission committee reviews each case.
benefits.source_title: Kentucky Department of Veterans Affairs - Admission to State Veterans Homes (KRS 40.325; 17 KAR 3:040)

benefits.benefit: Burial in a Kentucky State Veterans Cemetery (five cemeteries, no residency requirement)
benefits.details: Kentucky has five state veterans cemeteries: Kentucky Veterans Cemetery West, Central, North, North East and South East. Anyone eligible for a national cemetery under 38 U.S.C. 2402 qualifies, including spouses, minor children and some unmarried adult dependent children. Kentucky residency is not required. Starting January 1, 2026 (2025 Acts ch. 20), Guard and Reserve members who completed their initial service obligation with a discharge other than dishonorable, and Guard members who died on state active duty or Title 32 duty, are also eligible. Burial, plot, vault, headstone and perpetual care are free for the veteran; the KDVA page lists a $500 spousal fee due at the time of death. File the Kentucky Veterans Cemeteries Eligibility Application with KDVA in advance to speed things up.
benefits.source_title: Kentucky Department of Veterans Affairs - Kentucky Veterans Cemeteries (KRS 40.315, effective Jan. 1, 2026)

states.name: Louisiana
notes: Louisiana's disabled veteran property tax break is written into the state constitution (Article VII, Section 21(K)). It is an add-on to the regular $7,500 homestead exemption and applies only to the home you own and live in. The tiers are 50% to 69% (an extra $2,500 of assessed value), 70% to 99% (an extra $4,500), and 100% (the rest of the assessed value). Louisiana assesses homes at 10 percent of market value, so $7,500 of assessed value is about $75,000 of home value.

The 100% tier uses the words 'one hundred percent unemployability or totally disabled.' That means a total disability based on individual unemployability (TDIU) counts. The constitution does not say the rating must be permanent, so a 100% schedular rating that is not marked permanent and total (P&T) should also qualify. Ask your parish assessor what VA letter they want.

There is no single statewide filing deadline for the veteran exemption. You apply at your parish assessor's office, usually in person, with your VA rating letter and proof you own and live in the home. Each parish assessor sets its own paperwork, so call first. Jefferson Parish, for example, requires an in-person visit with a recorded act of sale and photo ID.

The 100% exemption does not always wipe out your whole tax bill. The homestead exemption covers state, parish, and special district taxes. City (municipal) taxes and fees may still be billed in many cities. The East Baton Rouge assessor says 'city taxes and fees will still be due.' Check your own parish and city.

A surviving spouse keeps the veteran exemption only while the spouse 'occupies and remains the owner of the property.' The spouse qualifies even if the veteran never claimed the exemption before dying. On November 3, 2026, voters will decide Act 39 of 2026 (SB 180), which would drop the stay-in-the-home rule and let the spouse move the exemption one time to a new home, starting with tax year 2027. Until voters approve it, the old rule stands.

The free 100% DAV license plate needs a 100% service-connected rating; a 50% rating gets you a free disabled veteran or military honor plate and mobility-impaired parking privileges, a free driver license or ID card, free hunting and fishing licenses, free state park day use, and free airport parking. Most of these need a form or affidavit signed by a Veterans Assistance Counselor at your parish veterans service office, so start there.

The free hunting and fishing license requires a 'permanent service connected disability classification of fifty percent or more.' It is open to residents and nonresidents and must be renewed each year. Veterans without a 50% rating can buy a $20 combination license (Act 321 of 2025, effective August 1, 2025) if they are Louisiana residents with an honorable discharge.

Title 29 tuition exemption is for children (ages 16 to 25) and spouses of veterans rated 90% to 100% or found unemployable, or who died in service or from a wartime service-connected disability. The veteran must have lived in Louisiana for 12 months (before entering service, before death, or before the child enrolls). It covers tuition and most fees at Louisiana public colleges. Apply through your parish veterans service office; LDVA issues a certificate you take to the school.

Louisiana does not tax military retired pay or Survivor Benefit Plan payments (R.S. 47:44.2). VA disability pay is not taxed because Louisiana starts with federal adjusted gross income. Since tax year 2025 the state has a flat 3% income tax with a $12,500 standard deduction ($25,000 joint) under Act 11 of the 2024 Third Extraordinary Session. A 2025 bill for a special disabled veteran deduction (HB 402) did not pass.

State and city civil service give 10 preference points to any honorably discharged veteran with a service-connected disability (any percentage) and 5 points to wartime and post-9/11 veterans. Points are added only on original hire and only if you pass the test. You must attach your DD-214 and a VA letter dated within the last 6 months.

Louisiana has no state veteran bonus, no vehicle sales tax exemption for disabled veterans, and no veteran-specific income tax deduction. A bill to add a vehicle sales tax exemption was not found enacted. New residents, veteran or not, pay no more than $90 use tax on a car they already owned (R.S. 47:302(D)).

benefits.benefit: Full homestead property tax exemption for 100% unemployability or totally disabled veterans
benefits.details: If the VA rates you 100% or pays you at the 100% rate for individual unemployability (TDIU), the constitution exempts 'the remaining assessed valuation' of your homestead from ad valorem tax, on top of the regular $7,500 homestead exemption. The exact words are 'one hundred percent unemployability or totally disabled by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs.' No permanent and total (P&T) requirement is written in the law. You must own and occupy the home. Apply at your parish assessor's office with your VA rating letter; there is no statewide deadline, so file as soon as you qualify. City taxes and fees may still be due in some municipalities.
benefits.source_title: Louisiana Constitution Art. VII, Sec. 21(K)(1)(c) (as amended by Acts 2022, No. 172, approved Nov. 8, 2022); LDVA State Benefits page

benefits.benefit: Additional $4,500 assessed value exemption for 70% to 99% service-connected veterans
benefits.details: If your VA service-connected rating is 'seventy percent or more but less than one hundred percent,' the next $4,500 of assessed value after the $7,500 homestead exemption is exempt, for a total of $12,000 of assessed value (about $120,000 of home value). You pay tax only on assessed value above $12,000. You must own and occupy the home as your homestead. Bring your VA rating letter to your parish assessor. The exemption began with tax year 2023.
benefits.source_title: Louisiana Constitution Art. VII, Sec. 21(K)(1)(b); East Baton Rouge Parish Assessor - Extended Homestead Exemption for Qualifying Veterans

benefits.benefit: Additional $2,500 assessed value exemption for 50% to 69% service-connected veterans
benefits.details: If your VA service-connected rating is 'fifty percent or more but less than seventy percent,' the next $2,500 of assessed value after the $7,500 homestead exemption is exempt, for a total of $10,000 of assessed value (about $100,000 of home value). Tax applies only to assessed value above $10,000. You must own and live in the home. File with your parish assessor with your VA rating letter; each assessor sets its own paperwork.
benefits.source_title: Louisiana Constitution Art. VII, Sec. 21(K)(1)(a); Jefferson Parish Assessor - Homestead Exemption

benefits.benefit: Surviving spouse continuation of the disabled veteran exemption (and pending 2026 transfer amendment)
benefits.details: The surviving spouse of a veteran in any tier (50% to 69%, 70% to 99%, or 100%) keeps the same exemption 'if the surviving spouse occupies and remains the owner of the property, whether or not the exemption was in effect on the property prior to the death of the veteran.' There is no remarriage rule in the text. Today the exemption is lost if the spouse sells and moves. Act 39 of 2026 (SB 180) asks voters on November 3, 2026 to remove the occupy-and-own rule and allow a one-time transfer of the exemption to a new homestead, capped at the amount claimed in the last year on the old home, starting with tax year 2027. Check with your parish assessor after the election.
benefits.source_title: Louisiana Legislature - 2026 Regular Session SB 180 (Act 39) proposing to amend Const. Art. VII, Sec. 21(K)(1); current text at Const. Art. VII, Sec. 21(K)

benefits.benefit: Free 100% DAV military honor license plate with accessibility symbol and free hang tag
benefits.details: A Louisiana resident with 'a service-connected disability of one hundred percent as determined by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs' gets a free lifetime plate marked '100% DAV' with the international symbol of accessibility, one for each vehicle registered in your name. No fee and no renewal. Holders get the same parking privileges as mobility-impaired plate holders and may also request a free accessibility hang tag that never needs renewal. Apply at any Office of Motor Vehicles (OMV) office with your vehicle registration and an LDVA-17 affidavit signed by a veterans service officer. Transfers to another of your vehicles cost $3; a lost plate costs $10 plus an $8 handling fee.
benefits.source_title: R.S. 47:490.31 Military honor license plate; 100% disabled veteran (Acts 2016, No. 194); OMV Policy 160.00 (rev. 08/28/2017)

benefits.benefit: Free disabled veteran, military honor, and Purple Heart DV plates and parking privileges for 50% or higher
benefits.details: LDVA says veterans rated 50% or higher may get a disabled veteran plate or a military honor plate at no charge, and OMV policy lets 'veterans who have a 50% or more service connected disability' get a mobility-impaired license plate and permanent placard with an affidavit from the Veterans Affairs office instead of a doctor's certificate. Purple Heart recipients 'who have a service-connected disability of fifty percent or more' get a free 'DV' Purple Heart plate and a free accessibility hang tag (R.S. 47:490.32). LDVA also reports free parking at Louisiana airports for any length of time and 7 days free at the Port of New Orleans cruise terminal (Louisiana residents only since Act 86 of 2025) for veterans rated at least 50%, with a form certified by a Veterans Assistance Counselor. The statute for the general 50% disabled veteran plate was not located, so confirm the fee with OMV.
benefits.source_title: R.S. 47:490.32 Military honor license plate; Purple Heart disabled veteran (Acts 2019, No. 6); OMV Policy 14.00 Mobility Impaired License Plates (rev. 07/21/2026); LDVA State Benefits page

benefits.benefit: Free driver license or ID card for 50% or higher disabled veterans; 100% DAV and Veteran designations
benefits.details: You pay no fees, including handling and parish fees, for a new, renewed, duplicate, or amended driver license or special ID card if you were honorably discharged, have 'a service-related disability of at least fifty percent,' receive VA compensation for it, and are not a sex offender registrant. Bring your DD-214 and a VA statement of your rating to an OMV office. A 100% rating lets you add a '100% DAV' indicator under your photo. Any honorably discharged veteran can add a 'Veteran' marker with a DD-214; it is free only if you turn in your current license at the same time. LDVA notes fee waivers may not be honored at privatized Public Tag Agent offices.
benefits.source_title: R.S. 32:412.2 Exemption from fees; certain veterans (Acts 2007, No. 123; 2010, No. 402; 2012, No. 95); OMV Policy 2.01 (rev. 08/31/2021)

benefits.benefit: Free Disabled Veterans Hunting and Fishing License for 50% or higher (residents and nonresidents)
benefits.details: Veterans of the U.S. Armed Forces or Louisiana National Guard 'having a permanent service connected disability classification of fifty percent or more' get a free annual Disabled Veterans Hunting and Fishing License; the Louisiana Wildlife and Fisheries Foundation pays the $4 fee.
