The MVAA page says military disability retirement pay received as a pension or similar allowance for injury or sickness from active service is not included in taxable income. Michigan has an income tax; civilian pay from the military does not qualify as military pay.
benefits.source_title: Are military retirement benefits exempt from Michigan individual income tax? (Treasury)

benefits.benefit: State hiring veterans' preference
benefits.details: Under Civil Service Rule 3-8, a veteran (90 or more days of active duty, honorable discharge) gets 5 points added to a final passing exam score, and a disabled veteran (found eligible for VA or military disability compensation for a service-connected disability) gets 10 points. Where an agency screens by score instead, the add-on is 5 percent or 10 percent of the highest screening score. A spouse of a disabled veteran with a service-connected rating over 50 percent also gets 10. Preference is not a guarantee of a job, and you must register with Civil Service to receive it.
benefits.source_title: Civil Service Commission Rule 3-8: Veterans' Preference

benefits.benefit: Michigan Veterans Trust Fund emergency grants
benefits.details: Discretionary emergency grants for veterans facing an unforeseen, short-term financial hardship that a grant can resolve. Applicants are Michigan residents, honorably discharged, generally with 180 days of wartime service (a separate program covers peacetime veterans age 65 and older). Apply through your county MVTF committee or call 1-800-MICH-VET; denials can be appealed to the MVTF Board of Trustees. Not tied to a disability rating.
benefits.source_title: Michigan Veterans Trust Fund (MVAA)

benefits.benefit: Michigan Veteran Homes (state nursing care)
benefits.details: Three state veteran homes (Grand Rapids, Marquette, Chesterfield Township) provide skilled nursing care. Eligibility includes honorably discharged veterans eligible for VA health care or VA long-term nursing care financial assistance, and certain dependents; Michigan residency is not required. Apply by contacting a home directly or a Veteran Service Officer.
benefits.source_title: Michigan Veteran Homes - Eligibility

states.name: Minnesota
notes: The homestead market value exclusion (Minn. Stat. 273.13, subd. 34) needs a service-connected rating of 70 percent or more and an honorable discharge. At 70 to 99 percent, $150,000 of the home's market value is excluded. A 'total (100 percent) and permanent disability' excludes $300,000. The statute and the Revenue page do not mention TDIU, so a TDIU rating by itself is not clearly enough for the $300,000 tier; ask your county assessor.

This is a reduction in taxable value, not a full tax exemption. The home must be classified as your homestead and you must own and occupy it on December 31. The exclusion does not stack with the regular homestead market value exclusion.

Apply to your county assessor by December 31 of the first assessment year you want the exclusion (taxes payable the next year). Some county forms list earlier dates (for example December 15), so call the county before the end of November. Bring your DD-214 and VA rating documentation; a County Veterans Service Officer can help.
On a farm homestead, only the house, garage, and one surrounding acre count toward the exclusion.

If a veteran with the $300,000 exclusion dies, it carries over to the surviving spouse while the spouse holds title and lives in the home; it ends on remarriage or if the property is disposed of. A spouse receiving Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) can also qualify under the Revenue page. A VA-approved primary family caregiver can claim it if the veteran owns no Minnesota homestead.

The vehicle registration exemption (Minn. Stat. 168.012, subd. 13) uses the definition of a veteran with a 'total service-connected disability': a 100 percent total and permanent rating shown by a VA (or military retirement board) document. It covers passenger automobiles, one-ton pickups, motorcycles, and recreational vehicles, up to two vehicles at a time. Personalized-plate fees and required special-plate donations are not waived.

Free hunting and fishing licenses require a 100 percent service-connected disability. The DNR page says 'proof of a 100% service-related disability'. It does not say whether a TDIU rating counts. A federal duck stamp is still required for waterfowl. The free permanent angling license is issued only at the DNR License Center in St. Paul.

The free state park vehicle permit is different: any level of service-connected disability qualifies (Minn. Stat. 85.053, subd. 10). Show a VA determination letter or other official validation each year.

VA disability compensation is not part of federal adjusted gross income, and Minnesota starts from federal AGI, so it is not taxed. No Minnesota page found says this in so many words. Military retirement pay is a full subtraction, but you cannot also claim the Credit for Past Military Service in the same year.

Minnesota state-job preference uses points on open exams: 10 points for a veteran and 15 for a disabled veteran (compensable service-connected disability). A disabled veteran gets the points only after passing the exam without them. Hiring under the newer applicant-pool system lists disabled veterans ahead of other applicants instead of using points.

The Minnesota GI Bill pays up to $5,000 per state fiscal year and $15,000 in a lifetime, and must be applied for through the state program. The Survivors and Dependents Education Program in Minn. Stat. 197.75 is for dependents of veterans who died from service; the 2026 amendments (Laws 2026 ch. 49) could not be read, so check the current text.

Minnesota Veterans Homes require an honorable discharge, Minnesota residency, and, under the statute, applicants must be 'without adequate means of support' unless the discretionary payment path in Minn. Stat. 198.03 applies.

benefits.benefit: Homestead market value exclusion, $150,000 (70 percent or more)
benefits.details: If you were honorably discharged and have a service-connected disability rating of 70 percent or more, $150,000 of your homestead's market value is excluded from taxation. You must own and occupy the home as your homestead on December 31. Apply to the county assessor by December 31 of the first assessment year you want it; the exclusion cannot be combined with the regular homestead market value exclusion. A 100 percent rating that is not clearly permanent and total falls into this tier.
benefits.source_title: Minn. Stat. 273.13, subd. 34 (Homestead of veteran with a disability); Minnesota Department of Revenue, Market Value Exclusion for Veterans with a Disability (updated Sept. 9, 2026)

benefits.benefit: Homestead market value exclusion, $300,000 (100 percent total and permanent)
benefits.details: Minnesota excludes $300,000 of your home's market value from property tax if you have a VA service-connected rating of 100 percent permanent and total, which the Department of Revenue says includes permanent Individual Unemployability (TDIU). If your rating is 70 percent or more but not total and permanent, the exclusion is $150,000. You need an honorable discharge and must own and live in the home. Apply to your county assessor by December 31 of the first assessment year you want it. This TDIU wording comes from a 2018 Department of Revenue fact sheet, so confirm with your assessor.
benefits.source_title: Disabled Veterans' Homestead Property Tax Exclusion (Fact Sheet 11), Minnesota Department of Revenue

benefits.benefit: Homestead exclusion for surviving spouses and primary family caregivers
benefits.details: If a veteran who qualified for the $300,000 exclusion dies, it carries over to the surviving spouse, who must hold title and live in the home; it ends on remarriage or when the property is disposed of. The Revenue page also lists a surviving spouse who receives DIC, and says the veteran's disability status is not a factor in that case. A primary family caregiver approved by the VA may qualify if the veteran owns no Minnesota homestead. Apply to the county assessor by December 31. The amount for a DIC spouse and the caregiver tiers should be confirmed with the assessor.
benefits.source_title: Minnesota Department of Revenue, Market Value Exclusion for Veterans with a Disability; Minn. Stat. 273.13, subd. 34(c)-(e)

benefits.benefit: Registration tax, plate and filing fee exemption for veterans with a total service-connected disability
benefits.details: A veteran with a 100 percent total and permanent service-connected disability rating shown by VA documentation is exempt from registration tax, administrative fees, filing fees and surcharges, and plate and validation sticker fees on a passenger automobile, one-ton pickup, motorcycle, or recreational vehicle. The exemption applies to no more than two vehicles at a time, and to vehicles jointly registered with a spouse or domestic partner. Personalized-plate fees and required special-plate donations are not waived. The Driver and Vehicle Services application procedure and disabled-veteran parking privileges could not be confirmed.
benefits.source_title: Minn. Stat. 168.012, subd. 13 (Disabled veterans); Minn. Stat. 171.01, subd. 51 (definition)

benefits.benefit: Free small game, deer, and permanent angling licenses (100 percent disabled)
benefits.details: Resident veterans with a 100 percent service-connected disability can get a free small game license, one free deer license a year (firearms, archery, or muzzleloader), and a free permanent angling license with no trout stamp. A permanent card lets you get the small game and deer licenses free each year. The permanent angling license is issued only by the DNR License Center in St. Paul. Federal duck stamps are still required. The DNR does not state whether TDIU counts.
benefits.source_title: Minnesota DNR, Military benefits (Resident Veterans); Minn. Stat. 97A.441, subds. 5, 6, 6a

benefits.benefit: Free annual state park vehicle permit (any service-connected disability)
benefits.details: The DNR issues an annual state park vehicle permit at no charge to any veteran with any level of service-connected disability (Minn. Stat. 85.053, subd. 10). Show a veteran award letter, VA healthcare ID card, DOD privilege card, or a Disabled Vet license plate to park staff. The statute says you must present a yearly federal determination letter or other official validation. Purple Heart recipients and active military also get free permits under subd. 8.
benefits.source_title: Minn. Stat. 85.053, subds. 8 and 10; Minnesota DNR, Military benefits

benefits.benefit: Minnesota GI Bill (education and training grant)
benefits.details: Veterans who served honorably in any branch at any time, and non-veterans with 5 or more cumulative years of honorable Minnesota National Guard or reserve service (some on or after Sept. 11, 2001), can receive up to $5,000 per state fiscal year and $15,000 in a lifetime for college, on-the-job training or apprenticeship, or licensing and certification. You must be a Minnesota resident, enrolled, making satisfactory progress, and have filed the FAFSA. Surviving spouses and children of a service member who died from service, and spouses and children of a service member with a total and permanent service-connected disability, are also covered if eligible for federal chapter 33 or 35 benefits. Apply through the state MN GI Bill program run by MDVA.
benefits.source_title: Minn. Stat. 197.791 (Minnesota GI Bill); MDVA MN GI Bill page (not readable by our tools)

benefits.benefit: Survivors and Dependents Education Program (tuition waiver and stipend)
benefits.details: Children and surviving spouses of a deceased veteran who meet the statute's definitions are admitted free of tuition to Minnesota public institutions until a bachelor's degree, and an educational stipend of $750 a year is paid to each eligible child and spouse. The statute was amended in 2025 and 2026 (Laws 2026 ch. 49), and the current definition of the veteran's death or disability that qualifies could not be read. Confirm eligibility with MDVA before relying on this.
benefits.source_title: Minn. Stat. 197.75 (Survivors and dependents education)

benefits.benefit: Military retirement pay subtraction from state income tax
benefits.details: Minnesota taxes income, but federally taxable pension or retirement pay from the federal government for military service is a subtraction, with no dollar cap in the statute (Minn. Stat. 290.0132, subd. 21). The subtraction applies to people who do not claim the Credit for Past Military Service. Claim it on Schedule M1M. VA disability compensation is not in federal adjusted gross income, so it is not taxed; no Minnesota page found states this directly.
benefits.source_title: Minn. Stat. 290.0132, subd. 21 (Military service pension; retirement pay)

benefits.benefit: Credit for Past Military Service (state income tax credit)
benefits.details: A person who has served at least 20 years, has a 100 percent service-connected disability rating, or is eligible for certain military retirement pay, and who separated before the end of the tax year, can claim a credit of $750, reduced by 10 percent of federal adjusted gross income above $30,000. You cannot take this credit and the military retirement subtraction together. Claim it on the Minnesota income tax return.
benefits.source_title: Minn. Stat. 290.0677, subds. 1a and 2 (Credit for past military service)

benefits.benefit: State job veterans preference (points and applicant-pool ranking)
benefits.details: On open civil service exams, a veteran who passes gets 10 points, and a disabled veteran with a compensable service-connected disability gets 15 points; on promotional exams a disabled veteran with a permanent rating of 50 percent or more gets 5 points for a first promotion (Minn. Stat. 197.455). In the state's applicant-pool system (Minn. Stat. 43A.11), disabled veterans are listed ahead of all other applicants, then other veterans, and the top five recently separated veterans must get an interview. A surviving spouse, or the spouse of a disabled veteran who cannot qualify, may use the preference. Claim it when you apply.
benefits.source_title: Minn. Stat. 197.455 (Veterans preference in civil service); Minn. Stat. 43A.11

benefits.benefit: Minnesota Veterans Homes
benefits.details: Minnesota runs state veterans homes for honorably discharged veterans who are Minnesota residents (statute: served in a Minnesota regiment or credited to Minnesota). Spouses and surviving spouses must be at least 55. Applicants must be without adequate means of support unless the discretionary payment path in Minn. Stat. 198.03 applies, and each home has its own application and waiting list. MDVA says residents must need skilled nursing care at some homes; confirm with the specific home.
benefits.source_title: Minn. Stat. 198.022 (Eligibility for admission); MDVA Veterans Homes admissions (page not readable by our tools)

states.name: Mississippi
notes: The Mississippi homestead exemption for veterans is for an honorably discharged veteran with a 'service-connected, total disability.' The statute (Miss. Code 27-33-67(2)(a)) does not say 'permanent,' and it does not list TDIU. The Department of Revenue rule asks for proof such as the Veteran's Consent of Release (Form 72-042). Whether a TDIU-only rating (100% pay level, not a 100% schedular rating) is accepted should be confirmed with your county Tax Assessor before you rely on it.

Apply for the homestead exemption in person at the county Tax Assessor's office, only between January 1 and April 1. You must own the home and live in it as your primary residence on January 1. Ownership must be on record before January 1, and the deed filed with the Chancery Clerk before January 7. Missing the April 1 date means no exemption for that year.

You can lose the homestead exemption, retroactively, if you or your spouse did not file or pay Mississippi income tax on time, filed as a nonresident, or did not properly register your vehicles. The Department of Revenue says you may have to repay the exemption. Change of VA benefit status, marriage, divorce, death, or a deed change can force you to re-apply.

A surviving spouse keeps the total homestead exemption only while unremarried. Department of Revenue rule 3.03 says that from January 1, 2026, the unremarried surviving spouse of a person who qualifies for the total-disability exemption also qualifies. Bills in 2025 and 2026 to widen surviving-spouse rules (HB 714, SB 2808, SB 3120) died in committee.

The state's $1 disabled veteran plate has TWO routes: a rating of 100% permanent, or at least 70% NONPERMANENT service-connected disability (Miss. Code 27-19-53, as amended effective July 1, 2025). A 70% nonpermanent holder must show an updated VA benefits letter at each renewal. Older MSVA pages that say only '100% permanent or TDIU permanent' are out of date.

The plate is $1 each for up to 2 passenger vehicles or pickup trucks plus 1 motorcycle, and those vehicles are exempt from ad valorem and privilege taxes. A third vehicle pays regular fees and taxes. Proof of ownership of each vehicle is required. The privilege exemption does not cover commercial vehicles; the statute says it applies only to passenger vehicles, pickups and motorcycles.

The hunting and fishing exemption needs a VA letter stating 100% service-connected disability. You are not required to buy a license, but you must carry proof of age, residency and disability status while hunting or fishing. MDWFP also sells an optional 'Disabled Exempt' card (fee listed as $5.79 on the form revised 7/2024) if you want a card instead of carrying papers.

Mississippi has NO tuition waiver for veterans with a service-connected disability or for their spouses and children. Bills to create one (HB 1226, SB 2058, SB 2444 in 2025) died in committee. The only veteran tuition rule is that nonresident veterans and GI Bill-eligible people pay in-state tuition (Miss. Code 37-103-25). The only dependent scholarship is for children of POW/MIA service members (37-108-1).

State employment preference is a list-order system. The State Personnel Board defines a 'disabled veteran' as a veteran certified by the VA within the last 90 days as having a service-connected rating of at least 30%, or a Purple Heart recipient. You must submit current VA proof for disabled veteran status. The sources I found show points (4 for veterans, 8 for disabled veterans) only in the reduction-in-force retention formula.

Mississippi has a state income tax (4.4% on taxable income over $10,000 per the Department of Revenue FAQ; the 2025 return instructions show scheduled reductions through 2030). But VA payments are not taxed, and retirement income from federal, state and private systems, which includes military retirement, is exempt in total per the 2025 return instructions. Separation pay and early plan distributions are not exempt.

State park and state lake discounts do not need a disability rating: the 15% park camping and lodging discount covers all veterans, and state lake 'exempt' permits are for ages 62+, 100% disabled, active service members or military veterans. Park proof of 100% disability is a VA letter stating '100% Service Connected Disability.'

A 2026 bill (HB 420, signed March 20, 2026, effective July 1, 2026) adds a total homestead exemption for honorably discharged veterans age 85 or older, starting with exemptions claimed in 2027, and extends it to unremarried surviving spouses. This is separate from the service-connected disability exemption.

benefits.benefit: Homestead exemption - total (service-connected total disability)
benefits.details: Honorably discharged veterans with a service-connected, total disability, and their unremarried surviving spouses, are exempt from all ad valorem (property) tax on their homestead (Tier 3 of the state homestead system). You must own and occupy the home as your primary residence on January 1, and apply in person at the county Tax Assessor's office between January 1 and April 1; once allowed, you generally do not re-file each year unless something changes. Proof is Department of Revenue-approved VA documentation, for example the Veteran's Consent of Release (Form 72-042). Special assessments and fees that are not ad valorem tax may still be due; confirm with your Tax Assessor.
benefits.source_title: Homestead Exemption - Mississippi Department of Revenue

benefits.benefit: Homestead exemption - TDIU or non-100% schedular rating (unclear)
benefits.details: The statute and rule say 'service-connected, total disability' and do not name TDIU or 'permanent and total.' A 2025 Attorney General opinion summary says civilian employability is irrelevant and only documentation of a service-connected total disability and honorable discharge is needed, but I could only find that opinion through a non-official summary. Ask your county Tax Assessor, in writing, whether a TDIU rating is accepted before relying on it.
benefits.source_title: 35 Miss. Admin. Code Part VI, Rule 3.03 (homestead applicants, total disability proof) - Secretary of State

benefits.benefit: Homestead exemption - veteran age 90+ (85+ from 2027)
benefits.details: An honorably discharged veteran who is at least 90 on January 1 gets a full ad valorem exemption on the homestead, and so does the unremarried surviving spouse. HB 420 (2026, effective July 1, 2026) lowers the age to 85 for exemptions claimed in 2027 and later. Documents are a birth certificate or state ID and the DD-214; apply at the county Tax Assessor between January 1 and April 1.
benefits.source_title: HB 420 (As Sent to Governor), 2026 Regular Session, amending Miss. Code 27-33-75

benefits.benefit: Disabled American Veteran license plates - $1 each
benefits.details: A Mississippi resident rated 100% permanent, OR at least 70% nonpermanent, service-connected can buy up to 2 passenger vehicle or pickup plates and 1 motorcycle plate per year for $1 each (Miss. Code 27-19-53). A 100% permanent rating may have the plate labeled '100% Disabled Veteran' or 'Disabled Veteran'; a 70% nonpermanent holder must show an updated VA benefits letter every renewal. Apply at the county Tax Collector with VA verification and proof of ownership; the unremarried surviving spouse can keep the plates.
benefits.source_title: SB 2052 (As Sent to Governor), 2025 Regular Session, amending Miss. Code 27-19-53

benefits.benefit: Vehicle ad valorem and privilege tax exemption (2 vehicles + 1 motorcycle)
benefits.details: Vehicles and the motorcycle that carry the $1 disabled veteran plates are exempt from all ad valorem and privilege taxes. The Department of Revenue says a qualified veteran may register up to 2 vehicles and 1 motorcycle this way; more vehicles pay regular fees and taxes. Same threshold as the plates: 100% permanent or at least 70% nonpermanent.
benefits.source_title: Motor Vehicle Frequently Asked Questions - Mississippi Department of Revenue

benefits.benefit: Hunting and fishing license exemption
benefits.details: Residents with a total service-connected disability from the VA do not have to buy a hunting or fishing license (Miss. Code 49-7-5 and 49-7-9). You must carry proof of age, residency and disability status (a VA letter stating 100% service connected) while hunting or fishing. MDWFP also issues an optional Disabled Exempt card for a small fee; WMA user permits are waived for exempt users.
benefits.source_title: Fishing License Requirements (Exemptions) - Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries, and Parks

benefits.benefit: Optional MDWFP Disabled Exempt hunting/fishing card
benefits.details: Instead of carrying papers, a 100% service-connected veteran can apply for a Disabled Exempt hunting/fishing license by mailing the MDWFP application, a current VA letter stating 100% service connected, and proof of Mississippi residency. The form revised 7/2024 lists the fee as $5.79. Veterans rated below 100% do not qualify for this exemption.
benefits.source_title: Application for Resident Exempt Hunting / Fishing License (Revised 7/2024)

benefits.benefit: State park 15% camping and lodging discount
benefits.details: Mississippi State Parks give a 15% discount off the camping and lodging rate to ages 62+, disabled, veterans and active service members (excluding holidays, special events and Buccaneer State Park Gulf View sites). Proof of status is required at check-in; for disability, a VA letter stating '100% Service Connected Disability.' This is a discount, not a free pass.
benefits.source_title: State Park Fees - Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries, and Parks

benefits.benefit: State fishing lake 'exempt' permit rates
benefits.details: State fishing lakes run by MDWFP charge reduced 'exempt' prices (for example annual boat launch/fishing $100 vs $125, annual fishing permit $35 vs $55, one-day camping $22 vs $25) for persons 62+, 100% disabled, active service members or military veterans. Veterans can show military veteran status; 100% disabled users use a VA letter stating 100% service connected.
benefits.source_title: State Fishing Lake Permit Fees - Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries, and Parks

benefits.benefit: In-state tuition for nonresident veterans and GI Bill users
benefits.details: A veteran as defined in Title 38, or a person entitled to Title 38 education benefits, is authorized in-state tuition at Mississippi public colleges (Miss. Code 37-103-25). There is no state tuition waiver for service-connected disabled veterans or their dependents; the only dependent scholarship is for children of POW/MIA service members. Contact the school's veterans office and the Mississippi VA State Approving Agency at (601) 576-4867.
benefits.source_title: State Benefits for Veterans - Mississippi VA

benefits.benefit: State income tax: VA disability pay and military retirement
benefits.details: Mississippi has a state income tax, but it does not tax VA payments, and retirement income from federal, state and private retirement systems is exempt in total per the Department of Revenue's 2025 return instructions. Separation pay and early distributions are not exempt. National Guard and Reserve pay: the first $15,000 is excluded; combat-zone pay is exempt.
benefits.source_title: Individual Income Tax Frequently Asked Questions - Mississippi Department of Revenue

benefits.benefit: State employment preference (disabled veteran listing and RIF points)
benefits.details: When state agencies get a list of eligible applicants, disabled veterans are listed before veterans at the top of the list. A disabled veteran is one certified by the VA within the last 90 days at 30% or more service connected, or a Purple Heart recipient (Miss. Code 25-9-301). In state layoffs, veterans get 4 points and disabled veterans 8 points toward the retention score. Submit VA proof when you apply on the State Personnel Board site.
benefits.source_title: Information for Veterans - Mississippi State Personnel Board

benefits.benefit: Concealed carry permit fee exemption
benefits.details: Veterans with any service-connected disability are exempt from concealed weapon permit fees and renewal fees, if resident of Mississippi for 12 months immediately before applying (waivers for certain out-of-state permit holders, stationed military and retired law enforcement). Miss. Code 45-9-101. Details of the application are handled by the Department of Public Safety; this row cites the MSVA summary.
benefits.source_title: State Benefits for Veterans - Mississippi VA

benefits.benefit: Veterans' Home Purchase Board home loan
benefits.details: The Veterans' Home Purchase Board makes below-market fixed-rate home loans to eligible veterans (listed rates effective March 1, 2026: 4.50% for 0-15 years and 5.00% for 16-30 years, maximum loan $500,000). You need a VA Certificate of Eligibility, a discharge other than dishonorable, and Mississippi residency before service or for 2 consecutive years before applying. Disability rating is not an eligibility requirement. A surviving spouse may qualify if the veteran died from service-connected causes.
benefits.source_title: VHPB Program Eligibility - Veterans' Home Purchase Board of Mississippi

states.name: Missouri
notes: The Property Tax Credit is a refund claimed on your state income tax return (MO-PTS) or on Form MO-PTC, not a lower local tax bill. It is capped at $1,550 of tax paid for tax year 2026 (up from $1,100) and is phased out by income, so a high-income household may get little or nothing.

The credit statute reads 'one hundred percent disabled as a result of such service.' It does not mention TDIU or P&T, and DOR forms ask for a VA letter that the disability is 100% from military service. Ask DOR whether a TDIU-only rating counts.

For a veteran who is 100% service-connected, VA payments are not counted as income for the credit. A veteran who is 100% disabled but not from service must count VA payments as income. Attach the VA letter.

Missouri has no general disabled veteran property tax exemption. Only a former POW with a total service-connected disability gets a full homestead exemption (constitution). Several 2026 bills (such as SB 1535, HB 2362, SJR 77 and SJR 94) would expand relief, but none was found enacted, so do not count on them.

The 'free' Disabled Veteran plates have a threshold that is unclear: DOR's page asks for a VA letter of service-connected disability, but the statute refers to total service-connected compensation or a VA automobile grant. Registration is free for one set only, and the plates do not give disabled parking unless the wheelchair symbol is added.
The no-permit hunting and fishing exemption starts at 60%. It does not cover deer, turkey, bear, elk, trapping, trout, or migratory birds, and you must carry a VA statement of eligibility.

The Returning Heroes tuition cap is for combat veterans (proof of combat service), has time limits (10 years undergraduate, 20 years graduate) and a 2.5 GPA. It is not tied to a disability rating, and it covers the veteran, not dependents.
Dependent tuition help (Wartime Veteran's Survivor Grant) is narrow: post-9/11, combat-related death or 80% combat disability, limited to 25 new grants a year.
Military retirement is fully subtractable for tax years 2021 and later; the older 2016 phase-in does not apply. Survivor Benefit Plan annuities are not treated the same way.
The state job points table is on an application form dated 08-17, while the statute was rewritten in 2018. Treat the 5/10 point figures as unconfirmed.
Free disabled parking placards depend on a permanent disability, not a VA percentage; the 'VETERAN' marking on a driver license costs nothing extra but normal license fees apply.

benefits.benefit: Property Tax Credit (circuit breaker)
benefits.details: A refundable state income tax credit (not a bill reduction) for a veteran who 'became one hundred percent disabled as a result of such service.' For tax year 2026 and later the credit can be based on up to $1,550 of property tax paid on an owned home ($1,055 of rent-equivalent for renters); the 2025 caps were $1,100 and $750. Income must be at or below $42,200 (single, owned and occupied all year) or $48,000 (married, owned and occupied all year) for 2026, and VA benefits do not count as income for a veteran who is 100% service-connected (attach a VA letter). File Form MO-PTS with your MO-1040, or Form MO-PTC if you do not file an income tax return, with the Department of Revenue; the 2025 claim was due April 15, 2026 and can be filed up to 3 years late. The law does not mention TDIU or P&T status, so confirm with DOR whether a TDIU-only veteran qualifies.
benefits.source_title: RSMo 135.010 and 135.025/135.030 (Property Tax Credit); DOR Form MO-PTC instructions

benefits.benefit: Former POW homestead property tax exemption
benefits.details: The Missouri Constitution exempts from all property tax the homestead of a Missouri citizen who is a former prisoner of war and has a total service-connected disability. You must own and live in the home as your primary residence, and give your county assessor a VA letter showing total service-connected disability and a DD-214 or other proof of POW status. It is not run by the Department of Revenue; apply at the county assessor's office. This does not help non-POW veterans.
benefits.source_title: Missouri Constitution Art. X, Sec. 6; State Tax Commission FAQ: Are Veterans or Former POWs Exempt from Property Tax

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran license plates (first set free)
benefits.details: Missouri residents honorably discharged with a service-connected disability can get one free set of Disabled Veteran plates, with no plate, transfer, processing or replacement fees (additional sets pay normal fees). Apply with Form 4601 and a VA letter (under 1 year old, from the VA itself, not a clinic) showing the disability is service-connected. DOR's page does not state a minimum percentage, but the statute (RSMo 301.071) refers to total service-connected compensation or eligibility for a VA automobile grant, so confirm your rating qualifies before applying. These plates do not allow disabled parking unless the wheelchair symbol is added with a physician statement (DOR-1776).
benefits.source_title: Disabled Veteran (DV) License Plates (DOR); RSMo 301.071, 301.072

benefits.benefit: Permanent disabled parking placard (free, VA letter accepted)
benefits.details: A permanent disabled parking placard is free, and a veteran can submit a VA letter verifying a permanent disability instead of a physician statement at first application. Disabled veterans do not need to submit another statement to renew. This turns on a permanent disability that limits mobility, not a VA percentage. Apply through the Department of Revenue.
benefits.source_title: Permanent Disabled Placard (Missouri DOR)

benefits.benefit: Military Award Placard (free parking at meters and public colleges)
benefits.details: Veterans awarded certain medals (including Purple Heart, Bronze Star, Silver Star, Distinguished Service Cross, Medal of Honor, and former POW) can get a removable placard for free parking in metered spaces (if local authorities approve) and in public college and university lots (except special events), for vehicles up to 6,000 pounds. Apply with Form 4601 plus the specialty plate or proof of the medal (DD-214 or similar). No disability rating is required.
benefits.source_title: Military Reference Guide (DOR, revised January 2025)

benefits.benefit: Hunting and fishing permit exemption (60% or POW)
benefits.details: An honorably discharged veteran with a service-related disability of 60% or more (or a former POW) may fish and hunt without a permit, except for deer, turkey, bear and elk, and may not trap. Trout permits or trout park tags, migratory bird permits and the federal duck stamp are still required. Carry a certified statement of eligibility from the VA. Nonresident veterans who meet the same test can buy resident-priced permits where a permit is required. A 2026 bill (HB 2202) to make permits free for 100% veterans was not shown as passed.
benefits.source_title: Permit Exemptions (Missouri Department of Conservation); Veteran Benefits (MDC)

benefits.benefit: State park camping discount
benefits.details: Missouri State Parks gives veterans, retired and active military, and people with disabilities a $2 per night camping discount, year-round. Ask for it at payment and show military ID (DD-214, DD-1173, CAC) or, for the disability discount, a state disabled placard or plate, an America the Beautiful Access Pass, or a VA or SSA letter. No percentage-based discount for disabled veterans was found.
benefits.source_title: Camping Rates (Missouri State Parks); Military Benefits and Services

benefits.benefit: Missouri Returning Heroes' Education Act (tuition cap)
benefits.details: Combat veterans honorably discharged and eligible to vote in Missouri (or Missouri residents) pay no more than $50 per credit hour at public colleges that receive state funds, for certificate, associate or bachelor's programs, if they keep a 2.5 GPA. Graduate programs (not professional degrees like law or medicine) are limited to 30% of tuition and fees. The eligibility window is 10 years from last discharge for undergraduate and 20 years for graduate. No disability rating is needed, but you must show combat service (combat theater, combat medal, or imminent-danger pay). Ask the school's veterans office.
benefits.source_title: RSMo 173.900 Missouri Returning Heroes' Education Act; DHEWD

benefits.benefit: Wartime Veteran's Survivor Grant (dependents)
benefits.details: For spouses and children (under 25) of post-9/11 service members who died or were injured in combat, or who became 80% disabled from combat injuries, and who were Missouri residents when entering service. The grant covers up to Mizzou-level tuition, up to $2,000 per semester room and board, and up to $500 per semester for books, for a first bachelor's degree, with a 2.5 GPA. Only up to 25 new grants are awarded per year within appropriations, and the Missouri Veterans Commission must certify the survivor.
benefits.source_title: RSMo 173.234 (Veteran's Survivors Grant)

benefits.benefit: Military retirement pay exempt from state income tax
benefits.details: Missouri has an income tax, but 100% of military retirement benefits reported on federal Form 1040 line 5b can be subtracted from federal AGI (Form MO-A, Part 1, Line 10), for tax years 2021 and later. A survivor annuity (SBP) does not qualify for this subtraction but may qualify for the public pension exemption. No disability rating is needed.
benefits.source_title: Pension FAQs (Missouri DOR); Military Reference Guide

benefits.benefit: VA disability compensation and state income tax
benefits.details: Missouri starts from federal adjusted gross income, and VA disability compensation is not included in federal AGI, so it is not taxed by the state. I did not find a DOR page that states this in one sentence; the DOR guide only addresses VA payments for the property tax credit. Confirm with DOR before relying on it.
benefits.source_title: Military Reference Guide (DOR, January 2025)

benefits.benefit: State employment veterans' preference
benefits.details: The State of Missouri application lists veterans' preference of 5 or 10 points (not cumulative) for open competitive recruitment only: 5 points for qualifying active duty or reserve service, and 10 points for a veteran who receives compensation for a service-related disability (attach a VA statement). RSMo 36.220 (amended 2018) says only that veterans, disabled veterans and spouses get preference and win ties when other factors are equal. The point table is on a form dated 08-17, so the current rule needs to be confirmed with the Office of Administration, Division of Personnel.
benefits.source_title: State of Missouri Application for Employment (veterans' preference section); RSMo 36.220

benefits.benefit: Missouri Veterans Homes
benefits.details: Seven state veterans homes offer 24-hour skilled nursing care. Applicants must meet VA veteran status, have lived in Missouri for 180 consecutive days before applying, have a physician document the need for 24-hour skilled nursing, and not be on a sex offender registry or have certain felony convictions. The 2026 monthly rate is $2,773. One waitlist application covers all homes; apply through the Missouri Veterans Commission.
benefits.source_title: Veterans Homes Program Admissions (Missouri Veterans Commission)

states.name: Montana

agency.name: Montana Veterans Affairs Division (Department of Military Affairs)

notes: Property tax: Montana's disabled veteran program (MDV) is a reduced property tax RATE (100%, 80%, 70% or 50% reduction by income), not a flat exemption. Income limits apply every year, and the benefit is lost if your income passes the top tier.

Property tax: you apply to a local Department of Revenue field office (not the county assessor) by April 15. A late application is considered for the following year, so file anyway. Include your current VA 100% letter.

Property tax: the rating must be 100% disabled or 'paid at the 100% disabled rate' (15-6-311). A veteran paid at the 100% rate through TDIU appears to fit that wording, but no Revenue page says so in plain words. Ask DOR before relying on it.

Property tax: the income test uses federal adjusted gross income, and your spouse's income counts even if the spouse is not on the deed. The home must be your primary residence, lived in at least seven months of the year. On farm or timber land only the one-acre home site qualifies.

Property tax, surviving spouses: only an UNMARRIED surviving spouse qualifies, with a lower income table (2027 top limit $56,276), and needs a VA letter showing the veteran was rated or paid at 100% at death, died on active duty, or died of a service-connected disability.

Vehicles: the registration fee waiver (61-3-460) covers TWO non-commercial vehicles for a veteran currently rated 100% or paid at the 100% rate, and it also waives the fee for two sets of special veteran plates. It is a fee waiver; no source found grants parking privileges with a veteran plate. Parking needs a separate disability parking permit.
Vehicles: a veteran rated 50% or more who received the Purple Heart also gets the registration fee waiver, but must still pay the veterans' cemetery fee on plates.

Hunting and fishing: Montana has NO general free hunting or fishing license for 100% disabled veterans. The only veteran-specific item on the FWP page is half-price deer and antelope licenses for 'certain combat-connected injuries' (up to 50 per year). Many blogs claim free licenses; the official page does not.

State parks: there is no free entry for disabled veterans found. Resident veterans get 50% off overnight camping fees (not electrical fees). Residents already pay a parks fee with vehicle registration.

Education: the Montana University System has no tuition waiver based on disability rating. The Honorably Discharged Veteran Waiver is a last-dollar award, and only after your federal education benefits are used up or expired. Dependents of a disabled veteran have no waiver; the war orphans waiver is only for children of a parent killed or who died of a combat-related injury.

Income tax: Montana taxes military retirement pay like other income, but a partial exemption (the lesser of 50% of retirement pay or Montana wage/business income) applies for up to 5 consecutive years. The 2033 sunset was removed in 2025 (SB 93).

State jobs: disabled veterans get 10 percentage points on scored hiring, veterans get 5, and you cannot stack them. It applies to initial hiring only, and you must claim it and document it when you apply.

benefits.benefit: Montana Disabled Veteran (MDV) property tax reduction
benefits.details: Reduces the property tax rate on your primary residence by 100%, 80%, 70% or 50%, depending on income. For tax year 2027 a single applicant needs 2025 FAGI of $64,551 or less (100% reduction up to $49,654); married or head of household needs $74,482 or less (100% up to $59,584). You must be rated or paid at 100% for a service-connected disability, own the home, and live in it at least seven months a year. Apply with a VA 100% letter to your local Department of Revenue field office by April 15.
benefits.source_title: Montana Disabled Veteran Assistance Program (MDV), Dept. of Revenue; 15-6-311, MCA

benefits.benefit: MDV: unmarried surviving spouse
benefits.details: An unmarried surviving spouse of a veteran who was rated or paid at 100%, died on active duty, or died of a service-connected disability can get the same reduction on a primary residence, with a lower income table (2027: 100% up to $41,379, 50% tier up to $56,276). A VA letter is required. Apply to the Department of Revenue by April 15.
benefits.source_title: Montana Disabled Veteran Property Tax Relief Application (Form MDV), Part III and V

benefits.benefit: MDV: TDIU and non-permanent ratings
benefits.details: The statute and form say 100% disabled or 'paid at the 100% disabled rate'; the form says a temporary rating means DOR will periodically ask for an updated VA letter, so permanence is not required. Whether TDIU pay counts is not stated in plain words by DOR. Ask a Revenue field office at (406) 444-6900 before relying on it.
benefits.source_title: Montana Disabled Veteran Assistance Program (MDV); Form MDV Part III

benefits.benefit: Motor vehicle registration fee waiver
benefits.details: A veteran currently rated 100% disabled or paid at the 100% rate by the VA is exempt from all motor vehicle registration fees under chapter 3 for two motor vehicles not used commercially. A veteran rated 50% or more who has the Purple Heart also qualifies. Unremarried surviving spouses of eligible veterans qualify. VA documentation is required; the statute does not name the office, so ask your county MVD office.
benefits.source_title: 61-3-460, MCA (Waiver of fees for veterans)

benefits.benefit: Special veteran license plates, fee waived
benefits.details: The same statute waives the veterans' cemetery fee on two sets of special veteran plates for 100% disabled veterans (Purple Heart recipients at 50%+ still pay it). An eligible veteran can apply the waiver to other special plates under 61-3-458(4) if they meet that plate's own rules. No source found gives parking privileges with the plate; disability parking needs a separate permit.

benefits.benefit: Half-price deer and antelope licenses (combat disabled)
benefits.details: Veterans with 'certain combat-connected injuries' may get half-priced deer and antelope licenses; up to 50 licenses are issued each year. The FWP page does not state the rating or injury threshold, so call FWP Licensing at 406-444-2950 to confirm eligibility and application steps.
benefits.source_title: Disabled Hunting and Fishing Licenses, Montana FWP

benefits.benefit: Resident disability conservation license ($8)
benefits.details: Residents with a qualifying disability can buy general deer, general elk, fishing and upland game bird licenses at half cost with the $8 conservation license. The FWP page does not state a VA rating threshold or the certification needed, so a service-connected rating may not by itself qualify. Confirm with FWP Licensing.
benefits.source_title: Disabled Hunting and Fishing Licenses, Montana FWP

benefits.benefit: State park camping discount for veterans
benefits.details: Montana resident veterans get 50% off overnight camping fees at state parks (electrical fees excluded). Proof is a DD 214, VA ID, or a driver's license showing veteran status. There is no found free day-use entry for disabled veterans. A 2026 FWP fee proposal may change rates, so check current fees.
benefits.source_title: State Parks: Fees and General Information, Montana FWP

benefits.benefit: Honorably Discharged Veteran tuition waiver (MUS)
benefits.details: A last-dollar waiver up to in-state tuition at Montana University System campuses for resident undergraduate or graduate students with an honorable discharge (not General) who have used up or let expire their Title 38 or Title 10 education benefits. Apply by the third week of the first semester through the Office of the Commissioner of Higher Education portal. There is no disability-rating based waiver.
benefits.source_title: MUS Tuition Waivers; 20-25-421, MCA

benefits.benefit: Dependent tuition waiver (war orphans only)
benefits.details: The War Orphans Waiver covers undergraduate tuition (not fees) for children age 25 or younger of a Montana resident who was killed in action or died of a combat-related injury or disease. It does not cover children or spouses of living disabled veterans, including 100% P&T. Commissioner approval is required.
benefits.source_title: MUS Tuition Waivers (War Orphans Waiver)

benefits.benefit: Military retirement income partial exemption
benefits.details: Montana has an income tax. Military retirement pay is taxable, but retirees who were residents or became residents on or after June 30, 2023 can exempt the lesser of Montana wage-type income or 50% of retirement pay, for up to 5 consecutive years starting tax year 2024. The sunset was removed by SB 93 (2025). Claim it with Form WMRE.
benefits.source_title: Montana Income Tax Guide for Military Members; 15-30-2120, MCA

benefits.benefit: VA disability compensation and state income tax
benefits.details: Montana starts from federal adjusted gross income, and VA compensation is generally not in federal income. No Montana Revenue page found says this directly, so treat it as unconfirmed and ask the Department of Revenue.
benefits.source_title: Montana Income Tax Guide for Military Members and Their Families

benefits.benefit: State employment preference points
benefits.details: When a public employer scores applicants for an initial hire, a disabled veteran gets 10 percentage points added (veterans get 5, no stacking). Unscored hiring gives preference in order: disabled veteran first. Applicant must be a U.S. citizen meeting minimum qualifications and must claim preference when applying. Covers state, county and city hiring.

benefits.benefit: Montana Veterans' Homes
benefits.details: The state runs veterans homes in Columbia Falls, Butte and Glendive for skilled and intermediate nursing care. Admission eligibility and cost were not confirmed on the pages found; Columbia Falls is (406) 892-3256.
benefits.source_title: Montana Veterans' Home, Columbia Falls (DPHHS)

states.name: Nebraska
notes: The big property tax break (Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-3506) is for a veteran with an honorable or general discharge who draws VA compensation for a 100% service-connected permanent disability, OR a total disability rating under 38 CFR 4.16 (TDIU). A veteran with a temporary 100% rating also qualifies, but must reapply every year with a VA certification. A 50% to 99% rating gets nothing from this exemption.

The exemption covers the full taxable value of the home. By statute the 'exempt amount' for this category is 'the taxable value of the homestead' (77-3501.01(3)), and the home-value reduction in 77-3506.03 does not apply to it. The income tables in 77-3507 and 77-3508 apply only to the other homestead categories, not to 77-3506.

You must own the home and live in it as a natural person from January 1 through August 15 of the year. The land is limited to one acre. File with the county assessor after February 1 and on or before June 30 (the county board may extend to July 20). Missing the deadline waives that year's exemption, with limited late-filing exceptions in 77-3514.01.
Permanent 100% and TDIU filers apply once; the exemption continues in later years with no new application. The temporary-100% category must reapply every year with VA certification.

A veteran who qualifies for the separate full exemption in 77-3526 to 77-3528 (paraplegic or multiple amputee whose home was substantially contributed to by VA) is carved out of the 77-3506 category. If that is you, ask the assessor which one applies.

A surviving spouse keeps the exemption while unmarried, or if remarried after reaching age 57. A spouse who remarries before age 57 loses it and must tell the county assessor within 30 days. Spouses of veterans who died of a service-connected disability, or who died on active duty, also qualify.

The Nebraska motor vehicle tax and fee exemption (new January 1, 2026) covers ONE vehicle and is open to any veteran with an honorable discharge who has a service-connected disability, even 0%. You must first be in the NDVA Military and Veterans' Registry and ask the county treasurer within 30 days after buying the vehicle, or before the last day of the renewal month. Plate fees, sales tax and wheel tax are still owed.

Disabled Veteran license plates need only 10% service-connected and no limit on number of vehicles, but they do NOT allow parking in handicapped spaces. For parking you need Disabled Veteran Handicap plates (medical provider certification) or a handicapped parking permit.

The free lifetime Game and Parks hunt/fish/fur permit and park entry permit require 50% or more service-connected (or 100% non-service-connected with a VA pension) and Nebraska residency. Rated 10% to 40% does not qualify for these two permits.

Waiver of Tuition is for DEPENDENTS (spouse or child), not the veteran. The veteran must be rated 100% permanently and totally disabled. A temporary total rating does not count; a TDIU rating counts only if permanent (80-411). It covers one community college credential and one bachelor's degree only, and no graduate school.

Nebraska excludes 100% of military retirement pay from state income tax starting tax year 2022, with no form needed. Nebraska starts from federal adjusted gross income, so VA disability compensation (not in federal AGI) should not be taxed, but no Nebraska page says so directly.

State job preference is a percentage added to a passing score: 5% for any qualifying veteran and 5% more for any service-connected disability, any percentage. Submit your DD-214 and a VA Summary of Benefits letter with each application.

benefits.benefit: Homestead exemption: 100% disabled veteran (full home value)
benefits.details: Exempts 100% of the taxable value of your home from property tax, with no income limit. You qualify with an honorable or general discharge and VA compensation for 100% service-connected permanent disability or a total rating under 38 CFR 4.16 (TDIU); a temporary 100% rating also qualifies but must be renewed yearly with VA certification. Apply with the county assessor after February 1 and by June 30 (Form 458); permanent and TDIU filers do not reapply.
benefits.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-3506 (Certain veterans; exemption; certain surviving spouses; application)

benefits.benefit: Homestead exemption: surviving spouse of qualifying veteran
benefits.details: An unremarried surviving spouse of a veteran who held the 100% permanent or TDIU status, or of any honorably or generally discharged veteran who died of a service-connected disability or on active duty, gets the same full exemption. A spouse who remarries after age 57 keeps it; one who remarries before 57 loses it and must notify the county assessor within 30 days. File with the county assessor after February 1 and by June 30.

benefits.benefit: Homestead exemption: veteran totally disabled, non-service-connected (income-based)
benefits.details: A veteran with honorable or general discharge who is totally disabled by a non-service-connected accident or illness may get a partial exemption that depends on household income and home value. Needs VA certification of total non-service-connected disability on the application. File with the county assessor after February 1 and by June 30.
benefits.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-3508 (Homesteads; exemptions; based on disability and income)

benefits.benefit: Motor vehicle tax and fee exemption (one vehicle)
benefits.details: Starting January 1, 2026, a disabled or blind veteran with an honorable discharge is exempt from the Nebraska motor vehicle tax and motor vehicle fee on ONE vehicle used for personal transportation. 'Disabled veteran' follows 5 U.S.C. 2108, so any service-connected disability counts (NDVA says even 0%), or receiving VA compensation or pension. Enroll in the NDVA Military and Veterans' Registry, then claim at the county treasurer within 30 days of purchase or before the last day of the registration expiration month; it renews automatically.
benefits.source_title: NDVA: Disabled/Blind Veteran Motor Vehicle Tax and Fee Exemption (Neb. Rev. Stat. 60-3,185)

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran license plates
benefits.details: Available to a veteran with honorable or general discharge who is at least 10% service-connected. Must be enrolled in the Nebraska Veterans' Registry and title the vehicle in your name. Standard alphanumeric plate has no fee beyond normal registration fees and taxes, there is no limit on the number of vehicles, and a message plate costs $40 a year. Order online or by mail to the DMV.
benefits.source_title: Nebraska DMV: Disabled Veteran Plates

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran Handicap plates and parking
benefits.details: Standard Disabled Veteran plates do not allow parking in handicapped spaces. For that you need Disabled Veteran Handicap plates, which require Registry enrollment and a medical provider's certification on the Application for Military Handicapped License Plates, or a handicapped parking permit. Apply to the DMV (message plates are not available on these).
benefits.source_title: Nebraska DMV: Disabled Veteran Plates

benefits.benefit: Free lifetime hunt/fish/fur permit
benefits.details: Nebraska resident disabled veterans rated 50% or more service-connected (or 100% non-service-connected receiving a VA pension) get a Disabled Veteran's Lifetime Annual Small Game Hunt/Fish/Fur Harvest Permit at no fee, and it includes all state stamps. Apply through Nebraska Game and Parks; NDVA's guide describes it as requiring a veterans service officer's involvement. Confirm current paperwork with Game and Parks.
benefits.source_title: NDVA Guide to Veterans' Benefits, April 2026 edition (p. 26)

benefits.benefit: Free lifetime state park entry permit
benefits.details: Nebraska resident disabled veterans rated 50% or more service-connected (or 100% non-service-connected with a VA pension) can get one perpetual Disabled Veteran's Lifetime Annual Park Entry Permit at no fee. An application form with a veterans service officer's signature is required; Game and Parks service centers can print the form. It covers park entry only, not camping or other fees.
benefits.source_title: NDVA Guide to Veterans' Benefits, April 2026 edition (p. 26)

benefits.benefit: Waiver of Tuition for spouse and children
benefits.details: The University of Nebraska, state colleges and community colleges waive all tuition and remaining fees (after federal grants and state scholarships) for a Nebraska-resident spouse, child or stepchild of a veteran rated permanently and totally disabled from service (a TDIU rating counts only if permanent), or who died of a service-connected disability. Children must be under 26 (extendable to 31 for post-18 active duty). Limited to one community college credential and one bachelor's degree; apply to NDVA before the term with the veteran's DD-214 and proof of relationship.
benefits.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 80-411 (Waiver of tuition and fees); NDVA Waiver of Tuition program page

benefits.benefit: Military retirement pay excluded from state income tax
benefits.details: For tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2022, all military retirees can exclude 100% of military retirement benefits from Nebraska taxable income, to the extent included in federal AGI. No election or form is needed. This applies to retirement pay, not to VA compensation.
benefits.source_title: Nebraska Department of Revenue: Military Retirement Benefits Exclusion (Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-2716)

benefits.benefit: VA disability compensation and state income tax
benefits.details: Nebraska individual income tax starts from federal adjusted gross income, and VA disability compensation is not included in federal AGI, so it should not be taxed by Nebraska. I could not find an official Nebraska page stating this in plain words, so confirm with the Department of Revenue before relying on it.
benefits.source_title: Nebraska Department of Revenue: Military Retirement Benefits Exclusion

benefits.benefit: State and local government hiring preference
benefits.details: Veterans with an honorable or general discharge get 5% added to a passing exam or numerical score for State of Nebraska and local government jobs, and a disabled veteran (any service-connected disability, any percentage per State Personnel) gets an additional 5%. Where no scoring is used, preference breaks ties among equally qualified candidates. Submit a DD-214 and, for the extra 5%, a VA Summary of Benefits letter with the application. Spouses of 100% permanent veterans qualify for 5%.
benefits.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-225 to 48-227 (Veterans preference); State Personnel Veterans Preference guide rev. 8/21/2025

benefits.benefit: Nebraska Veterans' Homes (Bellevue, Kearney, Norfolk, Scottsbluff)
benefits.details: Veterans with active-duty service and an honorable or general discharge can apply for admission to the state veterans' homes. Cost is on a sliding scale based on income and assets, and NDVA says veterans rated 70% to 100% service-connected may receive care at no cost once the rating is verified and their care level meets VA criteria. Apply through the home or NDVA.
benefits.source_title: NDVA: Veterans' Homes

states.name: Nevada
notes: Nevada's property tax relief is a deduction from assessed value, not a full exemption. Even at 100 percent it is the first $20,000 of assessed value (CPI-indexed, about $36,400 for 2026-27 per county assessor pages), worth roughly $1,300 a year in property tax. Real savings depend on your local tax rate.

The statute requires a 'permanent' service-connected disability (NRS 361.091 and 371.104). The assessor wants a VA letter or rating document showing the permanent percentage, plus an honorable discharge or DD-214. A rating that is not permanent may be turned down; ask the county assessor what document they accept.

Tier is set by your total combined percentage, capped at 100: 60-79, 80-99, or 100 percent. Below 60 percent there is no disabled veteran exemption, but you may still qualify for the smaller general veteran exemption if you served in a listed wartime or campaign period.

You cannot take both the disabled veteran and general veteran exemptions, and the exemption can be claimed in only one county. You can split it between your home's property tax and your vehicle governmental services tax, or donate part of it to the Veterans Home gift accounts.

The file-by date for real property is June 15 (July 5 if you bought the property between June 15 and June 30). Late or denied claims can go to the county board of equalization by January 15 of that fiscal year. File early, with the assessor of the county where you live.

Vehicle exemption: get an exemption number from the county assessor first and give it to the DMV at registration. It cannot be applied after the DMV transaction is finished, and the DMV exemption uses the same dollar amount as your property exemption.

Surviving spouses must have been married to and living with the veteran for the 5 years before death, must not have remarried, and the veteran must have been eligible. The statute lets you claim it as the spouse; line-of-duty death spouses are not given a separate property tax rule in the statute I read.

Disabled Veteran license plates require a 100 percent rating (or combined ratings reaching 100, or a permanent disability that qualifies for a disabled parking plate). A 60-99 percent veteran gets the tax exemption but not these plates. I found no statute waiving registration fees.
The reduced-fee $15 hunting and fishing license is for 50 percent or more service-connected only, plus honorable discharge. You must send a VA percentage letter; tags are not covered.

The state parks Disabled Veteran permit says 'permanent' service-connected disability, not a percentage. An older State Parks overview and some secondary sources describe different rules, so confirm with State Parks.

Nevada has no general disabled veteran tuition waiver. The statutory waiver is for Purple Heart recipients and their children, plus a discretionary graduate degree waiver. Nevada has no state income tax.

TDIU: the statutes do not mention TDIU. The exemption tier is based on the total percentage of permanent service-connected disability, so a veteran paid at the 100 percent rate through TDIU but rated, say, 70 percent schedular may be placed in the 60-79 tier by the assessor. Confirm with the county.

benefits.benefit: Disabled veteran property tax exemption
benefits.details: Nevada exempts part of the assessed value of property owned by a resident honorably discharged veteran with a permanent service-connected disability: the first $10,000 of assessed value at 60-79 percent, $15,000 at 80-99 percent, and $20,000 at 100 percent, with the dollar amounts raised each fiscal year by a CPI formula. County assessor pages for 2026-27 show roughly $18,200, $27,300 and $36,400 of assessed value. File an affidavit and proof with the county assessor where you live by June 15 (July 5 for property bought June 15 to June 30). Combined ratings count, up to 100 percent.
benefits.source_title: NRS 361.091 Exemption for veteran who has incurred service-connected disability and surviving spouse of such a veteran

benefits.benefit: Surviving spouse of disabled veteran: property tax exemption
benefits.details: The unremarried surviving spouse of a veteran with a permanent service-connected disability can claim the same tiered exemption. The spouse must file an affidavit that they were married to and living with the veteran for the 5 years before the veteran's death, that the veteran was eligible (or would have been if a Nevada resident), that they have not remarried, and that they are a Nevada resident. Apply with the county assessor by June 15. A surviving spouse who is also a veteran may also claim the general veteran exemption.
benefits.source_title: NRS 361.091, subsections 6 and 8

benefits.benefit: General veteran property tax exemption
benefits.details: Resident veterans with at least 90 continuous days of active duty during a listed wartime or campaign period, and an honorable discharge or certificate of satisfactory service, get the first $2,000 of assessed value exempt, CPI-indexed (about $3,640 for 2026-27 per the Douglas County assessor). A veteran who gets the disabled veteran exemption cannot also take this one. Apply with the county assessor by June 15; the exemption can be used in only one county.
benefits.source_title: NRS 361.090 Veterans exemptions

benefits.benefit: Disabled veteran vehicle governmental services tax exemption
benefits.details: The same permanent-disability tiers can be applied to the Governmental Services Tax (the main part of the vehicle registration cost): first $10,000 of determined valuation at 60-79 percent, $15,000 at 80-99 percent, and $20,000 at 100 percent. Get an exemption number from the county assessor (bring your DD-214 or discharge papers and VA proof of disability) and give it to the DMV at registration or renewal; it cannot be applied after the transaction is finalized. The same exemption amount cannot be used twice, so you split it between property tax and vehicles. A veteran may transfer it to a current spouse. A surviving spouse also qualifies.
benefits.source_title: NRS 371.104 Exemptions for veteran with a disability and surviving spouse

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran license plates (up to two sets)
benefits.details: A veteran who receives VA compensation for a qualifying service-connected disability can get DISABLED VETERAN plates with the access symbol, for up to two vehicles (private passenger vehicle, noncommercial truck or motor home). A qualifying disability is a 100 percent rating, combined ratings of at least 100 percent, or any rating that includes a permanent disability qualifying for a disabled parking plate under NRS 482.384. Apply in person at the DMV with VA or DoD proof. Normal registration fees and governmental services tax still apply; I found no statute waiving registration fees.
benefits.source_title: NRS 482.377 Disabled Veteran license plates; NRS 482.0962 Qualifying service-connected disability defined

benefits.benefit: Free parking for vehicles with Disabled Veteran plates
benefits.details: A vehicle displaying Disabled Veteran plates is exempt from any parking fees, including parking meters, charged by the State or any political subdivision or public body in Nevada (federal parking excluded). Eligibility follows the plate rules: a qualifying service-connected disability (100 percent or combined to 100, or a permanent disability that qualifies for a disabled parking plate).
benefits.source_title: NRS 482.377, subsection 5

benefits.benefit: Reduced-fee resident hunting and fishing license
benefits.details: A Nevada resident veteran with a VA service-connected rating of 50 percent or more and an honorable discharge or certificate of satisfactory service can get the annual specialty combination hunting and fishing license for $15 (plus nominal processing fee). Mail or submit the NDOW application with the VA Benefit Summary percentage letter, a Nevada ID, and a hunter education certificate if born after January 1, 1960. The license runs one year from purchase; tags and permits are separate.
benefits.source_title: NDOW Resident Disabled Veteran Specialty Combination Hunting and Fishing License application (March 2025); NRS 502.072 and 502.240

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran annual State Parks permit
benefits.details: A Nevada resident honorably discharged veteran with a permanent service-connected disability can get an annual permit for unlimited entrance, camping and boat launch use at all Nevada state parks for 12 months, for only a $30 administrative fee. It is a placard for one vehicle. Apply through Nevada State Parks (forms at reservenevada.com; by mail, email or online). Renewals are not offered, so you file a new application each year. State Parks' page does not state a minimum percentage, only permanent service-connected disability.
benefits.source_title: Nevada State Parks Annual Permits; NRS 407.065

benefits.benefit: Purple Heart veteran fee waiver at NSHE schools
benefits.details: The Board of Regents must waive registration, laboratory and other mandatory fees each semester for a veteran who was awarded the Purple Heart, down to the balance left after federal education benefits are credited. The student is treated as a Nevada resident for tuition. It covers any program at a Nevada System of Higher Education school. Submit the NSHE Purple Heart Fee Waiver form to your campus office. Disabled veterans without a Purple Heart do not get an automatic statutory waiver.
benefits.source_title: NRS 396.5443; NSHE Student Veterans page

benefits.benefit: Purple Heart veteran's child fee waiver at NSHE schools
benefits.details: A child of a Purple Heart veteran gets the same registration, laboratory and mandatory fee waiver if the veteran is (or was at death) a Nevada resident and the child graduated from a Nevada high school. It can be used until 10 years after the child turns 18 (or 10 years after enrolling, if enrolled before 18). The amount is reduced by any federal education benefits received. Apply through the campus using the NSHE Purple Heart Fee Waiver form.
benefits.source_title: NRS 396.5443, subsections 1(b) and 6

benefits.benefit: No state income tax on military retirement or VA compensation
benefits.details: Nevada does not impose a state income tax on individuals, so military retirement pay, VA disability compensation and other income are not taxed by the state, and there is no state return to file for wage or retirement income. The Department of Taxation page does not list military pay by name; it states the general rule only.
benefits.source_title: Nevada Department of Taxation, Income Tax in Nevada

benefits.benefit: State employment veterans preference and guaranteed interview
benefits.details: For classified state jobs, appointing authorities must give a preference to veterans, and must interview each qualified veteran with a service-connected disability (any rating, including 0 percent). At least 22 percent of those interviewed must be qualified veterans without a disability. Declare the preference at application and attach a DD-214 and a VA rating letter. Older statute text and secondary sites say 10 points; the current statute text I read gives a preference without stating points, so confirm the exact points.
benefits.source_title: NRS 284.260 and 284.265; NAC 284.325; State of Nevada Veteran Hiring Preference guide

benefits.benefit: Nevada State Veterans Homes
benefits.details: Nevada operates State Veterans Homes, including a 180-bed skilled nursing home in Boulder City serving eligible veterans, spouses and Gold Star parents, with Alzheimer's and dementia care. Eligibility is set by the home (not by a rating threshold here); contact the home for admission rules and cost. Veterans can also direct their property or vehicle tax exemption amount to the Veterans Home gift accounts.
benefits.source_title: Nevada Department of Veterans Services, State Veterans Homes

states.name: New Hampshire

agency.name: New Hampshire Department of Military Affairs and Veterans Services (Division of Veterans Services)

notes: New Hampshire property tax relief is a tax CREDIT that each city or town sets. The state sets a floor and a ceiling, but the town votes on the amount (RSA 72:27-a). Two veterans with the same rating can get different credits depending on the town. Ask your town assessor or selectmen what your town adopted.

Apply with your town assessor or selectmen on the state form (PA-29) by April 15 before the tax rate is set (RSA 72:33). It is a permanent application, so you file once and keep the credit each year as long as you stay in the same home. If you move, file a new one by December 1 after the move. A late filing is allowed only for 'accident, mistake, or misfortune' and only before the town's tax rate is approved.

The service-connected total disability credit (RSA 72:35) needs a VA certification that you are 'rated totally and permanently disabled from service connection.' The statute does not mention TDIU by name. The specially adapted housing exemption (RSA 72:36-a) does name 'total and permanent total ratings and unemployability.' If you have TDIU, ask your town whether it accepts your VA letter.

The optional service-connected credit under RSA 72:35 can be set by the town anywhere from $701 up to $5,000 (raised from $4,000 in 2025). The statute says it 'shall replace' the regular veterans' credits and is not added on top. The state veterans page still says $2,000, so it is out of date.

The regular veterans' credit (RSA 72:28) is only $50 unless the town votes more, and the town maximum rises from $750 to $1,000 on April 1, 2027 (2026 law, chapter 96). The standard credit also requires service in a listed wartime period or armed conflict, and the veteran must have lived in New Hampshire at least one year before April 1. Many post-1975 veterans qualify only if their town adopted the 'all veterans' credit (RSA 72:28-b).

The credits apply only to your principal home (your 'residential real estate'), plus attached land and buildings and manufactured housing used as your home. A surviving spouse keeps the credit only while unmarried (a spouse who later divorces regains status). Ownership in a revocable trust counts.

The free perpetual Fish and Game license is for veterans who are 'totally and permanently disabled' from a service-connected condition and live in New Hampshire (RSA 214:13). It costs a one-time $10. Veterans rated at least 80% but not 100% can buy a lifetime license at half price. A 10% to 70% rating gets no license discount.

State park day-use admission is free for any New Hampshire disabled veteran with any service-connected rating, shown by a disabled veteran plate or a VA letter (RSA 216-A:3-g, IV). You still pay for camping, ski lifts, tram rides, food, and other 'enterprise' activities. Metered parking is also not waived for these veterans unless your vehicle has the special plate described in paragraph VI.

The free disabled veteran plate, free registration, and free license fee all hinge on the VA rating of 'permanently and totally disabled' from service-connected disability. Only one vehicle gets the plate set. Plates with the accessibility symbol get free parking (RSA 265:73 as described by the state veterans page). A veteran who picks the standard veterans' plate instead gives up the free parking.

Free tuition for a child is at the University System of New Hampshire only, and only if the parent is rated 100% total and permanent, was living in New Hampshire when entering service or when rated, and is still a New Hampshire resident. The child must also file the FAFSA. The waiver runs through the semester the child turns 27 (RSA 187-A:20). There is no tuition waiver for the veteran under these laws; New Hampshire's other tuition waivers go to National Guard members and children of killed or missing service members.

New Hampshire has no tax on wages. The Interest and Dividends Tax ended for tax periods starting January 1, 2025. The state veterans page says the state does not tax military retirement pay, VA disability compensation, or DIC. No state income tax return is needed for these.

Senate Bill 448 (2026 chapter 252, effective August 31, 2026) changed many statutes to use the RSA 21:50 definition of 'veteran,' which now covers a general discharge under honorable conditions. Veterans who were previously turned away for a general discharge should ask again. A lifetime hunting and fishing license for veterans that appeared in early versions of the bill is not in the final text I read.

benefits.benefit: Service-connected total disability property tax credit
benefits.details: Veterans (or an unremarried surviving spouse) with a total and permanent service-connected disability, or a double amputee or paraplegic from service, get a $700 yearly credit on the home they live in. Towns may vote to raise it to as much as $5,000. File a permanent application with your town assessor or selectmen by April 15 with a VA certification that you are rated totally and permanently disabled. The statute does not name TDIU, so confirm with your town if you have TDIU.
benefits.source_title: RSA 72:35 Tax Credit for Service-Connected Total Disability

benefits.benefit: Specially adapted housing full property tax exemption
benefits.details: A veteran who owns a home adapted with a VA Specially Adapted Housing or Special Home Adaptation grant (or bought with proceeds from selling one) is 'exempt from all taxation on said homestead.' The veteran must be 100% permanently and totally disabled per 38 C.F.R. 3.340 (the statute names 'unemployability'), a double amputee or paraplegic, or blind in both eyes at 5/200 or worse, from service. A surviving spouse is also covered. Apply with the town assessor by April 15 with proof of the service-connected disability.
benefits.source_title: RSA 72:36-a Certain Disabled Veterans

benefits.benefit: Standard and optional veterans' tax credit
benefits.details: A resident veteran with at least 90 days of active service in a listed war or armed conflict (or a spouse or surviving spouse) gets a $50 yearly credit on the home. Towns may vote to raise it from $51 up to $750, rising to $1,000 on April 1, 2027. A veteran discharged because of a service-connected disability also qualifies, and so does the surviving spouse of a service-connected death. This is not tied to a disability rating. Apply with the town by April 15.
benefits.source_title: RSA 72:28 Standard and Optional Veterans' Tax Credit

benefits.benefit: All veterans' tax credit (town option)
benefits.details: If the town has adopted it, a resident veteran with at least 90 days of active service gets the same dollar credit as the town's regular veterans' credit, with no wartime-period requirement.
