You cannot receive it if you are eligible for or get the RSA 72:28 or 72:35 credit. Apply with the town assessor by April 15. Whether it exists depends on your town.
benefits.source_title: RSA 72:28-b All Veterans' Tax Credit

benefits.benefit: Combat service tax credit (town option)
benefits.details: Towns may adopt a credit of $50 up to $500 (up to $750 from April 1, 2027) for a New Hampshire National Guard or reserve member called to active duty in a combat area. It replaces, not adds to, the regular veterans' credit and requires military orders with the application. It is for current service members, not a disability benefit.
benefits.source_title: RSA 72:28-c Optional Tax Credit for Combat Service

benefits.benefit: Disabled veteran plate, free registration, and parking
benefits.details: A veteran evaluated by the VA as 'permanently and totally disabled' from a service-connected disability (or an amputee or paraplegic who received a vehicle from the government) gets one set of special plates with the accessibility symbol free, and pays no registration fee for the vehicle. Plates with the accessibility symbol receive free parking time in cities and towns. Apply through the town clerk and the DMV. Veterans rated below 100% P&T do not qualify for the free plate or registration.
benefits.source_title: RSA 261:86 Special Number Plates for Certain Veterans; RSA 261:141, VIII

benefits.benefit: Driver license fee waiver
benefits.details: No fee is charged for a driver's license for a veteran evaluated by the VA as permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected disability, or for an amputee or paraplegic veteran who received a vehicle from the government. Present VA proof of the rating at the DMV.
benefits.source_title: RSA 263:42 Driver's License Fees, paragraph III

benefits.benefit: Free perpetual hunting and fishing license
benefits.details: A New Hampshire resident veteran with a discharge other than dishonorable who is 'totally and permanently disabled' from a service-connected disability gets a perpetual fishing, hunting, or bow-and-arrow license for a one-time $10 administrative fee. Apply to the Fish and Game Department with your VA award letter showing the permanent 100% rating. Veterans at least 80% but under 100% can get a lifetime license at 50% of the regular lifetime price.
benefits.source_title: RSA 214:13 Licenses for Disabled Veterans

benefits.benefit: Free state park day-use admission
benefits.details: A disabled veteran of New Hampshire with a service-connected disability of any rating pays no day-use admission fee at state parks. Proof is a disabled veteran plate or a VA letter certifying a service-connected disability. Camping, ski lifts, tram rides, food service, and other enterprise activities still cost money.
benefits.source_title: RSA 216-A:3-g Fees for Park System, paragraph IV

benefits.benefit: Tuition waiver for children of 100% P&T veterans
benefits.details: A child (biological, adopted, or stepchild) of a veteran who is totally and permanently disabled from service attends any University System of New Hampshire institution without tuition. The parent must have lived in New Hampshire at service entry or at the VA disability determination and must still live there. Apply to the university system trustees with the VA letter showing 100% total, permanent, service-connected. Eligibility lasts through the semester the child turns 27, and the child must file the FAFSA.
benefits.source_title: RSA 187-A:20 Tuition Waived

benefits.benefit: Tuition for children of killed or missing service members
benefits.details: The state veterans page says children of military members who die in wartime service, and children of certain wartime veterans who die of a service-connected disability, may get free tuition at New Hampshire public colleges. A need-based scholarship of up to $2,500 per year for up to 4 years may also be furnished (RSA 193:19 to 193:21). Children of service members missing or captured after February 28, 1961 get free community college tuition under RSA 188-F:15. I read this on the agency page and did not read the RSA 193 text.
benefits.source_title: NH State Benefits for Veterans (Education Benefits)

benefits.benefit: State income tax on military pay, VA compensation, and other income
benefits.details: New Hampshire taxes no wages and has no general income tax. The Interest and Dividends Tax was repealed for tax periods starting January 1, 2025, so there is no state tax on that income either. The state veterans page says military retired pay, VA disability compensation, and DIC are not taxed and no state return is needed.
benefits.source_title: NH Department of Revenue Administration: Repeal of NH Interest and Dividends Tax Now in Effect

benefits.benefit: State employment hiring preference
benefits.details: When the state is the employer, preference in hiring goes to a veteran (as defined in RSA 21:50) who is one of multiple otherwise equally qualified candidates. Towns, cities, and counties give preference to state-citizen veterans with at least 90 days of wartime service. There is no points system and no disability tier in this statute. Spouses of totally disabled wartime veterans and unremarried surviving spouses get the preference under RSA 283:5, per the agency page.
benefits.source_title: RSA 283:4 Employment of Veterans

benefits.benefit: New Hampshire Veterans' Home (Tilton)
benefits.details: The Veterans' Home in Tilton is a 250-bed intermediate, long-term care facility, with 100 beds for residents with dementia. Contact the home at (603) 527-4400 to learn who is eligible and the costs. I did not read the eligibility statute (RSA 119) because the page would not load, so check with the home.
benefits.source_title: NH State Benefits for Veterans (Miscellaneous Benefits); RSA 119:9

states.name: New Jersey

agency.name: New Jersey Department of Veterans Affairs

notes: The full property tax exemption is for a veteran who has 'active duty service' and is honorably discharged, and whose VA certification says the disability is 100% permanent and total. The state claim form (D.V.S.S.E., rev. March 2025) has a box for a 'Service-connected disability rated unemployable with payment of 100% and stated to be totally and permanently disabling,' so a TDIU rating counts only if it is paid at 100% and the VA states it is permanent and total. A 100% rating that is not marked permanent does not qualify, and the exemption cannot start before all of these are met.

The Treasury page says the veteran must be 100% permanently and totally disabled 'during active duty service.' The statute also says the disability must be 'sustained through enemy action, or accident, or resulting from disease contracted while in such active service.' A disability that comes only from National Guard or Reserve training, with no active duty, is a risk; ask the assessor before assuming it counts.

You must own the home (all or part) and live in it as your principal residence, and be domiciled in New Jersey. The exemption covers the house and the 'lot or curtilage' it sits on, not extra land or rental units. For a multi-unit building, only the part you occupy is exempt. An absence from the state of 12 months is treated as evidence you gave up your New Jersey domicile.

You file the claim (Form D.V.S.S.E.) with your municipal tax assessor, not the state. You can file any time during the tax year, and a prorated exemption is allowed from the date you acquire the home. Refunds of past tax are up to each town's governing body (N.J.S.A. 54:4-3.32) and cannot go back before January 16, 2018 unless you had qualifying wartime service. If the assessor denies you, appeal to your County Board of Taxation on Form A-1 by April 1 (January 15 in Burlington, Gloucester and Monmouth counties).

A surviving spouse keeps the exemption only while unmarried and only while owning and living in the home; if the spouse remarries or forms a new civil union, it ends. A surviving spouse of a service member who died on active duty also qualifies, and the surviving spouse of a veteran who is declared disabled after death can qualify. Claimants must tell the assessor about any change that affects eligibility.

The separate $250 deduction does not need any disability, but you must have 'active duty' service (Reserve and Guard members only if called to active duty; 'Active duty for training is ineligible') and an honorable discharge, and own the property on October 1 of the year before the tax year. The wartime-service rule for both the $250 deduction and the disabled veteran exemption ended December 4, 2020. Note that a Department of Veterans Affairs Gold Star page still says the $250 deduction needs wartime service; the Division of Taxation page (updated 8/12/25) controls.

New Jersey has no ordinary vehicle registration fee waiver for a 100% rated veteran. Free registration is limited to veterans blind from war service, or veterans with another service-connected disability who qualified for a free automobile from the VA and whose vehicle has special equipment. A disabled veteran who buys a car with VA or NJDVA money pays no sales tax only on the part of the price those agencies fund. Wheelchair symbol plates and parking placards for disability follow separate medical-certification rules.

The disabled veteran parking placard (N.J.S.A. 39:4-207.10) only exempts the vehicle from municipal parking meter fees for up to 24 hours. It does not allow parking in wheelchair-labeled spaces. It works only when you own the vehicle and are the driver or a passenger, and it must be renewed every 3 years.

The free hunting and fishing license program covers a veteran with a service-connected disability 'of any degree,' but you must be certified by mail first (not online or at a license agent) and have lived in New Jersey at least six months. The certification is invalid if you move out of New Jersey. You still need to complete hunter education and any other hunting requirements, and certified veterans do not get lottery preference.

New Jersey does not tax U.S. military pension or survivor benefit payments at any age, but federal civil service pensions are taxable even if they count military time. VA disability compensation is not part of New Jersey taxable income, but no page I could read directly says that in so many words, so confirm it with the Division of Taxation if it matters for your return.

The state civil service preference needs an honorable discharge and service in a listed war era; Reserve and Guard training time (basic training, advanced training, OCS, weekend drills, annual training) does not count toward the active duty requirement. Disabled veteran preference also requires at least 10% VA disability compensation. Many recent veterans have the 'wartime' dates problem, so check the era list before assuming you qualify.

Three older tuition programs are narrow: the Veterans Tuition Credit Program is only for Dec. 31, 1960 to May 7, 1975 service ($400 a year), War Orphan aid is for children of those who died in service or from service-connected disability ($500 a year), and POW-MIA free tuition is for children of POW or MIA parents. In-state tuition (NJTEAM Act) depends on qualifying for the federal All-Volunteer Force or Post-9/11 GI Bill programs, not on a disability rating.

benefits.benefit: 100% disabled veteran property tax exemption (N.J.S.A. 54:4-3.30)
benefits.details: Your home and its lot are fully exempt from property tax if you served on active duty, were honorably discharged, and the VA certifies that you are 100% permanently and totally disabled from your service. The state claim form also accepts a service-connected disability 'rated unemployable with payment of 100% and stated to be totally and permanently disabling.' You must own all or part of the home, live in it as your principal residence, and be a New Jersey resident. File Form D.V.S.S.E. with your municipal tax assessor at any time during the tax year, with your DD-214 and the VA certification of disability; there is no income limit and no fixed deadline, and the exemption is prorated from the date you acquire the home.
benefits.source_title: NJ Division of Taxation - 100% Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption (updated 8/12/25); Claim Form D.V.S.S.E. (rev. March 2025); N.J.S.A. 54:4-3.30 as amended by P.L.2019, c.413

benefits.benefit: Property tax exemption for the surviving spouse of a 100% disabled veteran or of a service member who died on active duty
benefits.details: An unremarried surviving spouse, civil union partner, or domestic partner gets the same full exemption on the home if the deceased veteran was a New Jersey resident, had active duty service, and was honorably discharged and VA-certified 100% permanently and totally disabled (or died on active duty). The surviving spouse can also qualify if the VA declares the veteran disabled after death. You must own and live in the home as your principal residence and live in New Jersey, and the exemption ends if you remarry or form a new civil union. File Form D.V.S.S.E. with the municipal assessor with the death certificate, marriage record, DD-214 (or Military Notification of Death) and the VA certification.
benefits.source_title: NJ Division of Taxation - 100% Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption (surviving spouse requirements); N.J.S.A. 54:4-3.30(b)-(c)

benefits.benefit: $250 Veterans Property Tax Deduction
benefits.details: Any honorably discharged veteran with active duty service can take $250 off the tax bill each year; Reserve and Guard members must have been called to active duty, and active duty for training does not count. As of October 1 of the year before the tax year, you must be a New Jersey legal resident and own the property. The unremarried surviving spouse of an eligible veteran or of a service member who died on active duty also qualifies. File Form V.S.S. with your local assessor or tax collector with your DD-214 and proof of ownership and residency; if denied, appeal to the County Board of Taxation (Form A-1, by April 1).
benefits.source_title: NJ Division of Taxation - $250 Veterans Property Tax Deduction (updated 8/12/25); Form V.S.S.

benefits.benefit: Free registration for blind or service-disabled veterans (and sales tax exemption on a VA-funded vehicle)
benefits.details: The Motor Vehicle Commission offers free registration only to a veteran without sight from war service who is eligible for state compensation under N.J.S.A. 38:18-1, or a veteran with another service-connected disability who has qualified for a free automobile from the VA. The vehicle must be equipped with special attachments needed to operate it, be insured in New Jersey, and you need a New Jersey driver license. Call 609-292-6500 ext. 5076 for the application and mail it with the VA seal or stamp to the MVC Government Unit, P.O. Box 016, Trenton, NJ 08666-0016. Separately, a disabled veteran pays no Sales Tax on the part of a car's price paid with VA or NJDVA funds; any out-of-pocket amount is taxed.
benefits.source_title: NJ Motor Vehicle Commission - Active Duty Military Personnel and Veterans (free registration); NJ Division of Taxation Consumer Automotive Tax Guide, Q49

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran (DV) license plates and parking-meter placard
benefits.details: A Disabled Veteran plate series (DV1000-DV9999) is listed at $15, and the MVC form says you need a copy of your DD-214 or DD-215 and the VA 'Award of Disability percentage letter,' with the application approved by a liaison who certifies membership; the MVC pages do not state a minimum rating. Separately, a Disabled Veteran placard (Form SP-47, DD-214 plus VA Award of Disability letter) exempts a vehicle you own from municipal parking meter fees for up to 24 hours, requires you to be the driver or a passenger, must be renewed every 3 years, and cannot be used in wheelchair-labeled spaces. Apply at any MVC agency or by mail to the NJMVC Special Plates Unit, P.O. Box 015, Trenton, NJ 08666-015.
benefits.source_title: NJ Motor Vehicle Commission - Disabled Veteran, Purple Heart Recipient Placards (N.J.S.A. 39:4-207.10); Military Personnel plates page; Form SP-23

benefits.benefit: Free hunting and fishing licenses, stamps and permits for disabled veterans
benefits.details: Honorably discharged New Jersey resident veterans whom the VA has declared to have a 'service-connected disability of any degree' get free hunting and fishing licenses, stamps and permits. You must be certified by mail first: send the Disabled Veterans application with your VA disability letter or VA card, your DD-214, and proof of at least six months of New Jersey residency to Disabled Veteran Licensing, Division of Fish and Wildlife, PO Box 420, Trenton, NJ 08625-0420. Certified veterans get unlimited antlerless deer permits, but the state does not give them lottery preference, and hunter education is still required to hunt.
benefits.source_title: NJ DEP Division of Fish and Wildlife - Disabled Veteran License Information; Instructions for Free NJ Disabled Veterans License

benefits.benefit: State park disability pass and free Island Beach State Park disabled veteran vehicle permit
benefits.details: New Jersey has no general free state park pass for disabled veterans. The state park Senior Citizen and Disability Pass gives free entrance and discounted camping to New Jersey residents with a disability, with no veteran requirement, and the department said it was being updated (disability passes only from the Trenton office, 1-800-843-6420). Island Beach State Park has a free disabled veteran vehicle permit for designated fishing areas; it needs a DD-214 showing honorable discharge and proof of a service-connected disability. I could not read the DEP park pages directly, so confirm both with the State Park Service.
benefits.source_title: NJ DEP State Parks, Forests and Historic Sites - State Park Pass; Island Beach State Park permits

benefits.benefit: In-state tuition at New Jersey public colleges (NJTEAM Act)
benefits.details: A veteran or covered family member 'living in New Jersey and attending a public institution of higher education in New Jersey' is treated as a state resident for tuition, whatever their home state. The veteran must have served on active duty, been discharged or released, and qualify for federal All-Volunteer Force or Post-9/11 GI Bill education benefits. Covered individuals are family members entitled to Post-9/11 benefits through a veteran (transferred benefits) and, for terms beginning after March 1, 2019, people entitled to VA Vocational Rehabilitation and Employment benefits. Show your VA education benefit eligibility to the college's registrar or veterans office.
benefits.source_title: New Jersey Legislature - P.L.2015, c.32 (NJTEAM Act) as amended by P.L.2019, c.264 (N.J.S.A. 18A:62-4.1a, 4.1b)

benefits.benefit: State veteran tuition aid: Veterans Tuition Credit Program, War Orphan Tuition Assistance, POW-MIA Tuition Benefit
benefits.details: The Veterans Tuition Credit Program pays $400 a year ($200 per semester full-time; $100 per semester part-time) to veterans eligible for federal education benefits who served on active duty from Dec. 31, 1960 to May 7, 1975 and lived in New Jersey at induction or for a year before applying. War Orphan Tuition Assistance pays $500 a year for four years to children of service members who died in service or from service-connected disability, or who are MIA. The POW-MIA Tuition Benefit gives free undergraduate tuition to a child of a New Jersey POW or MIA declared after January 1, 1960. Contact the Veterans Benefits Bureau at 888-865-8387 or VBB@dva.nj.gov.
benefits.source_title: NJ Department of Veterans Affairs - NJ Veterans Benefits Guide (PDF created April 2026), Education section

benefits.benefit: Military pension and survivor benefit exemption from state income tax
benefits.details: The Division of Taxation says 'U.S. military pension and survivor's benefit payments are not taxable' for New Jersey residents, at any age and without a disability test. Regular military pay is taxable, but combat zone pay is not taxable for tax year 2021 and later. Federal civil service pensions are still taxable even if they credit military service. New Jersey has an income tax, so other income is taxed normally. VA disability compensation is not part of New Jersey taxable income as far as I can tell, but I could not find a page I could read that says so directly; confirm with the Division of Taxation.
benefits.source_title: NJ Division of Taxation - Military Personnel and Veterans (updated 4/30/25)

benefits.benefit: $6,000 Veteran Income Tax Exemption
benefits.details: If you were honorably discharged or released under honorable circumstances from active duty on or before the last day of the tax year, you can claim a $6,000 exemption on your New Jersey income tax return, in addition to your other exemptions. Your spouse can claim a second $6,000 on a joint return if they are also a veteran. Check the veteran exemption oval (resident return) or box (nonresident return); the first time you claim it you must provide official documentation such as a DD-214, or pre-certify it with the Veteran Income Tax Exemption Submission Form. It does not pass to a surviving spouse except for the year of death on a joint return.
benefits.source_title: NJ Division of Taxation - Income Tax Exemption for Veterans

benefits.benefit: Civil service Veterans and Disabled Veterans preference
benefits.details: Eligible veterans who pass an open competitive civil service exam are placed at the top of the list ahead of non-veterans, and eligible disabled veterans are placed above both. You need an honorable discharge from active duty with service in a qualifying war era (some eras require 90 days; later eras need 14 days or a service-incurred injury, and the right geographic area), and for the disabled veteran level 'at least a 10% disability compensation' from the VA. Spouses and surviving spouses of disabled veterans can qualify in some cases. Submit the Civil Service Veterans Preference Claim Form, DD-214 and VA award letter through the NJ Department of Veterans Affairs (888-865-8387, VBB@dva.nj.gov), up to 8 days before a list is issued.
benefits.source_title: NJ Department of Veterans Affairs - Civil Service Preference for Veterans (updated 10/02/2026); P.L.2007, c.115

benefits.benefit: New Jersey Catastrophic Entitlement ($150 a month)
benefits.details: A New Jersey resident wartime veteran with a 100% permanent service-connected rating from the VA for one of seven catastrophic disabilities gets a monthly payment of $150. The listed disabilities are loss of sight; amputation of both hands, both feet, or one hand and one foot; hemiplegia with permanent paralysis of one leg and one arm on the same side; paraplegia; osteochondritis with permanent loss of use of both legs; multiple sclerosis with loss of use of both feet or legs; and quadriplegia. A widow or widower who was in receipt of the entitlement, or would have been entitled to apply, can qualify. Contact the Veterans Benefits Bureau at 888-865-8387 or VBB@dva.nj.gov and use the Catastrophic Entitlement Application.
benefits.source_title: NJ Department of Veterans Affairs - Benefits & Resources (updated 10/06/2026); Gold Star Families page; Veterans Benefits Guide

benefits.benefit: New Jersey Veterans Memorial Homes and state veterans cemetery
benefits.details: The three state long-term care homes (Paramus, Menlo Park, Vineland) are open to veterans honorably discharged from war or peacetime service, their spouses, and spouses and parents of members killed in action in wartime; preference goes to applicants who were state residents for at least two years, and residents pay according to ability based on income. The Brigadier General William C. Doyle Veterans Memorial Cemetery in Wrightstown offers free interment and perpetual care to veterans, their spouses, and dependent children, and pre-registration is encouraged. Contact each home through the NJDVA Memorial Homes page, and the cemetery at 609-738-2400.
benefits.source_title: NJ Department of Veterans Affairs - Veterans Memorial Homes (updated 10/13/2026); Doyle Veterans Memorial Cemetery page; Veterans Benefits Guide

states.name: New Mexico

agency.name: New Mexico Department of Veterans' Services

notes: New Mexico's disabled veteran property tax exemption changed for tax year 2026. It used to be an all-or-nothing benefit for 100% rated veterans; now it is prorated by VA rating from 10% to 100% (HB 47 of 2025 and HB 285 of 2026, after the November 2024 constitutional amendments). The state's own August 2026 release says 7,096 partially disabled veterans received it from March through June 2026.

The amount is your rating percent times the taxable value left after the $10,000 standard veteran exemption is subtracted. Example: a 40% rating on $200,000 of taxable value is 40% of $190,000. Check the arithmetic with your assessor.

The statute says 'permanent service-connected disability,' and the DVS application asks for a VA finding of service-connected disability. State releases say every rating from 10% to 100% qualifies. I could not find an official page that says how a non-permanent rating is treated, and none that says TDIU alone counts, so ask DVS if your rating is temporary or TDIU-only.

You apply through DVS first, not the assessor. DVS issues a certificate of eligibility. DVS accepts only a NM driver's license or ID, voter registration, or latest NM income tax return as proof of residency. Then you file the certificate and an occupancy form with the county assessor.

Deadline: file no later than 30 days after the county assessor mails the Notice of Value (NOV), or the exemption is not allowed for that tax year. HB 285 lets you file a protest if the claim is still pending at 30 days, and the exemption is not applied to prior tax years.

The home must be your principal residence and you must occupy it continuously. If two disabled veterans own the same home, the highest rating is used. Property in a grantor trust can qualify. You must tell the assessor by the end of February after you lose eligibility, and knowingly claiming a false exemption is a misdemeanor with up to a $1,000 fine.

Surviving spouses: for the standard exemption the spouse must be unmarried; for the disabled exemption the spouse must have been married to the veteran at death and keep living in the home. DVS says the spouse qualifies even if the veteran never applied.
Moving: you may keep the exemption on the old home for the rest of the year or move it to the new principal residence, even if you did not file within 30 days of the notice.

The free 50% disabled veteran plate waives the registration fee for up to two vehicles, but MVD guidance says people qualifying for more than one free military plate category get only one category. The disabled parking symbol is a separate step through the HP plate route.

The State Parks Lifetime Veteran Pass (HB 161) is now for all resident veterans, not just 50% rated ones. Free lifetime hunting and fishing is 100% only; anyone below 100% pays $10 for the combo license.

New Mexico is an income tax state. Military retirement pay is exempt up to $30,000 per qualifying retiree (2025). I did not find an official New Mexico page that states how VA disability compensation is treated, so do not assume.
The Wartime and Vietnam scholarships are for the veteran only. Tuition help for children is limited to children of deceased veterans, per DVS, and is not tied to disability rating.

benefits.benefit: Disabled veteran property tax exemption (prorated by rating)
benefits.details: Starting with the 2026 property tax year, the home's taxable value (after the $10,000 standard veteran exemption is subtracted) is reduced by a percentage equal to your VA disability rating, so 100% rated is fully exempt and 30% rated is 30% exempt. The home must be your principal residence and you must occupy it continuously. The statute says 'permanent service-connected disability' but New Mexico's agencies describe the benefit as available at every rating from 10% to 100%. Get a certificate of eligibility from the NM Department of Veterans' Services (DVS), then file it with your county assessor within 30 days after the assessor mails the Notice of Value.
benefits.source_title: HB 285 (2026), amending NMSA 7-37-5.1 and 7-38-17

benefits.benefit: Standard veteran property tax exemption ($10,000, indexed)
benefits.details: Any New Mexico resident veteran who is honorably discharged (not dishonorable or misconduct) and served 90 continuous days of active duty (or fewer days if discharged for a service-connected disability) gets $10,000 off the taxable value of property they own, for tax year 2025. From tax year 2026 the amount is adjusted yearly for inflation. No disability rating is needed. Apply with DVS for a certificate, then file it with the county assessor.
benefits.source_title: HB 47 (2025), amending NMSA 7-37-5

benefits.benefit: Surviving spouse of a veteran or disabled veteran
benefits.details: An unmarried surviving spouse who is a New Mexico resident keeps the $10,000 standard exemption. For the disabled veteran exemption, the spouse must have been married to the veteran at the time of death and must continue to live in the home continuously as a principal residence. DVS says the spouse is entitled to the disabled exemption even if the veteran never applied. A spouse who remarries and then divorces is not entitled to the standard exemption.
benefits.source_title: DVS Form 1: Application for Veteran and Disabled Veteran Tax Exemption (rev. March 2025)

benefits.benefit: Reduced vehicle registration fees (two-thirds rate)
benefits.details: A veteran entitled to the veteran property tax exemption who does not have enough real or personal property to use up the full exemption may pay motor vehicle registration fees at two-thirds of the regular rate on vehicles the veteran owns. DVS lists this benefit; I could not pull the statute text itself, and the NMAC rule I saw may bar anyone who claimed part of the property tax exemption. Ask DVS or MVD before relying on it.
benefits.source_title: NM DVS State Benefits: Reduced Registration Fees

benefits.benefit: 50% Disabled Veteran license plate with no registration fee
benefits.details: A veteran who is at least 50% disabled from service can get the Disabled Veteran plate for up to two vehicles, including motorcycles, with no fee of any kind, including the regular registration fee. Apply with MVD form MVD10353 and proof of the 50% rating. A veteran who also qualifies for a limited mobility (HP) plate can have the wheelchair symbol put on this plate, which is the route to disabled parking privileges.
benefits.source_title: NM MVD Chapter 7 Special Plates (NMSA 66-3-412)

benefits.benefit: Motor vehicle excise tax exemption (loss of use of limbs)
benefits.details: A New Mexico resident veteran who lost, or lost the total use of, one or both legs at or above the ankle or one or both arms at or above the wrist, from service or a service-connected cause, is exempt from the motor vehicle excise tax on vehicle purchases. This is a loss-of-use test, not a percentage test. Medical certification is needed; contact MVD or DVS for the exact form.
benefits.source_title: NM DVS State Benefits: Exemption from Excise Taxes on Vehicle Purchases (NMSA 7-14-6)

benefits.benefit: Lifetime Veteran Pass for all NM State Parks
benefits.details: Under HB 161 (2025), every New Mexico resident veteran who was not dishonorably discharged can get a free lifetime hang-tag pass covering day-use, camping and utility fees at all State Parks Division parks as of July 1, 2025. No disability rating is required. It does not cover reservation fees ($3 to $10), group shelters, cabins or yurts. Apply through DVS with a DD 214; the old 50% annual passes are honored only until they expire.
benefits.source_title: NM State Parks: For Veterans (HB 161)

benefits.benefit: Free lifetime hunting and fishing (Disabled Veteran card)
benefits.details: New Mexico residents who are 100% disabled from service get a free lifetime game-hunting and fishing license by applying for a Disabled Veteran card from the Department of Wildlife. The card also allows a free deer license, but only if you apply and are drawn or buy a leftover; a habitat stamp is still needed for privileges the card does not cover. Apply with DD 214, VA award letter and proof of residency.
benefits.source_title: NM Dept. of Wildlife: Age, Disability, Military licenses

benefits.benefit: $10 combination hunting and fishing license (under 100%)
benefits.details: A New Mexico resident disabled veteran who is below 100% can buy a $10 combination game-hunting and fishing license online, by phone or from vendors, at any service-connected percentage. A Habitat Management and Access Validation and Habitat Stamp are required where applicable. Show proof of disability to the Department of Wildlife.
benefits.source_title: NM Dept. of Wildlife: Age, Disability, Military licenses

benefits.benefit: Free State Monuments and Museums pass
benefits.details: A New Mexico veteran rated 50% or higher service-connected disabled may obtain a free State Monument and Museum Pass for personal use only. Apply using the Monuments and Museums Pass application on the DVS benefits page.
benefits.source_title: NM DVS State Benefits: Free and Reduced-Fee Recreational Benefits

benefits.benefit: Wartime Veterans Scholarship
benefits.details: Pays tuition, required fees and books at New Mexico public schools for resident undergraduate and graduate students who are honorably discharged war veterans with a combat campaign or service medal on the DD 214 and are certified by DVS. Awards are first come, first served, last one academic year and renew with satisfactory progress. Apply through DVS. This is for the veteran, not dependents.
benefits.source_title: NM Higher Education Dept.: Wartime & Vietnam Veterans Scholarship

benefits.benefit: Vietnam Veterans Scholarship
benefits.details: Pays tuition, required fees and books for resident students who are honorably discharged Vietnam veterans with the Vietnam campaign medal for service between August 5, 1964 and the official end of the conflict, and who lived in NM at entry or for 10 years or more. Certified by the NM Veterans Service Commission and applied for through DVS. Renewable yearly.
benefits.source_title: NM Higher Education Dept.: Wartime & Vietnam Veterans Scholarship

benefits.benefit: Immediate in-state tuition for veterans, spouses and children
benefits.details: DVS states that veterans, their spouses and their children no longer have to wait to establish in-state residency when applying for college, so those using GI Bill education benefits can pay resident tuition at any state-funded college, university or vocational program right away. Ask the school's registrar how it documents this.
benefits.source_title: NM DVS State Benefits: In-State Tuition

benefits.benefit: Income tax exemption for armed forces retirement pay ($30,000)
benefits.details: For tax year 2025, an armed forces retiree or surviving spouse of a retiree may exempt $30,000 of armed forces retirement pay from New Mexico net income (claimed on Schedule PIT-ADJ, line 24; each qualifying spouse on a joint return gets $30,000). 'Retiree' means someone who qualified by years of service or disability for lifetime benefits. A 2026 bill to remove the cap (SB 116) appears to have stalled, and a TRD analysis said the exemption sunsets after 2026, so check the 2026 instructions.
benefits.source_title: 2025 Instructions for PIT-ADJ, Line 24 (NM Taxation and Revenue)

benefits.benefit: State employment preference points
benefits.details: Per DVS, honorably discharged veterans and current National Guard members get 5 points added to their final passing score on State Personnel Office screening exams. Honorably discharged veterans with a service-connected disability get 10 points. Submit your DD 214 and VA documentation with the state job application.
benefits.source_title: NM DVS State Benefits: Veterans Hiring Preference (NMSA 10-9-13.2)

states.name: New York

agency.name: New York State Department of Veterans' Services

notes: New York property tax breaks for veterans are local options. The state law lets each county, city, town, village and school district choose whether to offer the Alternative Veterans Exemption, the Cold War exemption and the new permanent and total disability exemption, and many set their own dollar caps. Ask your assessor or municipal clerk what your specific home gets. The state tax page says municipalities decide whether to offer these.

Alternative Veterans Exemption (RPTL 458-a): 15% off assessed value for wartime service, 10% more for combat zone service, plus 50% of the VA disability rating. The default state caps are $12,000, $8,000 and $40,000 (each multiplied by the state equalization rate, or the class ratio for special assessing units, whichever is less). A local law can lower or raise those caps, so a 100% rated veteran may get far less or far more than the default depending on the town and school district.

The Alternative Veterans Exemption is for the primary residence of the veteran or the unremarried surviving spouse. The statute allows temporary absence for medical reasons or institutionalization. The general application deadline is the taxable status date, which is March 1 in most communities, but check with your assessor. Cities of one million or more (New York City) accept applications by March 15.

A new full exemption for veterans the VA considers permanently and totally disabled as a result of military service (RPTL 458-a(11)) is a local option and applies to assessment rolls with taxable status dates on or after October 1, 2026. It covers the primary residence, including property taxes, special ad valorem levies and special assessments. Ask whether your municipality or school district has adopted it. Bills to loosen or change the eligibility language were pending in 2026 and were not confirmed as law.

New York does not have a statewide disabled-veteran property tax exemption that applies everywhere. No official page we found says that TDIU alone qualifies for any of the property tax exemptions. The new full exemption asks for VA documentation of permanent and total disability from military service, so ask your assessor whether a permanent TDIU rating counts.

Fee-exempt vehicle registration is tied to Title 38 (VA automobile adaptive equipment grant) vehicles, not simply to a disability percentage. DMV says it can be used for one vehicle, and replacing the vehicle needs new documentation. The separate Disabled Veteran plate costs $28.75 to start with no renewal fee, but ordering requires an existing Symbol of Access plate or the Universal Symbol of Access process, and orders are by mail on form CP-30 only.

Reduced-fee hunting and fishing licenses and the Sportsman license need a service-related disability of 40% or more, with annual proof from the VA. The Lifetime Liberty Pass, which used to require a disability rating, no longer does for state residents who are veterans (see the Parks page). Do not assume a rating is needed for the pass.

The Veterans Tuition Award is not disability based. Since the 2025 change, veterans with at least four years of active duty can qualify even without combat service. Recipients of Chapter 33 or Yellow Ribbon tuition coverage are not eligible if those programs already cover tuition. The Regents Award for children of disabled veterans pays only $450 per year, needs a 40% or higher rating, and needs the veteran to have served in a designated war or national emergency.

New York State income tax: military retirement pay is totally exempt from New York State, New York City and Yonkers income tax, and benefits paid on account of a veteran follow federal treatment, so amounts excluded from federal gross income (such as VA disability compensation) are excluded. New York does have an income tax; this is an exemption, not an absence of tax.

Civil Service Law section 85 gives a disabled veteran 10 additional points on an original-appointment competitive exam and 5 on promotion, if the VA certifies a disability rated at 10% or more. The credit can be used for only one permanent appointment or promotion, and it is added only after you pass the exam and the eligible list is created. Credits you already used as a non-disabled veteran are subtracted.

Thruway E-ZPass for disabled veterans is free and unlimited on the NYS Thruway only, and the only requirement is a fee-exempt DMV registration, so it comes through the Title 38 vehicle path. Renewal is every two years.

benefits.benefit: Alternative Veterans Exemption (wartime, combat, disability-based)
benefits.details: Local-option reduction in assessed value of the veteran's primary residence: 15% for wartime service, 10% more for combat zone service, plus 50% of the VA disability rating. Default state caps are $12,000, $8,000 and $40,000 times the equalization rate, but local laws can lower or raise them. Unremarried surviving spouses qualify. File with the local assessor by the taxable status date (usually March 1; March 15 in cities of one million or more).
benefits.source_title: NY Real Property Tax Law section 458-a (Alternative veterans exemption)

benefits.benefit: Permanent and total disability exemption (full)
benefits.details: Local-option full exemption from property taxes, special ad valorem levies and special assessments on the primary residence of a veteran the VA documents as permanently and totally disabled as a result of military service (honorable discharge or qualifying discharge). Applies to rolls with taxable status dates on or after October 1, 2026, and only where the municipality or school district adopts it. Apply to the assessor, usually by March 1. Whether TDIU alone counts is not stated; ask the assessor.
benefits.source_title: Alternative veterans exemption and veterans with a permanent and total disability exemption (NYS Tax Dept.)

benefits.benefit: Cold War Veterans Exemption
benefits.details: Local-option exemption for Cold War veterans (active duty September 2, 1945 to December 26, 1991) on the primary residence: 10% (cap $8,000) or 15% (cap $12,000) of assessed value, plus 50% of the service-connected disability rating (cap $40,000), each adjusted by the equalization rate. The base exemption does not need a disability. Unremarried surviving spouses qualify. Apply to the local assessor.
benefits.source_title: NY Real Property Tax Law section 458-b (Cold War veterans exemption)

benefits.benefit: Fee-exempt vehicle registration (Title 38)
benefits.details: A veteran who receives a vehicle under federal Title 38 (VA adaptive equipment benefit) is eligible for a fee-exempt registration, usable for one vehicle only. Replacing the vehicle needs new documentation. DMV requires the VA Form 21-4502 paperwork. This is tied to the VA vehicle benefit, not a stated disability percentage.
benefits.source_title: DMV: Information for Military and Veterans

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran license plate
benefits.details: Custom Disabled Veteran plate: $28.75 initial purchase with a DMV-assigned number, $0.00 annual renewal, cannot be personalized. Requires a DD-214 or NA Form 13038 and an existing plate with a Symbol of Access (or the Universal Symbol of Access process). Order by mail only on form CP-30. The DMV page does not state a disability percentage. Do not confuse with the Disabled American Veteran plate, which needs DAV lifetime membership.
benefits.source_title: DMV: Disabled Veteran plate

benefits.benefit: Free Thruway E-ZPass for disabled veterans
benefits.details: Free unlimited travel on the NYS Thruway for qualifying disabled veterans whose vehicle has a DMV fee-exempt registration. The Authority says disability percentage and specialty plates do not decide eligibility. Apply with form TA-W5175 and a copy of the fee-exempt registration; renew every two years.
benefits.source_title: NYS Thruway Authority: E-ZPass for Disabled Veterans

benefits.benefit: Reduced-fee hunting and fishing licenses
benefits.details: Resident veterans with a service-related disability of 40% or more can get reduced-fee hunting and fishing licenses, including a Sportsman license. Annual proof from the VA is required. Contact a DEC regional office or the hotline listed by the veterans agency. The current dollar price was not confirmed.
benefits.source_title: Reduced Fee New York State Hunting and Fishing Licenses for Disabled Veterans (NYS Dept. of Veterans' Services)

benefits.benefit: Lifetime Liberty Pass (state parks)
benefits.details: Free for NY residents who are veterans (or Gold Star parents, spouses or children): free vehicle entry to most state-operated parks and DEC day-use areas, free greens fees at state golf courses, free pool entry, and discounted camping and cabins. No disability rating is required. Order free at shop.parks.ny.gov with a DD-214 or a NY DMV ID with the Veteran designation; discharge must be other than dishonorable or bad conduct.
benefits.source_title: NYS Parks: Lifetime Liberty Pass

benefits.benefit: Veterans Tuition Award
benefits.details: Pays tuition up to the average SUNY undergraduate resident tuition (or actual tuition if lower) for NY residents of 12 continuous months who are veterans with at least four years of active duty or combat service in Vietnam, the Persian Gulf or Afghanistan, and not dishonorably discharged. No disability needed and no income limit. Apply through HESC with the FAFSA and TAP application each year. Not available where Chapter 33 or Yellow Ribbon already covers tuition.
benefits.source_title: HESC: Veterans Tuition Award

benefits.benefit: Regents Award for Children of Deceased and Disabled Veterans
benefits.details: $450 per year for the child of a veteran who served in a designated war or national emergency and, as a result, died, has a 40% or higher disability, was missing in action or was a POW. The veteran must be or have been a NY resident; the student must be a 12-month NY resident at an approved NY college. No income limit, open year-round. Apply through HESC.
benefits.source_title: HESC: Regents Awards for Children of Deceased and Disabled Veterans

benefits.benefit: Military retirement pay and veterans benefits income tax treatment
benefits.details: New York has a state income tax, but military pension payments to a retiree or beneficiary are totally exempt from NY State, New York City and Yonkers income tax. Benefits paid on account of a veteran follow federal treatment, so amounts excluded from federal gross income are excluded in New York. VA disability compensation is not named on the page; it relies on the federal exclusion.
benefits.source_title: Information for military personnel and veterans (NYS Tax Dept.)

benefits.benefit: Civil service additional credits for disabled veterans
benefits.details: Disabled veterans (VA-certified disability rated 10% or more) get 10 additional points on competitive exams for original appointment and 5 on promotion exams. Credits are added after you pass, when the eligible list is established, and can be used for one permanent appointment or promotion. Submit proof to the Department of Civil Service within the time given in the exam announcement (the statute allows at least two months from filing).
benefits.source_title: NY Civil Service Law section 85

states.name: North Carolina

agency.name: North Carolina Department of Military and Veterans Affairs

notes: The property tax exclusion is not based on a percentage alone. G.S. 105-277.1C requires either a VA certification of a 'service-connected, permanent, and total disability' as of January 1 before the tax year, or receipt of specially adapted housing benefits under 38 U.S.C. 2101. A 100% rating that is not permanent and total does not qualify, and the statute does not mention TDIU, so a TDIU-only veteran should ask the county before assuming eligibility.

The exclusion removes only the first $45,000 of appraised value from taxation. It is not a full exemption. A bill to raise it to $61,000 (House Bill 118, 2025) was last sent back to the House Rules Committee on 9/23/2025 and has not become law, so $45,000 is still the current figure.
A veteran who takes the homestead exclusion 'may not receive other property tax relief' under the same section, so you cannot stack it with the elderly or disabled exclusion.

The home must be a permanent residence that you own and occupy. You must be a North Carolina resident. There is no income limit in the statute. The unmarried surviving spouse of a qualifying veteran can also claim it.

Apply at your county tax office using Form AV-9 plus Form NCDVA-9 (certified by a county veteran service officer). Papers must be in by June 1 of the tax year. Get the VSO certification well before then.

The Disabled Veteran plate is for a 100% combined rating or Individual Unemployability paid at the 100% rate, per the state veterans agency. The plate statute itself only says '100% service-connected disability.' Veterans rated under 100% get a Partially Disabled Veteran plate instead.

The plate itself carries a $0 special fee, but NCDMV materials list it as 'in addition to regular license fee.' I did not find an official page that waives the regular yearly registration fee for disabled veterans, so expect to pay it unless NCDMV tells you otherwise.

The lifetime hunting and fishing license needs a 50% or higher VA rating and a mail-in or in-person application with VA certification. It is reduced price, not free (about $15 for the basic licenses), and it stays valid only while you remain at 50% or higher.

The free State Parks Annual Pass (S.L. 2024-45) only needs an honorable discharge and any service-connected disability benefit or certification. Most state parks already charge no entry fee, so the pass mainly covers reservoir day-use fees, boat launches, and some rentals.

North Carolina's own wartime-veteran children's scholarship pays for the CHILD, not the veteran. Class I-B (parent rated 100% for wartime service) covers tuition and fees; other classes include room and board. The child must be under 25 and an NC resident, and the parent's service must be in a defined wartime period.

North Carolina has an income tax (4.25% for 2025). Military retirement pay is deductible since 2021 only if the retiree served 20 or more years or was medically retired. VA disability compensation is excluded from federal income, and NC starts from federal AGI, but I did not find an NC page stating it outright.

State job preference is experience credit for military training and service, not added points. It applies to a 'veteran who served during a period of war,' a peacetime veteran with a service-connected disability, and certain spouses.

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran Property Tax Homestead Exclusion
benefits.details: The first $45,000 of appraised value of your permanent residence is excluded from taxation. You qualify if you have an honorable or under-honorable discharge and, as of January 1, a VA certification of a service-connected, permanent, and total disability, or you receive specially adapted housing benefits under 38 U.S.C. 2101. An unmarried surviving spouse of such a veteran, or of a veteran who died of a service-connected condition, also qualifies. Submit Form NCDVA-9 (VSO certified) and Form AV-9 to your county tax office by June 1; there is no income test.
benefits.source_title: G.S. 105-277.1C Disabled veteran property tax homestead exclusion

benefits.benefit: Homestead exclusion: how to apply (NCDVA-9 and AV-9)
benefits.details: Complete Sections 1 and 2 of Form NCDVA-9, have a local veterans service office certify it, then give NCDVA-9 and Form AV-9 to your county tax office. The state agency says the date for timely submission is June 1 of the current tax year. Non-spouse co-owners who each qualify still get no more than $45,000 total.
benefits.source_title: NCDMVA Veterans Property Tax Relief

benefits.benefit: Proposed increase to $61,000 (not law)
benefits.details: House Bill 118 (2025) would raise the exclusion to $61,000. Its last action was re-referral to the House Rules Committee on 9/23/2025, and the statute text still says $45,000. A different version summarized by the UNC School of Government would tie the exclusion to the VA rating percentage, but that was an earlier draft. Check the county or the General Assembly before relying on a higher figure.
benefits.source_title: House Bill 118 Disabled Veterans Tax Relief Bill

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran license plate (100%)
benefits.details: The DV plate is issued to a veteran with a 100% service-connected disability; the state veterans agency says a combined 100% rating or Individual Unemployability paid at the 100% rate qualifies. NCDMV lists a $0 special fee, and NCDMV form MVR-33A allows one free plate per person per year. You need an MVR-33A certified by a county VSO or NCDMVA, then you apply at a license plate office; one form per vehicle. Personalization costs $30 a year.
benefits.source_title: NCDMVA Military and Veteran License Plates

benefits.benefit: Partially Disabled Veteran plate
benefits.details: Veterans with a service-connected disability under 100% can get a Partially Disabled Veteran plate (prefix PD) with a $0 special fee. It is issued on the same MVR-33A with VSO certification. It does not carry any registration fee waiver that I could find.
benefits.source_title: G.S. 20-79.4 Special registration plates, subdivision (b)(190)

benefits.benefit: Registration fee and parking for disabled veterans
benefits.details: I found no official page that waives the regular annual registration fee, highway use tax, or gives parking privileges for disabled veterans. The only fee provision located is a $1.55 fee for a vehicle given by the federal government to a veteran for a war disability (G.S. 20-87). The DV plate shows a $0 special fee in addition to the regular license fee. Ask NCDMV before assuming a waiver; the disability parking placard is a separate medical program.
benefits.source_title: G.S. 20-87 Annual license fees

benefits.benefit: Lifetime disabled veteran hunting and fishing license
benefits.details: A resident veteran rated 50% or more by VA can buy a lifetime license at a reduced price: $15 for inland fishing, coastal fishing, or the hunting/inland fishing combo, and $131 or $144 for the Sportsman packages, plus a $5 transaction fee. It stays valid for life while you remain at 50% or more. Mail or bring the NCDMVA-50 form with VA certification to the Wildlife Resources Commission; disabled licenses cannot be applied for online.
benefits.source_title: NC Wildlife Resources Commission Disabled Licenses

benefits.benefit: Free State Parks Annual Pass for disabled veterans
benefits.details: Veterans discharged honorably who received benefits or certification of a service-connected disability get the Annual Pass (normally $90) free under S.L. 2024-45. Send the request form with your VA Summary of Benefits Letter to the Division of Parks and Recreation. It covers day-use at Falls, Jordan, and Kerr Lake, some boat launches, and select rentals.
benefits.source_title: NC State Parks: Free Annual Pass for Veterans with Disabilities

benefits.benefit: Scholarship for Children of War Veterans
benefits.details: The state scholarship is for the child of a wartime veteran. Class I-B covers a child of a parent rated 100% disabled by VA for wartime service, with free tuition and certain fees at public schools and $2,800 per nine-month year at private schools. Class II (parent rated 20% to under 100%, or Purple Heart) adds room and board. The child must be under 25 and an NC resident, with the application sent to NCDMVA.
benefits.source_title: NCDMVA Scholarship for Children of War Veterans Synopsis (Rev. 8-2021)

benefits.benefit: In-state tuition for veterans and dependents
benefits.details: A veteran, a dependent of a veteran, or another covered person under the federal Choice Act rule can pay in-state tuition without waiting 12 months, if their abode is North Carolina and they file a letter of intent to establish residence. This is for GI Bill-type covered individuals, not a disability-based waiver. I found no state tuition waiver for the disabled veteran personally.
benefits.source_title: G.S. 116-143.3A Waiver of 12-month residency requirement

benefits.benefit: Military retirement pay deduction
benefits.details: North Carolina taxes income at 4.25% for 2025. Uniformed-service retirement pay is deductible on Form D-400 Schedule S Line 21 if you served at least 20 years or were medically retired under 10 U.S.C. chapter 61; severance pay is excluded. Bailey Settlement retirees (5 years of service by August 12, 1989) use Line 20 instead and cannot take both.
benefits.source_title: 2025 D-401 Individual Income Tax Instructions

benefits.benefit: VA disability compensation and state income tax
benefits.details: North Carolina starts from federal adjusted gross income, and VA disability compensation is not in federal income. I did not find an NC Department of Revenue page that says this directly for VA compensation, so treat this as an inference and confirm with the Department of Revenue.
benefits.source_title: 2025 D-401 Individual Income Tax Instructions

benefits.benefit: State government hiring preference
benefits.details: State agencies subject to the Human Resources Act must give an eligible veteran credit for military training, schooling, and experience toward minimum qualifications, plus extra experience credit for other military service. Eligible veterans include wartime veterans, peacetime veterans with a service-connected disability, and certain spouses and survivors. It is experience credit, not added points; appeal under G.S. 126-34.01.
benefits.source_title: G.S. 126-82 State Human Resources Commission to provide for preference

benefits.benefit: North Carolina State Veterans Homes
benefits.details: The state runs skilled nursing homes for veterans at Black Mountain, Fayetteville, Kernersville, Kinston, and Salisbury, licensed and approved for Medicare, Medicaid and third-party insurance. The state page did not list eligibility or costs, so call 844-624-8387 for admission rules.
benefits.source_title: NCDMVA North Carolina State Veterans Homes

states.name: North Dakota

agency.name: North Dakota Department of Veterans Affairs

notes: The property tax credit is not a full exemption. It is your VA rating percentage applied to only the first $9,000 of taxable valuation of your homestead (about $180,000 of true and full value). A 50% rating gets 50% of $9,000; 100% gets the full $9,000 of taxable value.

Property tax credit requires a 50% or higher service-connected rating, or an extra-schedular rating including individual unemployability that pays at the 100% rate, plus an honorable discharge or military retirement. The home must be owned and occupied by you as your homestead.

File the credit application (SFN 24770) with the county auditor by April 1 of the first year you claim it, with a DD-214 and a VA certificate of your rate. A 2025 bill to change this statute (HB 1266) failed in the Senate, so the $9,000 base was not changed.

The credit ends at the end of the tax year in which the applicant dies. A surviving spouse can claim a credit in their own right; a spouse receiving VA Dependency and Indemnity Compensation gets the 100% credit.

Registration-fee waiver and the DAV plate require 100% service-connected (or 100% through extra-schedular/unemployability) or Public Law 79-663 eligibility. A 50% to 90% rating gets no registration waiver; a 2019 bill to lower this to 50% failed.
The registration waiver and sales/excise tax exemption cover no more than two vehicles at a time, each at or under 26,000 pounds registered gross weight.
The state veterans site says vehicles with the DAV plate may use designated handicap parking spots in North Dakota. Other plates do not carry that privilege.
The state park free lifetime pass needs 50% or higher service-related disability (or former POW) and North Dakota residency. Veterans below 50% can buy an annual permit for $28.

Game and Fish discounts begin at 50%. The veteran combined hunting license is $10 plus a $2 certificate (and $5 Waterfowl Restoration Stamp if hunting waterfowl). A 2025 law lowered the threshold from 100% to 50% at $3, but a later 2025 fee law appears to have raised it to $10, so confirm the price when you buy.

The tuition waiver is for dependents (child, stepchild, spouse, widow or widower), not for the veteran. It requires a resident veteran with a 100% rating (extra-schedular or unemployability counts), a POW, a person missing in action, or a service-connected death. Covers undergraduate degrees and certificates only, and excludes aviation flight charges.

North Dakota exempts retired military pay from state income tax to the extent included in federal taxable income. VA disability compensation is not part of federal taxable income, so it is not taxed by the state.

Veterans preference points (5 for a veteran, 10 for a disabled veteran) apply to state and local government hiring that uses a scored process, and need a DD-214 and a VA letter less than one year old for disabled veterans.

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veterans Property Tax Credit
benefits.details: Credit equal to your VA disability rating percentage applied against the first $9,000 of taxable valuation of your owned and occupied homestead. Eligible: 50% or higher service-connected, or extra-schedular/unemployability paid at the 100% rate, with an honorable discharge or military retirement. No income test appears in the statute. File SFN 24770 with the county auditor by April 1 of the first year, with DD-214 and VA rate certificate.
benefits.source_title: N.D.C.C. 57-02-08.8 Property tax credit for disabled veterans

benefits.benefit: Property Tax Credit for Surviving Spouses
benefits.details: The surviving spouse of an eligible disabled veteran may claim the credit on the homestead they own and occupy. A surviving spouse receiving VA Dependency and Indemnity Compensation gets a 100% credit of the first $9,000 of taxable valuation. The credit ends at the end of the tax year of the applicant's death. Apply with the county auditor by April 1.
benefits.source_title: Application for Disabled Veterans Property Tax Credit, SFN 24770 (2026)

benefits.benefit: Registration Fee Waiver and DAV Plates
benefits.details: Motor vehicles at or under 26,000 pounds owned by a veteran with a 100% service-connected rating (including extra-schedular/unemployability at the 100% rate) or Public Law 79-663 eligibility are exempt from registration fees, with a free distinctive or standard plate. Limit is two vehicles at once; a DIC surviving spouse gets one. Apply with a VA certification letter and form SFN 2872.
benefits.source_title: DAV Plates (ND Dept. of Veterans Affairs); N.D.C.C. 39-04-18(2)(j)

benefits.benefit: Vehicle Sales and Use Tax Exemption
benefits.details: Vehicles acquired by disabled veterans under Public Law 79-663 are exempt from state sales or use tax (refund if paid). It also covers a passenger vehicle or pickup at or under 26,000 pounds, limited to two such vehicles at a time. The state veterans site says the DAV plate is tied to this two-vehicle excise exemption.

benefits.benefit: Disabled Parking with DAV Plate
benefits.details: The state veterans site says vehicles with the DAV plate may park in designated handicap parking spots in North Dakota, with no extra placard needed (cites N.D.C.C. 39-01-15). Same 100% certification as the DAV plate.
benefits.source_title: DAV Plates (ND Dept. of Veterans Affairs)

benefits.benefit: Veteran Combined Hunting License
benefits.details: Resident disabled veteran with at least a 50% service-connected rating (or extra-schedular/unemployability) gets a combined general game, habitat stamp, small game and fur-bearer license for $10, plus a $2 certificate. Eligibility is verified through the ND Department of Veterans Affairs. A 2025 law set this at $3 but a later fee change appears to have set $10; confirm at purchase.
benefits.source_title: N.D.C.C. 20.1-03-12(46); Game and Fish Resident Licenses

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran Fishing License
benefits.details: Resident fishing license is $10 (instead of $25) for a resident disabled veteran with at least a 50% service-connected rating, or extra-schedular/unemployability bringing the total to at least 50%, plus a $2 certificate. Buy through Game and Fish.
benefits.source_title: Resident Licenses and Requirements (ND Game and Fish); N.D.C.C. 20.1-03-12(6)

benefits.benefit: State Parks Free Lifetime Permit
benefits.details: North Dakota veterans with a 50% or greater service-related disability, and former POWs, are eligible for a free lifetime pass to state parks. Proof is a current VA Summary of Benefits Letter. Other ND veterans with a service-related disability may buy an annual permit for $28. Contact parkrec@nd.gov.
benefits.source_title: Daily & Annual Permits (ND Parks and Recreation)

benefits.benefit: Dependent Tuition Waiver
benefits.details: Free tuition and fees at North Dakota University System institutions for the child, stepchild, spouse, widow or widower of a resident veteran who is 100% service-connected (extra-schedular/unemployability counts), a POW, missing in action, or died from service-connected causes. Undergraduate degree or certificate only; excludes aviation flight charges. Apply through the campus financial aid or veterans office.
benefits.source_title: ND Dependent Tuition Waiver; N.D.C.C. 15-10-18.2 and 15-10-18.3

benefits.benefit: Military Retirement Pay Income Tax Subtraction
benefits.details: North Dakota reduces taxable income by retired military personnel benefits (including those paid to a surviving spouse) to the extent included in federal taxable income. VA disability compensation is not included in federal taxable income, so it is not state taxed. North Dakota does have a state income tax.

benefits.benefit: Veterans Preference in Public Employment
benefits.details: In scored hiring by state and local governments, 5 points are added for a veteran and 10 points for a disabled veteran. For unscored hiring, a disabled veteran is first entitled to the position absent documented justifiable cause. Provide a DD-214 and, for disabled preference, a VA letter less than one year old.
benefits.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 37-19.1 Veterans' Preferences

benefits.benefit: North Dakota Veterans Home (Lisbon)
benefits.details: State veterans home offering basic care and skilled nursing for eligible veterans, spouses and surviving spouses with honorable service and North Dakota ties. Admission requires a formal application approved by the home's board of admissions. No disability rating required. Bed counts differ between pages, so call the home.
benefits.source_title: North Dakota Veterans Home (ND Dept. of Veterans Affairs)

states.name: Ohio
notes: The enhanced homestead reduction for disabled veterans (R.C. 323.151(F), 323.152(A)(2)) needs honorable discharge or release under honorable conditions AND a 'total disability rating or a total disability rating for compensation based on individual unemployability.' The Ohio tax form DTE 105I says the applicant 'must be 100% disabled by or be receiving 100% compensation' on January 1 of the year the exemption is sought. A TDIU award letter showing compensation at 100% plus the IU approval document is accepted. Nothing in the statute requires 'permanent' for this one.
The homestead reduction for a disabled veteran has no income test. The ordinary senior/disabled homestead exemption does have one, and the statute excludes disabled veterans from it.

The homestead amount is indexed every year: $58,000 of true value for tax year 2025 and $59,400 for tax year 2026 (Ohio Department of Taxation). It is not a flat $50,000. It is a credit equal to the taxes on that much value, so the dollar savings depend on your local tax rate. It applies to one homestead only (the dwelling plus up to one acre) and you must own and live in it.

Real property applications go to the county auditor and the DTE 105I form says 'on or before December 31.' The form has a late-application box for prior years. The statute text on codes.ohio.gov for 323.152 shows an effective date of September 23, 2026 (House Bill 479); I could not tell what that bill changed, so check with your county auditor before filing.

Disabled veterans plates (R.C. 4503.41) and the free driver license fees (R.C. 4507.23(I)) require a service-connected disability 'rated or compensated at one hundred per cent.' The plate also qualifies a veteran who was awarded the VA automobile allowance. The BMV needs a VA letter dated within the past year. The first registration is free; each additional vehicle titled in your name pays the usual fees.

The free hunting and fishing license (R.C. 1533.12(B)(1)) is NOT tied to a plain 100% rating. It requires a disability the VA has determined to be 'permanently and totally disabling', VA pension or compensation, and an honorable discharge, OR ownership of disabled-veteran plates under 4503.41. ODNR form DNR 9032-B is sent to the Ohio Department of Veterans Services (Cleveland) for certification and lasts five years, but you must still get the license each year from an agent or online.

The free state park camping pass uses the same 'permanently and totally disabled' plus VA compensation test. It is a camping pass; I found no official Ohio state park entry-fee waiver because I found no general entry fee page.

The Ohio War Orphan and Severely Disabled Veterans' Children Scholarship is for CHILDREN, not the veteran. The parent must have a 60 percent or greater service-connected rating (or VA permanent and total non-service-connected benefits), must have entered service as an Ohio resident (with exceptions), the child must be 16 but not yet 25 at application, and there is a financial need requirement. Deadline for 2027-28 is May 15, 2027, and a FAFSA is required.

Ohio taxes start from federal adjusted gross income, so VA disability compensation, which is not in federal AGI, is not taxed by Ohio. Military retirement pay is a separate state deduction (R.C. 5747.01(A)(23)), and Guard/Reserve and active-duty military pay has its own deduction (A)(21).

The civil service credit (R.C. 124.23(C)) is 20 percent added to the passing exam grade for honorably discharged veterans who file a certificate of service or honorable discharge. It does not need a disability rating and applies to the classified civil service exam process.

A 2025 law (House Bill 96) lets each county's commissioners adopt an extra local-option homestead exemption that matches the state amount, but only if that county approved it. Ask your county auditor whether yours did.

benefits.benefit: Enhanced homestead exemption for disabled veterans
benefits.details: Taxes are reduced as if $58,000 of the home's true value (tax year 2025) or $59,400 (tax year 2026) were exempt, with no income limit. You need honorable discharge and a total (100%) disability rating or a 100% rating based on individual unemployability (TDIU), in place on January 1 of the year you apply. File form DTE 105I with the county auditor on or before December 31 with your DD-214 and VA award letter. It covers one owned and occupied home plus up to one acre.
benefits.source_title: Ohio Department of Taxation, Homestead Exemption FAQ (amounts) and form DTE 105I; R.C. 323.151(F), 323.152(A)(2)

benefits.benefit: Homestead exemption for surviving spouses of disabled veterans
benefits.details: A surviving spouse who occupied the home when the veteran died and then owns it (or the spouse of a veteran who died before receiving the total rating, once that rating is received for the deceased spouse) gets the same reduction amount. It continues through the tax year in which the surviving spouse dies or remarries. Apply with form DTE 105I (check 'surviving spouse') at the county auditor by December 31.

benefits.benefit: County local-option homestead exemption
benefits.details: House Bill 96 (2025) allows county commissioners to add a second homestead exemption equal to the state amount with the same eligibility requirements, which would roughly double the reduction. It applies only in counties whose commissioners approved it. Ask your county auditor whether it is in effect.
benefits.source_title: Ohio Department of Taxation, Homestead Exemption FAQ, question 16

benefits.benefit: Disabled veterans license plates and free registration
benefits.details: Veterans with a service-connected disability 'rated or compensated at one hundred per cent' by the VA, or who received the VA automobile allowance, pay no registration fee, service fee or local motor vehicle tax on the first vehicle and get red, white and blue plates with the wheelchair symbol. Additional vehicles titled in your name can be registered but pay the usual fees. Apply at a BMV deputy registrar with form BMV 4507 and a VA letter dated within the past year.
benefits.source_title: R.C. 4503.41 (last updated July 21, 2025); Ohio BMV Veterans with Disabilities Plates

benefits.benefit: Disabled parking privileges (plates and removable placard)
benefits.details: The 100% disabled veteran plates carry the international access symbol and may be used in marked accessible spaces. Separately, any veteran with a documented service-connected disability that limits or impairs the ability to walk can get a free removable windshield placard (form BMV 4531, a VA letter dated within one year, and a prescription or health care provider certification).
benefits.source_title: Ohio BMV Removable Windshield Placard

benefits.benefit: Free driver license and permit fees
benefits.details: A veteran with a service-connected disability rated or compensated at 100% can get a temporary permit, new, renewal, reprint or duplicate driver's or commercial license, and a motorcycle endorsement without paying the statutory fees. Apply at the BMV or a deputy registrar with proof of the rating. Ohio BMV also lists state ID card fees as waived under R.C. 4507.50, which I could not read in full.
benefits.source_title: R.C. 4507.23(I) (effective March 20, 2026)

benefits.benefit: Free hunting and fishing licenses
benefits.details: Resident veterans with a VA-determined permanently and totally disabling disability who receive VA pension or compensation and have an honorable discharge, or who hold disabled veterans plates under 4503.41, get free fishing, hunting, fur taker, deer, wild turkey and wetlands habitat stamp. Send form DNR 9032-B to the Ohio Department of Veterans Services office in Cleveland. Approval lasts five years and you must still obtain the licenses each year.
benefits.source_title: R.C. 1533.12(B)(1) (effective March 20, 2026); ODNR form DNR 9032-B

benefits.benefit: Free state park camping pass
benefits.details: An honorably discharged Ohio resident veteran who is a former prisoner of war, or who is permanently and totally disabled and receiving VA compensation, gets free camping at Ohio state parks. Apply online at reserveohio.com (Applications tab) and upload a VA benefit letter. The reservation fee still applies.
benefits.source_title: ODNR Discounts on Camping and Lodging

benefits.benefit: War Orphan and Severely Disabled Veterans' Children Scholarship
benefits.details: For children of a veteran with a 60% or greater service-connected disability (or VA permanent and total non-service-connected benefits). It covers up to 100% of general and instructional fees at public colleges, with a reduced percentage possible if funds run short, or a grant at private schools, for up to five academic years. Child must be 16 but under 25 at application, with financial need. Apply to the Ohio Department of Higher Education by May 15, 2027 (for 2027-28) with a VA overall rating letter and FAFSA.
benefits.source_title: Ohio War Orphan and Severely Disabled Veterans' Children Scholarship Application; R.C. 5910.03, 5910.04

benefits.benefit: State income tax: military retirement pay
benefits.details: Ohio lets you deduct military retired pay for service in the uniformed services, reserves or National Guard, and Survivor Benefit Plan payments to a surviving or former spouse, to the extent not already excluded from federal AGI. Claim it on the Ohio return (IT 1040 schedule of adjustments). Active duty and reserve military pay is also separately deductible under (A)(21).
benefits.source_title: R.C. 5747.01(A)(23) and (A)(21) (effective March 5, 2026)

benefits.benefit: State income tax: VA disability compensation
benefits.details: Ohio income tax starts from federal adjusted gross income, and VA disability compensation is excluded from federal gross income, so it is not part of the Ohio base. I did not find a tax.ohio.gov page that states this in so many words, so confirm with the Ohio Department of Taxation.
benefits.source_title: R.C. 5747.01 (definition of Ohio adjusted gross income)

benefits.benefit: Civil service exam credit for veterans
benefits.details: Honorably discharged veterans who are Ohio residents may file a certificate of service or honorable discharge with the director and receive an additional credit of 20 percent of their total grade on a civil service examination they pass. National Guard and reserve members with more than 180 days of active duty ordered by the president or Congress also qualify. A reserve member who finished initial entry training gets 15 percent. No disability rating is needed.
benefits.source_title: R.C. 124.23(C) (effective March 20, 2025)

states.name: Oklahoma
notes: The full homestead property tax exemption (Okla. Const. Art. 10, Sec. 8E) requires an honorable discharge, Oklahoma residency, and VA certification of a 100% permanent disability sustained through military action or accident (or disease contracted in service). A lower rating gets nothing from this exemption; a proposed amendment for ratings below 100% is only a pending proposal.

The state property tax form (OTC 998) says you must own and live in the home on January 1 of each year, including the year you apply, and your deed must be recorded with the county clerk by February 1 of the first year. It also asks if you are 'Head of Household.'

The OTC 998 asks for a VA award letter showing 100% service-connected disability, or proof you are paid at the 100% rate. The form language does not say whether a TDIU rating (paid at the 100% rate but not a schedular 100%) qualifies. Ask your county assessor before assuming.

The sales tax exemption for 100% disabled veterans is limited to $25,000 per year in qualifying purchases, covers sales and use tax only, and does not cover gasoline tax, tobacco tax, or the 7% medical marijuana excise tax. It also requires registering with ODVA. It is not retroactive to purchases before you hold the exemption.

A surviving spouse who has not remarried keeps the sales tax exemption but only up to $1,000 per year. The vehicle excise tax break does not extend to surviving spouses, according to Service Oklahoma's refund form.
The vehicle excise tax exemption for 100% disabled veterans covers only one vehicle purchased every three years, counted from purchase date to purchase date with no grace days.

The Disabled American Veteran (DAV) plate needs only 50% service-connected and costs a flat $5.00 plus a $1.50 insurance fee on Service Oklahoma form 751-J.
