A DAV plate with the accessibility symbol also requires an existing disabled parking placard; the plate alone does not give parking privileges.
The $25 lifetime combination hunting/fishing license starts at 60%; veterans rated below 60% can still buy it but pay $200. You need a VA award letter showing your combined rating.
Free state park and museum admission is for any honorably discharged veteran who lives in Oklahoma, not just disabled veterans, and you must show a valid Oklahoma ID plus a DD 214.

Some ODVA benefit-page text is out of date. It still says military retirement is exempt up to the greater of 75% or $10,000, while the Oklahoma Tax Commission says 100% is excludable beginning tax year 2022. Trust the Tax Commission.

State hiring preference points appear to be gone: the state HR office says Veterans Preference and points no longer apply to state hiring since the 2022 civil service reform, replaced by a guaranteed-interview Veterans Placement program. Older rules and pages still showing 5/10 points are likely outdated.
Oklahoma has a state income tax. VA disability compensation is federally tax-free and is not part of Oklahoma taxable income.

benefits.benefit: 100% disabled veteran homestead property tax exemption
benefits.details: Full exemption from the fair cash value of the homestead (no dollar cap) for an honorably discharged head of household certified by the VA as 100% permanently disabled from military action, accident, or disease contracted in service; the unremarried surviving spouse also qualifies. Apply with OTC Form 998 plus a current VA award letter to the county assessor where the property is located. You must own and occupy the home on January 1 and have your deed recorded by February 1; a filing deadline was not stated on the form, so ask your assessor. Whether TDIU qualifies is not stated on the form.
benefits.source_title: OTC Form 998, Application for 100% Disabled Veterans Real Property Tax Exemption (Tax Year 2026, revised 11-2025)

benefits.benefit: Surviving spouse property tax exemption
benefits.details: The unremarried surviving spouse of a qualifying 100% disabled veteran can claim the same full homestead exemption under Section 8E, and OTC 998 has a box for 'surviving spouse of such 100% compensated veteran.' The Constitution also lets the veteran or spouse sell and buy another homestead in the same year and keep the exemption. Apply through the county assessor with the VA documentation.
benefits.source_title: Oklahoma Constitution Art. 10, Sec. 8E (text via 50constitutions.org; ODVA page confirms surviving spouse)

benefits.benefit: Sales and use tax exemption
benefits.details: Residents certified by the VA as paid at the 100% rate for a permanent service-connected disability are exempt from sales and use tax on up to $25,000 of purchases per year; an unremarried surviving spouse gets up to $1,000 per year. Apply online with the Oklahoma Tax Commission (OkTAP) with a VA letter for this state benefit and ODVA registry enrollment; ODVA helps at 888-655-2838. Gasoline and tobacco taxes are not exempt.
benefits.source_title: Oklahoma Tax Commission Help Center: Exemptions (no last-updated date shown)

benefits.benefit: Vehicle excise tax exemption
benefits.details: 100% disabled veterans are exempt from motor vehicle excise tax on one vehicle purchased every three years, measured from purchase date. Show your 100% DAV sales tax exemption card or a VA letter with raised seal when you title the vehicle with Service Oklahoma. Does not extend to surviving spouses per Service Oklahoma's refund form.
benefits.source_title: Service Oklahoma Fees: Excise Tax Exemptions

benefits.benefit: Disabled American Veteran (DAV) license plate
benefits.details: Veterans with at least 50% service-connected disability can get a DAV plate for a $5.00 plate fee plus $1.50 insurance fee (form 751-J, revised 2/2025), or keep a regular tag for up to two vehicles of one ton or less. Plates are only moved to a new vehicle at initial title and registration. The accessibility-symbol version requires a Service Oklahoma disabled parking placard.
benefits.source_title: Service Oklahoma Form 751-J and OAC 260:135-7-152

benefits.benefit: Free driver license issuance and renewal
benefits.details: An honorably discharged veteran certified by the VA as paid at the 100% rate for a permanent disability sustained through military action or accident or disease contracted in service is not charged a fee to issue or renew an Oklahoma driver license (47 O.S. 6-101). Ask Service Oklahoma what proof they require.
benefits.source_title: ODVA Benefits: Free License & Renewal for 100% Disabled Military/Veteran (page published 01/12/2026)

benefits.benefit: Lifetime disabled veteran combination hunting/fishing license
benefits.details: Resident disabled veterans with VA certification can buy a lifetime combination hunting/fishing license for $25 at 60% or more, or $200 below 60%. Bring a VA award letter showing your combined rating. The $25 license includes some tags not in the free permit.
benefits.source_title: Oklahoma Dept. of Wildlife Conservation Lifetime License Info Sheet (June 2024)

benefits.benefit: Free permit and Wildlife Land Stamp exemption (60%+)
benefits.details: ODVA's page, quoting state wildlife law, lists a free hunting and fishing permit for resident veterans with 60% or more disability and an exemption from the Wildlife Land Stamp requirement. The same page says 100% rated veterans are exempt from fees for deer gun, deer archery, primitive firearms, and bonus/second deer gun licenses. Confirm the current permit process with the Wildlife Department.
benefits.source_title: ODVA Benefits: Hunting and Fishing Licenses (page published 01/12/2026)

benefits.benefit: Free state park and museum admission
benefits.details: Honorably discharged veterans who currently live in Oklahoma get free admission to state-owned or state-operated parks and museums. Show a valid Oklahoma driver license or state ID and your DD 214 or similar proof of honorable discharge. This is not limited to disabled veterans.
benefits.source_title: ODVA Benefits: Admission to State Parks (page published 01/12/2026)

benefits.benefit: Military retirement pay excluded from state income tax
benefits.details: Oklahoma has an income tax. Beginning in tax year 2022, each individual may exclude 100% of retirement benefits from any component of the Armed Forces; claim it on Schedule 511-A (residents) or 511NR-B. VA disability compensation is federally tax-free and not part of Oklahoma taxable income.
benefits.source_title: Oklahoma Tax Commission Help Center: Income Tax

benefits.benefit: State employment: Veterans Placement program
benefits.details: The state HR office says Veterans Preference and points no longer apply to state hiring after House Bill 1146. In their place, honorably discharged veterans (Oklahoma residency not required) who submit a DD 214 to the Office of Veterans Placement are guaranteed an interview for state jobs they meet the minimum qualifications for. Special disabled veterans may choose this or the provisions of 72 O.S. 401-404, whose current text I did not confirm.
benefits.source_title: OMES Civil Service FAQ (no date shown)

benefits.benefit: State college tuition for disabled veterans and dependents
benefits.details: I did not find a current official statute or State Regents policy that waives tuition for disabled veterans or their dependents. Verified items only: a State Regents policy gives in-state status to discharged service members who file a letter of intent to reside in Oklahoma, and a 2026 bill (HB 3956) to waive tuition for permanently disabled veterans is only introduced. Heroes Promise (children of those killed in the line of duty after 1/1/2000) is not for disabled veterans. Contact ODVA or the State Regents before relying on any waiver.
benefits.source_title: OSRHE Policy 3.18, In-State/Out-of-State Status of Enrolled Students

states.name: Oregon
notes: The property tax exemption (ORS 307.250-307.283) starts at a 40% disability certification. A bill to lower it to 10% (HB 2361) and a bill to raise the amounts (SB 387) were still sitting in committee on the legislature's site, and the Department of Revenue's January 2026 guide still says 40%.

The exemption takes a fixed amount off assessed value, not the whole home: $32,512 for a veteran with service-connected disabilities of 40% or more, or $27,092 otherwise (for example a 40%+ certification by a physician). Both figures rise 3% a year. It is applied to your home first and then to taxable personal property.

The exemption is not automatic and does not move with you to a new home. File with the county assessor on or before April 1 before the tax year. If you buy between March 1 and July 1, file within 30 days after the purchase. Changes in ownership or use of the home require a new claim by April 1.

A VA or armed forces disability certificate must be dated within three years before your claim. If a private physician certifies you instead, you must be recertified every year and your prior-year gross income (counting VA compensation and military retirement) cannot exceed 185% of the federal poverty level.

You must be an Oregon resident who owns and lives in the home. A buyer under a recorded purchase contract or a life estate holder counts as an owner. The state form does not say 100% P&T or TDIU is required, so any certified rating of 40% or more qualifies; TDIU is not addressed separately.

An unmarried surviving spouse or registered domestic partner can claim the exemption if the veteran died of a service-connected cause, or had received at least one year of the maximum exemption. A surviving spouse of a recently deceased veteran can continue by telling the assessor.

Oregon Disabled Veteran plates need any service-connected disability (a VA letter), an honorable discharge, and the vehicle cannot be commercial. They are a one-time permanent registration ($15 registration plus a plate fee, about $41 total for a new standard plate per DMV; confirm), but they do NOT allow parking in disabled parking spaces.

The free ODFW combination license needs a 25% or higher rating and six consecutive months of Oregon residency. A different, free Oregon Disabilities Hunting and Fishing Permit is available at 65% or higher.

The state parks Special Access Pass is for Oregon veterans with any service-connected rating, but the state parks page, the ODVA page, and a 2026 rule change (effective April 6, 2026) disagree on nights allowed and how long the pass lasts. Spouses and survivors do not qualify. Call OPRD before relying on the details.

The state college tuition waiver (ORS 350.285) is for spouses and children, not the veteran. It requires the service member to be 100% disabled (or died on duty), the student to be admitted to a bachelor's or master's program at a public university or OHSU, and a child must be 23 or younger when applying. It waives tuition only.

Oregon taxes military retirement unless the service was before October 1, 1991, and then only the pre-1991 share is subtractable. VA disability compensation is not in federal income and is therefore not taxed. Oregon has an income tax and no 'no tax' shortcut.

The 5-point and 10-point public employment preference needs a DD-214 and, for the 10-point disabled veteran preference, VA disability documentation. There is no minimum rating in the statute, and it is a preference for scoring and interviews, not a guaranteed job.

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption (service-connected 40%+)
benefits.details: Exempts $32,512 of homestead assessed value for a veteran certified by the VA or an armed forces branch as having service-connected disabilities of 40 percent or more. The amount increases 3 percent each year. Must be an Oregon resident who owns and lives in the home. File the Disabled Veteran or Surviving Spouse Exemption Claim (Form 150-303-086) with the county assessor on or before April 1; if you acquire the property between March 1 and July 1, file within 30 days. Minimum rating is 40%; not limited to 100% P&T or TDIU.
benefits.source_title: Disabled Veteran or Surviving Spouse Property Tax Exemption (DOR 150-310-676, Rev. 11-07-25)

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption (40% disabled, lower amount)
benefits.details: Exempts $27,092 of assessed value for a veteran certified by the VA or armed forces as having disabilities of 40 percent or more, or a veteran certified each year by a licensed physician as 40 percent or more disabled. The physician route has a prior-year gross income limit of 185 percent of the federal poverty level (counting VA compensation and retirement pay) and requires yearly recertification. Same April 1 county assessor filing deadline.
benefits.source_title: Disabled Veteran or Surviving Spouse Property Tax Exemption (DOR 150-310-676)

benefits.benefit: Surviving spouse property tax exemption
benefits.details: An unmarried surviving spouse or registered domestic partner may claim the exemption. The higher $32,512 amount applies if the veteran died due to service-connected injury or illness, or received at least one year of the maximum exemption; otherwise the $27,092 amount. Must own and live in the home and file with the county assessor by April 1. A surviving spouse of a recently deceased veteran can continue by notifying the assessor.
benefits.source_title: Disabled Veteran or Surviving Spouse Property Tax Exemption (DOR 150-310-676)

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran license plates and permanent registration
benefits.details: ORS 805.100 allows registration of a vehicle for a disabled veteran who was honorably discharged (90 consecutive days of service or discharged for a service-connected injury or illness) and has a VA letter. Registration is permanent with a one-time fee under ORS 803.420; DMV Form 6736 lists $15 registration plus a plate fee (about $41 for a new standard plate). One set of plates per disabled veteran, no commercial vehicles, and the plates do not allow parking in disabled parking spaces. Apply to Oregon DMV.
benefits.source_title: ORS 805.100 Disabled veterans; DMV Form 6736 and Chapter K

benefits.benefit: Free ODFW disabled veteran combination license
benefits.details: Oregon resident veterans with at least a 25 percent disability rating from the VA or an armed forces branch get a free resident hunting, fishing, and shellfish license including the Columbia Basin and Ocean endorsements. Must have lived in Oregon six consecutive months before applying. Apply by mail or in person with the most recent VA rating letter. Resident disabled veterans can also buy an elk tag for $29 (the ODVA page still says $25).
benefits.source_title: ODFW: Exclusive benefits for uniformed services and disabled veterans (page dated July 8, 2026)

benefits.benefit: Oregon Disabilities Hunting and Fishing Permit
benefits.details: A veteran rated at least 65 percent can apply for the separate free Oregon Disabilities Hunting and Fishing Permit, which adds access to certain accessible fishing sites and hunting accommodations. It is not a license or tag, so you still need a license (the 25% free license covers that).
benefits.source_title: ODFW: Exclusive benefits for uniformed services and disabled veterans

benefits.benefit: State parks Special Access Pass (camping and day-use parking)
benefits.details: Oregon veterans with any level of service-connected disability can get free day-use parking at fee parks and free camping at tent, RV, and standard horse sites. The state parks page says four nights at a time at one park or four per calendar month, valid 10 years, with a VA letter and proof of Oregon address. The ODVA page says four years, and an OPRD rule adopted effective April 6, 2026 refined the pass for Oregon residents; confirm current nights and term with Oregon State Parks. Yurts, cabins, reservation and dump fees are not covered; spouses and survivors do not qualify.
benefits.source_title: Oregon State Parks: Special Access Pass for Veterans with Disabilities

benefits.benefit: Veteran Qualified Dependent tuition waiver
benefits.details: ORS 350.285 waives tuition for the spouse, unremarried surviving spouse, or child of a service member who is 100 percent disabled from a service-connected disability (VA or armed forces certified) or who died on duty or from a service-connected cause, and for children of Purple Heart recipients (wounds in combat, 2001 or later). The student must be an Oregon resident and admitted to a bachelor's or master's program at a public university or OHSU. Limits: four years undergraduate, two years graduate, and a child must be 23 or younger when applying.
benefits.source_title: ORS 350.285 Tuition waiver for qualified veteran dependents

benefits.benefit: In-state tuition for nonresident veterans
benefits.details: Veterans pursuing undergraduate study at an Oregon public institution pay tuition and fees no greater than the Oregon resident rate even without Oregon residency, and the savings extend to dependents using transferred benefits. It does not apply to active duty members, and certain online-only programs may be excluded. No disability rating is required.
benefits.source_title: ODVA: Education benefits

benefits.benefit: State income tax on military retirement
benefits.details: Oregon taxes military retirement pay but allows a subtraction (code 307) for federal pension income based on months of service or points earned before October 1, 1991: 100 percent if all service was before that date, none if none was, otherwise the pre-1991 percentage. Disability payments before the minimum retirement age are excluded from that subtraction. Oregon also taxes remaining military pay with limited subtractions, up to $6,000 of other military pay. Oregon has a state income tax.
benefits.source_title: 2025 Publication OR-17 (Rev. 01-29-26), Federal pension income, Military pay

benefits.benefit: State income tax on VA disability compensation
benefits.details: Oregon's own veterans agency says VA disability compensation is set by federal law and is not subject to state or federal income tax. You do not report it as income on your Oregon return. The same page says this about Special Monthly Compensation too. Nothing to apply for.
benefits.source_title: Oregon Department of Veterans' Affairs : Disability Compensation : Benefits & Programs : State of Oregon

benefits.benefit: Veterans' preference in public hiring (5 and 10 points)
benefits.details: ORS 408.230 gives veterans 5 additional percentage points on scored application screens and exams, and disabled veterans 10 points. A disabled veteran under ORS 408.225 has a VA disability rating, a service-incurred disability discharge, or a Purple Heart; the statute sets no minimum percentage. Unscored processes elevate a veteran one level and a disabled veteran two levels. Current and former Oregon National Guard members are also covered. Submit a DD-214 and VA documentation to the employer.
benefits.source_title: ORS 408.230 and 408.225 Public employment preference; DAS Veterans' Preference Guide

benefits.benefit: ODVA Oregon Veteran Home Loan Program
benefits.details: State fixed-rate home loans for owner-occupied single-family homes, up to the Fannie Mae limit, purchase only (no refinance), with a lifetime maximum of four home loans. The page shown did not list the state program's eligibility rules or any disability-specific terms; apply through ODVA.
benefits.source_title: ODVA: Home Loans

benefits.benefit: Oregon Veterans' Homes (The Dalles and Lebanon)
benefits.details: Skilled nursing care for qualifying veterans, their spouses, and parents who had a child die in service. Veterans must have served as defined by the VA, have an honorable discharge, and have a physician recommend skilled nursing care. No service-connected rating is required.
benefits.source_title: ODVA: Oregon Veterans' Homes

states.name: Pennsylvania

agency.name: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)

notes: Property tax: the Disabled Veterans' Real Estate Tax Exemption needs all of these: Pennsylvania resident, honorable or under honorable conditions discharge, service during a VA-defined period of war, home owned by you (alone, or with your spouse, or as an estate by the entirety) and used as your principal dwelling. Your rating must be '100 percent permanent service-connected disability, total disability individual unemployability, or service-connected blindness, paraplegia, or loss of two or more limbs.' A temporary 100% rating is not enough. Peacetime-only veterans do not qualify.

Property tax financial need: you must also show financial need. Income of $114,637 or less gets a 'presumption of need' (effective January 1, 2025). Above that, you can still qualify if verified monthly expenses (including a cost-of-living allowance) exceed monthly household income. DMVA invites people denied for need before 2025 to reapply. I could not find a 2026 change to this figure.

Property tax application: you apply through your County Director of Veterans Affairs, not the county assessor. DMVA says not to email completed applications. The exemption page also lists surviving spouses, but DMVA's page does not spell out the surviving spouse rules (remarriage, ownership); ask the county director. A constitutional amendment on this exemption (HB 1257) was reported pending in the Senate; that is not confirmed as law.

Vehicle registration: free registration covers ONE passenger car or truck of 9,000 lbs. or less. PennDOT form MV-145V says a Severely Disabled Veteran with 100% service-connected disability certified by VA, or paid at 100% because of unemployability (TDIU), may have free registration. The two plates are different: the Severely Disabled Veteran plate (SDV) includes disability parking privileges; the plain Disabled Veteran plate does NOT, and costs a fee.

The free-registration form (MV-371DV) also covers partially disabled veterans who lost a limb or eye or became partially paralyzed in service, Purple Heart and Medal of Honor recipients, and former POWs. The Medal of Honor plate must be applied for through DMVA first. The veteran must certify no other vehicle is already registered at a reduced rate. Vehicles over 9,000 lbs. and extra plates pay full fees.

Hunting: the Game Commission's free disabled veteran license requires that the disability was 'incurred during a war or armed conflict' AND be loss or loss of use of a limb, or VA certification of 100%. Fishing has a similar page but the Fish and Boat Commission's license page lists only 'Be 100% disabled as certified by the VA' (its FAQ still carries older war-or-conflict wording). A bill to widen the hunting rule (SB 1020) was reported but I could not confirm it became law.

Reduced licenses: veterans rated 60% to 99% pay $2.97 for a resident disabled-veteran hunting license (issued annually) and can get a reduced-fee fishing license. Free licenses must be validated each year; the lifetime hunting license is sold only at county treasurer offices and must be renewed annually to receive harvest tags. A lifetime holder who moves out of state can no longer renew it.

State parks have no entrance fee. People with a disability can ask for a $4.50 discount off the base campsite price. DCNR does not say how the disability must be shown or that it applies to veterans' ratings. I found no veteran-specific park pass.

Income tax: Pennsylvania has a flat personal income tax, but 'retired or retainer pay' of a member of a uniformed service under Title 10 Chapter 71 is exempt, and disability pensions or similar allowances for injury or sickness from armed forces service are exempt. Active duty pay earned outside Pennsylvania is exempt; active duty pay for service inside Pennsylvania is taxable.

Education: Pennsylvania has no tuition waiver for disabled veterans themselves that I could verify. The Educational Gratuity Program helps children of veterans with a 100% permanent and total rating (or who died in service in wartime): up to $500 per term, up to eight payments, paid to an approved school. The child must be 16 to 23, have lived in Pennsylvania five years, and show financial need.

State jobs: eligible veterans get 10 points added to a passing civil service exam score. The preference extends to the spouse of a veteran with a VA-classified permanent total disability and to surviving spouses. A 'disability discharge' counts only if the DD-214 says 'Disability'; a VA rating alone is not that. Preference does not apply to promotions or internal postings.
State pensions: the Blind Veterans Pension and the Amputee and Paralyzed Veterans Pension each pay $150 a month, but you must have been a Pennsylvania resident when you entered the military.

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veterans' Real Estate Tax Exemption (full exemption, needs-based)
benefits.details: Your home is exempt from real estate tax if you are a Pennsylvania resident with an honorable or under honorable conditions discharge, served during a period of war, own the home and live in it as your principal dwelling, and have a '100 percent permanent service-connected disability, total disability individual unemployability, or service-connected blindness, paraplegia, or loss of two or more limbs.' You must show financial need: income of $114,637 or less is presumed to qualify (since January 1, 2025); above that, verified monthly expenses must exceed income. Apply through the County Director of Veterans Affairs in the county where you live. DMVA's page lists surviving spouses as eligible but does not give separate spouse rules; confirm with the county director. I found no filing deadline.
benefits.source_title: Department of Military and Veterans Affairs - Real Estate Tax Exemption (51 Pa.C.S. Ch. 89)

benefits.benefit: Surviving spouse of a disabled veteran: real estate tax exemption
benefits.details: DMVA states the mandatory eligibility criteria are for 'disabled veterans and their surviving spouses,' so a surviving spouse can qualify under the same residency, ownership, principal dwelling, and financial need rules, with the veteran's qualifying rating. DMVA's page does not say whether remarriage ends eligibility or how the veteran's rating is proved after death. Apply through your County Director of Veterans Affairs and ask them about those points.
benefits.source_title: Department of Military and Veterans Affairs - Real Estate Tax Exemption

benefits.benefit: Free registration for one vehicle and Severely Disabled Veteran plate
benefits.details: A Severely Disabled Veteran with a 100% service-connected rating certified by VA, or paid at 100% because of unemployability, may have free registration for one passenger car or truck of 9,000 lbs. or less. The Severely Disabled Veteran plate lets you park in disability spaces and 60 extra minutes beyond legal parking time (not where parking is prohibited). Apply to PennDOT with form MV-145V (plate; a fee applies to the plate itself) and MV-371DV (free registration), plus a VA award letter or Summary of Benefits letter showing 100%. Extra vehicles pay full fees.
benefits.source_title: PennDOT Form MV-145V (1-26) Application for Disabled Veteran, Severely Disabled Veteran Registration Plate; Form MV-371DV (4-25)

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran plate (service-connected, under 100%) and limb/eye/paralysis fee relief
benefits.details: Any veteran with a service-connected disability under 100% who does not meet the severe-disability reason codes can get a Disabled Veteran plate. It carries 'No special benefits' and 'No Special Parking Privileges,' and a fee is required. A veteran who lost a limb or eye or became partially paralyzed in service may have the processing fee waived (MV-145V) or free registration for one vehicle (MV-371DV). Purple Heart, Medal of Honor, and former POW status also earn free registration for one vehicle. Apply to PennDOT with form MV-145V or MV-371DV and a VA letter or DD-214.
benefits.source_title: PennDOT Form MV-371DV (4-25) Supplemental Application for Free Registration for Veterans; Form MV-145V

benefits.benefit: Free resident disabled veteran hunting and furtaker license (100%)
benefits.details: The Game Commission issues a free Resident DV Hunting License (annual, or lifetime at county treasurers only) to a Pennsylvania resident whose disability was 'incurred during a war or armed conflict' AND who meets one of: loss of one or more limbs, loss of use of one or more limbs, or VA certification of 100% (or 100% total compensation). Veterans with a TDIU award paid at 100% are covered by the 100% compensation wording. Get it at a county treasurer or Game Commission office with VA documentation; free licenses must be validated each year. Recent law changes (SB 1020) to drop the war requirement could not be confirmed.
benefits.source_title: Pennsylvania Game Commission - 2026-2027 Instructions for Issuing Agents Manual (Resident Disabled Veteran licenses)

benefits.benefit: Reduced-fee hunting license (60% to 99%)
benefits.details: A Pennsylvania resident veteran with a disability rating from 60% to 99% certified by VA, incurred in a war or armed conflict, can buy a Resident Reduced DV Hunting License for $2.97 (replacement $6.97), issued each year. Get it online, at a county treasurer, or at a Game Commission office with VA documentation. Veterans below 60% do not qualify.
benefits.source_title: Pennsylvania Game Commission - 2026-2027 Instructions for Issuing Agents Manual

benefits.benefit: Free fishing license (100%) and reduced fishing license (60% to 99%)
benefits.details: A Pennsylvania resident veteran with a service-connected disability who is '100% disabled as certified by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs' gets a free fishing license, and the Combination Trout/Lake Erie Permit is also free. Residents rated 60% to 99% can get a reduced-fee resident fishing license (the page gives no dollar amount). Apply first at a county treasurer, the Fish and Boat Commission Harrisburg office, or a regional office with PA ID and written VA certification, then renew annually at huntfish.pa.gov. The Commission's FAQ still has older wording tied to war or armed conflict, so confirm with them.
benefits.source_title: Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission - Apply for Fishing License (Disabled Veteran)

benefits.benefit: State parks: no entrance fee; $4.50 campsite discount for people with a disability
benefits.details: Pennsylvania state parks 'do not charge an entrance fee.' People with a disability can ask for a $4.50 discount off the base campsite price. DCNR's page does not say whether a VA rating counts or what proof is needed, and there is no veteran-specific park pass that I could find. Ask when you reserve at 888-727-2757 or online.
benefits.source_title: Department of Conservation and Natural Resources - RV and Tent Campsites (Campsite Discounts)

benefits.benefit: Educational Gratuity Program (children of 100% P&T veterans)
benefits.details: Children of a veteran with a '100% permanent and total service-connected disability rating' (honorable or under honorable discharge, wartime service) or of a veteran who died in service in wartime can get up to $500 per term or semester for up to four school years (eight payments), paid directly to an approved school. The child must be 16 to 23, have lived in Pennsylvania five years before applying, attend an approved Pennsylvania school, and show financial need. Apply through your County Director of Veterans Affairs with the DD-214, birth certificate, ID, and five years of residency proof. Pennsylvania has no tuition waiver for disabled veterans themselves that I could verify.
benefits.source_title: Department of Military and Veterans Affairs - Educational Gratuity Program

benefits.benefit: Military retired pay and disability pay exempt from state income tax
benefits.details: Pennsylvania's personal income tax guide says 'retired or retainer pay' of a member or former member of a uniform service (Title 10, Chapter 71) is exempt, and amounts received as a disability pension, annuity, or similar allowance for injuries or sickness from armed forces service are exempt. Active duty pay earned outside Pennsylvania is not taxable; pay for service inside Pennsylvania is taxable. The guide does not name VA disability compensation, but it is a disability allowance for service injury and is also not in federal taxable income. No application is needed; use the PA-40 instructions.
benefits.source_title: Department of Revenue - PA Personal Income Tax Guide: Gross Compensation; Military Pay

benefits.benefit: 10-point veterans preference on state civil service exams
benefits.details: Eligible veterans get an additional 10 points added to a passing civil service exam score, and a veteran within the rule of three also gets an appointment preference. Eligible veterans must have a discharge other than dishonorable. The preference also covers the spouse of a veteran with a VA-classified permanent total disability and surviving spouses. A 'disability discharge' counts only if the DD-214 says 'Disability.' It does not apply to promotions or internal postings. Claim it when you apply for the job or exam, with your DD-214.
benefits.source_title: Pennsylvania Office of Administration - Veterans' Preference (51 Pa.C.S. 7101.1-7111)

benefits.benefit: Blind Veterans Pension and Amputee and Paralyzed Veterans Pension ($150 a month)
benefits.details: Each pension pays $150 a month. You must have been a Pennsylvania resident when you entered the military, with an honorable or under honorable discharge. Blind: service-connected vision loss of 3/60 or 10/200 or worse in the better eye, or a visual field of 20 degrees or less. Amputee and paralyzed: loss or loss of use of two or more extremities, with at least a 40% VA rating in each limb. Apply through your County Director of Veterans Affairs with the DD-214, proof of Pennsylvania residency on entering service, and the VA decision letter.
benefits.source_title: Department of Military and Veterans Affairs - Amputee and Paralyzed Veterans Pension; Blind Veterans Pension

benefits.benefit: Veterans Temporary Assistance (VTA) up to $1,600 in 12 months
benefits.details: Temporary help of up to $1,600 in a 12-month period for food, shelter, fuel and clothing. You must be a Pennsylvania resident who was discharged under honorable conditions after active duty, or have a service-connected disability certified by VA, or be the unmarried surviving spouse of an eligible veteran. You must have a temporary, unforeseen loss of income or rise in costs and not be getting enough help from another state or federal agency. Apply through your County Director of Veterans Affairs.
benefits.source_title: Department of Military and Veterans Affairs - Veterans Temporary Assistance

states.name: Rhode Island

agency.name: Rhode Island Office of Veterans Services (Department of Human Services)

notes: Rhode Island property tax breaks for veterans are set town by town. State law (R.I. Gen. Laws 44-3-4) sets the starting amount or a maximum, but most disabled-veteran exemptions only exist if the city or town council passed an ordinance. Always ask your own assessor what your town gives.

The dollar amounts are small and differ widely. For the 100% service-connected exemption the statute says $10,000 of value as the base, with town exceptions such as Cranston (up to $250,000), Cumberland ($47,544 max), Westerly ($39,000) and Narragansett ($20,000 real estate). The state's 2022 report lists Providence at $17,247 and Warwick at a $346 tax credit. Those report figures are self-reported by towns and may be out of date.

The statute says 'totally disabled through service-connected disability' as determined by the VA. It does not use the words P&T, TDIU or schedular. Whether a TDIU rating counts is the town assessor's call. Ask before assuming. Partial ratings (under 100%) get no state-level property exemption; the statute only lets Bristol offer one by ordinance.

Deadlines are local and strict. The statute says proof must be filed with the assessors by the last day sworn statements may be filed for that tax year (South Kingstown: at least 5 days before the tax roll is certified). The state's 2022 report shows March 15 for several towns (Providence, Warwick, West Warwick). The proof stays good while your legal residence stays the same.
You must be a legal Rhode Island resident. The exemption is applied in the town where you live; if it does not use up the whole amount, you may claim the rest on property you own in another RI town.

A surviving spouse can keep the benefit only while unmarried (a remarriage that is void, ended by death, annulled or dissolved does not bar it). Specially adapted housing and the fully exempt adapted homestead pass to the surviving spouse by statute. Cranston extends its large exemption to the unmarried widow or widower.

Vehicle fee waiver and 'Disabled Veteran' plates (31-6-8) require a 100% combined service-connected rating OR a VA 'individually unemployable' rating. TDIU qualifies, and the statute does not require the rating to be permanent. Only ONE set of plates per veteran, and it covers an automobile or a commercial vehicle up to 12,000 lbs.

Free DEM fishing and combination (hunting) licenses are for veterans with a 100% disability rating. DEM requires the ORIGINAL VA decision document on VA letterhead. DEM's form says Explanation of Benefit letters do not apply. Apply by mail or in person to DEM in Providence, not through the regular online license system.

Free state beach/park parking and golf greens fees come from the DEM fee rule and R.I. Gen. Laws 32-1-17 for veterans determined by the VA to be 100% disabled through a service-connected disability. Camping, picnic table, equestrian and similar special fees are still charged.

The tuition waiver (30-30.1-1) covers the veteran only, at 10% to 100% service-connected, for permanent RI residents. It covers tuition, not other fees and charges, and you must apply for financial aid first (aid is applied to tuition first). I found no state tuition waiver for children or spouses of disabled veterans.

Rhode Island does tax income, but military service pensions are subtracted from RI income starting tax year 2023 (Schedule M, line 1v of the RI-1040, with no age or income limit). Do not also claim that same amount on the regular pension modification line.
Do not count on a car tax break. The state's car tax phase-out finished and the municipal report lists motor vehicle veteran exemptions as N/A, so the old vehicle-tax exemption is mostly moot.

benefits.benefit: Wartime veteran property tax exemption
benefits.details: Veterans who served in listed wartime periods (including Cold War service 1947-1991) with an honorable or other-than-dishonorable discharge, and their unmarried widow or widower, get a property tax exemption of $1,000 as the base, with town-specific amounts (for example Burrillville and Newport $4,000, Lincoln up to $10,000, Glocester up to $30,000, Westerly up to $40,500). This is for service, not a disability rating. Present proof to the town assessor by that year's deadline; the proof stays good while you live at the same legal residence.
benefits.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws 44-3-4 Veterans' exemptions

benefits.benefit: Totally disabled veteran property tax exemption
benefits.details: A veteran 'determined... to be totally disabled through service-connected disability' by the VA may get a $10,000 exemption on real or personal property, but only 'by ordinance' passed in the town where the property is assessed. Town amounts differ (Cranston up to $250,000 and extended to the unmarried widow or widower, Cumberland $47,544, Westerly $39,000, North Kingstown $11,000, Narragansett $20,000). Apply to the local tax assessor by the town deadline (several towns use March 15). The statute does not name TDIU or P&T, so ask the assessor about TDIU.
benefits.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws 44-3-4(c) Veterans' exemptions

benefits.benefit: Specially adapted housing property tax exemption
benefits.details: A veteran, or unmarried widow or widower, who is totally disabled through service-connected disability and got VA specially adapted housing help gets a $10,000 exemption on real estate, if the home is their domicile (only the occupied part of a multi-family home counts). Some towns set other amounts (Cranston up to $30,000, Narragansett up to $50,000, Westerly up to $40,500). Give the assessors satisfactory evidence of the VA assistance.
benefits.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws 44-3-4(b) Veterans' exemptions

benefits.benefit: Fully exempt adapted homestead
benefits.details: A veteran with a 'totally and permanently disabled' service-connected rating who owns a homestead acquired or modified with a VA special adaptive housing grant (or bought with proceeds from the sale of one) and that meets VA and ADA guidelines is 'exempt from all taxation on the homestead.' The veteran's surviving spouse also qualifies. Westerly caps this at $46,500. Apply with the town assessor.
benefits.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws 44-3-4(i) Veterans' exemptions

benefits.benefit: Disabled veteran registration fee waiver
benefits.details: A veteran with a combined VA service-connected rating of 100%, or who is considered 'individually unemployable' (TDIU), or who qualifies under the older loss-of-limb-use rules, pays no fee for the annual registration or license to operate the vehicle. The statute does not require the rating to be permanent. Provide VA documentation to the DMV.
benefits.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws 31-6-8 Disabled veterans

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran plates
benefits.details: The DMV issues 'Disabled Veteran' plates for an automobile or a commercial vehicle up to 12,000 lbs to eligible veterans (same 100% or individually unemployable criteria). Only one set per veteran, issued after VA certification or other satisfactory documentation. After the holder dies the plates may pass to the surviving spouse for life or until remarriage.
benefits.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws 31-6-8 Disabled veterans

benefits.benefit: Free fishing and combination (hunting) license
benefits.details: Veterans with a 100% disability rating can get a no-fee 100% Permanent Disability Fishing or Combination license. DEM requires the original final decision document on VA letterhead (Explanation of Benefit letters do not apply). For hunting you also need a prior RI or out-of-state hunting license, a hunter safety card, or a DD-214. DEM says the veteran license is permanent. Permits and stamps (such as the waterfowl stamp) still cost money. Mail to RI DEM, 235 Promenade St., Room 360, Providence.
benefits.source_title: DEM Application for 100% Permanent Disability Fishing/Combination License

benefits.benefit: State beach and park fee waiver
benefits.details: No fee for parking, admission or golf greens fees at state-owned recreation facilities for a person with a disability, which includes a veteran the VA has determined is 100% disabled through a service-connected disability. Proper DEM identification is required. Camping, picnic table, equestrian and similar special fees are not waived.
benefits.source_title: User Fees at State Beaches, Parks, and Recreational Areas (250-RICR-100-00-3) section 3.5

benefits.benefit: Disabled veteran tuition waiver
benefits.details: A permanent RI resident veteran with a VA rating of 10% to 100% for service-connected disability may take courses at any public RI institution of higher education without paying tuition (other fees and charges are not covered). You must apply for financial aid first, and aid goes toward tuition. Register at the start of open registration; competitive program admission rules still apply. Ask the school bursar or veterans office to start the waiver.
benefits.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws 30-30.1-1 Educational benefits for disabled American veterans

benefits.benefit: Military retirement pay income tax exemption
benefits.details: For tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2023, taxpayers get a modification reducing federal AGI for military service pension benefits, entered on line 1v of Schedule M. There is no age or income limit in the instructions. Rhode Island does have a state income tax, so other income is still taxed. Do not also include the same amount on the regular pension line.
benefits.source_title: 2025 RI-1040 Resident Instructions (Schedule M, line 1v)

benefits.benefit: Civil service veterans hiring points
benefits.details: On competitive entrance tests for the state classified service (not promotions), veterans who reach the minimum passing score get 5 points added and disabled veterans get 10 points. Disabled veteran is defined in chapter 3 of title 36, which I did not read, so confirm the exact rating needed with the state Division of Human Resources. Attach the DD-214 and VA proof with the application.
benefits.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws 36-4-19 Placement of names on employment lists - Listing of veterans

states.name: South Carolina

agency.name: South Carolina Department of Veterans' Affairs

notes: The big property tax break is for a veteran who is 'permanently and totally disabled as a result of a service-connected disability' (S.C. Code 12-37-220(B)(1)). The law defines that as unable to do substantial gainful employment because of an impairment lasting 12 months or more or ending in death. SCDOR's page says 'total and permanent service-connected disability'. It does not say whether a permanent TDIU rating counts, so ask SCDOR (803-898-5700) before assuming it does.

A VA rating decision letter is NOT enough. SCDOR says 'VA Rating decision letters do not meet requirements of law.' You need a certificate from the VA or from your county veterans affairs (service) officer stating the disability is total and permanent, with the effective date. Get this certificate first.

Apply to the state, not the county. SCDOR (not the county auditor) handles the veteran exemption, online through MyDORWAY or on paper with Form PT-401I. The county auditor and assessor get the approval letter. The general 65/disabled homestead exemption is different and is filed with the county auditor.

Vehicles: the exemption covers two private passenger vehicles you own or lease, registered with SCDMV before you apply. Property tax on a vehicle is only exempt if it comes due on or after the date of your total and permanent rating. A surviving spouse gets only one vehicle.

Back claims: a 2024 change lets you claim the real estate exemption from the year you became disabled. SCDOR now says claims reach back only two years and require taxes paid on time. SCDVA's 2024 news item says 'retroactive to 2022'. The sources differ, so confirm the window with SCDOR.

A surviving spouse keeps the home exemption while unmarried, living in the house and owning it in fee or for life. SCDOR says to reapply. Surviving spouses of service members killed in action also qualify for the home exemption.

The South Carolina disabled veteran plate is free (no plate fee and no registration fee), but it does NOT give handicap parking. Disabled-parking rights need a separate physician-certified RG-007A application and the 'wheelchair' version of the plate. As of May 6, 2022, a surviving spouse cannot newly obtain a Disabled Veteran plate unless one was already registered in their name before that date.
Military plates cannot be bought online or at a branch. They are mail-in only to SCDMV Specialty Plates, and you must send proof of paid county vehicle tax or no tax due.

The free tuition benefit for children (59-111-20) requires that the VETERAN served honorably during a federal war period AND is 'permanently and totally disabled, as determined by the Veterans Administration from any cause' (or another listed category). The student must be 26 or younger and in an undergraduate degree. Apply to SCDVA online; benefit starts on the date the application is received and is not retroactive.

The free SCDNR disability hunting/fishing license has no VA percentage listed. SCDNR's page only says you must be disabled, receiving disability benefits from the VA (or another listed agency) and a 365-day SC resident. Ask SCDNR if a low rating qualifies. It is valid for 3 years and then must be recertified.

Pending in the legislature in 2026, not law: H.4700 (partial property tax exemption equal to rating percentage for veterans below total and permanent; no action since January 21, 2026) and H.4811 (free campsites for disabled veterans in state parks). Do not tell veterans these exist yet.
South Carolina has an income tax, but military retirement pay is fully deductible at any age starting tax year 2022. Active duty pay of nonresidents stationed in SC is not taxed by SC.

benefits.benefit: Disabled veteran home property tax exemption
benefits.details: Exempts the house and lot (the lot is whatever qualifies for the 4% legal-residence classification, which SCDOR describes as up to five acres) from property tax for a veteran who is permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected disability. You need a certificate from the VA or county service officer showing total and permanent service-connected disability with its effective date; a rating decision letter is not accepted. Apply to SCDOR online (MyDORWAY) or by Form PT-401I; SCDOR page lists no deadline. Whether a permanent TDIU rating qualifies is not stated by SCDOR, so confirm.
benefits.source_title: S.C. Code 12-37-220(B)(1), exemption of house of eligible owner; SCDOR Exempt Property page https://dor.sc.gov/property/exempt-property

benefits.benefit: Property tax exemption on two vehicles
benefits.details: Two private passenger vehicles owned or leased by a disabled veteran (or a spouse living with the veteran at the same address) are exempt from property tax if the veteran has a certificate of total and permanent disability from the county service officer or VA, or has the special disabled veteran plates. Vehicles must be registered with SCDMV before applying; apply through SCDOR (MyDORWAY or PT-401I). The tax must come due on or after the date of the total and permanent rating.
benefits.source_title: S.C. Code 12-37-220(B)(3), vehicle exemption; SCDOR Exempt Property page

benefits.benefit: Surviving spouse property tax exemption
benefits.details: A surviving spouse of a qualifying disabled veteran keeps the home exemption while unmarried, living in the house and owning it in fee or for life; the spouse of a service member killed in action also qualifies. The spouse must reapply with SCDOR. For vehicles, a surviving spouse gets the exemption on one vehicle only, for life or until remarriage.
benefits.source_title: S.C. Code 12-37-220(B)(1)(f)(iii) and (B)(3); SCDVA 2024 news https://scdva.sc.gov/news/property-tax-exemption-disabled-south-carolina-veterans-expanded

benefits.benefit: Homestead exemption, first $50,000 of value
benefits.details: Exempts the first $50,000 of fair market value of your dwelling from county, municipal and school real estate taxes if you are 65 or older, legally blind, or classified as totally and permanently disabled by a state or federal agency (the VA counts). You need one year of SC residency and fee simple or life estate title. Apply in writing to the county auditor before July 16 of the tax year or you wait until next year; this is separate from the veteran exemption.
benefits.source_title: S.C. Code 12-37-250, homestead exemption

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran license plate, no fees
benefits.details: The Disabled Veteran plate has no plate fee and no registration fee, up to three plates. Eligibility is a letter from the county or US VA office showing loss or use of a leg, arm, or vision, or classification as totally and permanently disabled due to service-connected disabilities, plus honorable or general discharge. Mail Form MV-37 to SCDMV Specialty Plates; the plate does not allow handicap parking.
benefits.source_title: SCDMV Form MV-37 Application for Military License Plate (02/2026) and https://dmv.sc.gov/node/1522

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran (wheelchair) plate and Purple Heart plate parking
benefits.details: The Disabled Veteran (wheelchair) plate also has a free registration fee and gives handicap parking and free parking at metered or timed spaces, but you must also submit Form RG-007A signed by a licensed physician. Purple Heart plates (no fee) also include free parking at municipal meters. Other disabled veterans must get disabled parking separately through RG-007A.
benefits.source_title: SCDMV Military Plates FAQ (published 03/25/2024) and MV-37 (02/2026)

benefits.benefit: Free disability hunting and fishing license
benefits.details: A resident for at least 365 days who is disabled and receiving benefits from the VA (or Social Security, Medicaid and others listed) can get a free 3-year disability combination license covering freshwater and saltwater fishing, hunting, big game, WMAs and the waterfowl permit. No VA percentage is stated. Email DisabilityLicense@dnr.sc.gov to request the application; renewal needs recertification. Quadriplegic, paraplegic or legally blind applicants get a lifetime license.
benefits.source_title: SCDNR Disability License Information; S.C. Code 50-9-525

benefits.benefit: State park free admission for permanently and totally disabled veterans
benefits.details: An SC resident veteran classified by the VA as permanently and totally disabled may enter any state park without charge by showing an identification card from the county veterans affairs officer. Under the same section, disabled residents get campsites at half price, and parks discount at least 35 percent for these residents; free entry does not cover campsites, lodging or recreation buildings. SCPRT's FAQ separately lists 35 percent off and a 50 percent off all-parks passport for 100% disabled residents.
benefits.source_title: S.C. Code 51-3-60 and 51-3-65; https://southcarolinaparks.com/faqs

benefits.benefit: Free tuition for children of certain wartime veterans
benefits.details: A child of a wartime veteran can attend any state-supported college, university or technical school free of tuition if the veteran served honorably in a war period and was killed in action, died in service or of a service-related disease, was a POW or MIA, has a Medal of Honor or combat Purple Heart, or is 'permanently and totally disabled, as determined by the Veterans Administration from any cause'. The child must be 26 or younger in an undergraduate degree, with SC residency (a 2026 change also covers children resident since birth). Apply online to SCDVA; no retroactive reimbursement.
benefits.source_title: S.C. Code 59-111-20; Act 135 of 2026 (H.3453, signed May 15, 2026); https://scdva.sc.gov/education

benefits.benefit: Military retirement pay fully deductible
benefits.details: South Carolina has a state income tax, but since tax year 2022 you can deduct all military retirement income at any age, with no cap. Surviving spouses receiving military retirement income or DIC tied to the deceased spouse's service can also deduct it. Claim it on the SC1040 military retirement lines. Reserve and National Guard retirement pay is also not taxed.
benefits.source_title: SCDOR Revenue Ruling 22-11 and S.C. Code 12-6-1171

benefits.benefit: VA disability compensation and state income tax
benefits.details: I found no SCDOR page that states VA disability compensation is exempt from SC income tax. SC taxable income starts from federal income and VA compensation is not federally taxable, so it is very likely not taxed, but that is an inference. Confirm with SCDOR (803-898-5700) before relying on it.
benefits.source_title: SCDOR Retirees tax tips and SC1040 instructions

benefits.benefit: Veterans employment preference in state jobs
benefits.details: Honorably discharged veterans who receive a federal preference get preference in state agency and higher education hiring, with at least one qualified veteran interviewed per posted position. SC uses an interview and preference rule, not a point system. Submit a DD-214 with your state application or you get no preference. Effective January 1, 2021.
benefits.source_title: S.C. Code 1-1-550; https://scdva.sc.gov/news/new-veterans-hiring-preference

benefits.benefit: State Veterans Homes
benefits.details: SCDVA runs state veterans nursing homes (Stone Veterans Pavilion in Columbia, Victory House in Walterboro, Palmetto Patriots Home in Gaffney, Patriot's Village in Sumter and others). Admission requires general or honorable discharge, SC residency, and a need for skilled or intermediate nursing care. Apply through the home or your county veterans affairs officer.
benefits.source_title: SCDVA State Veterans Homes

states.name: South Dakota

agency.name: South Dakota Department of Veterans Affairs

notes: The big property tax break is a $200,000 reduction in the taxable value of your home (not a full exemption), and it requires a permanent and total (P&T) service-connected rating. A 100% rating that is not P&T may not qualify; ask the county director of equalization.
Apply for the property tax exemption to the county director of equalization by November 1. Once approved you do not reapply, but it ends if you sell, stop living there, or the use changes.
The home must be classified owner-occupied (your principal residence). Only one dwelling can be classified this way, and the exemption covers the home, garage and lot.

Missed the deadline? State law lets you petition the county commissioners for a refund. If your P&T claim was still pending with VA, taxes back to the claim effective date (up to 4 years) must be refunded.
A surviving spouse keeps the $200,000 exemption only while unremarried. The spouse qualifies if the veteran was rated P&T or if the spouse receives VA DIC for a service-connected death.

Separate, fuller exemption: a paraplegic veteran (or veteran with loss or loss of use of both lower extremities) with a wheelchair-designed home can be fully exempt from property tax, and the injury does not need to be service related.

The disabled veteran plate needs a total service-connected allotment, K award, or statutory loss-of-use benefit, and the disability must have been incurred in wartime or an armed-conflict mission. A 100% rating alone may not satisfy that.
The reduced-fee hunting and fishing card starts at 40% service-connected, but the state park lifetime pass requires 100% total disability (or K award). The two thresholds differ, so check each.

Free tuition for veterans is capped at 1 to 4 academic years, is for wartime veterans, and is paid only after federal education benefits are used up. A veteran qualifying solely on a disability needs at least a 10% VA rating.
South Dakota has no individual income tax, so military retirement pay and VA compensation are not taxed by the state.

The 2026 Legislature amended the veteran property tax laws (SL 2026 ch 40); the $200,000 figure in the current code text is unchanged, but confirm the effective date and any application form changes with your county.

benefits.benefit: Disabled veteran property tax exemption ($200,000)
benefits.details: Exempts $200,000 of the full and true value of an owner-occupied dwelling (home, garage and lot) for a veteran rated permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected disability. Apply on the Department of Revenue form to your county director of equalization on or before November 1, with a VA statement or benefits letter showing P&T. No annual reapplication once approved. Whether a TDIU-only veteran qualifies is not stated in the statute.
benefits.source_title: SDCL 10-4-40 Partial exemption--Owner-occupied dwellings of certain disabled veterans

benefits.benefit: Surviving spouse property tax exemption ($200,000)
benefits.details: The same $200,000 exemption applies to the owner-occupied home of the surviving spouse of a veteran rated P&T, or of a surviving spouse who receives VA DIC for a service-connected death. It ends if the spouse remarries, sells, stops living there or the use changes. Apply to the county director of equalization by November 1.
benefits.source_title: SDCL 10-4-41 Partial exemption--Owner-occupied dwellings of surviving spouses of certain veterans

benefits.benefit: Paraplegic veteran full property tax exemption
benefits.details: A dwelling designed for wheelchair use that a paraplegic veteran, or a veteran with loss or loss of use of both lower extremities (or the unremarried widow or widower), owns and occupies for the full calendar year is exempt from property tax. The Department of Revenue says the injury does not have to be service related and no annual reapplication is needed. Apply to the county director of equalization by November 1.
benefits.source_title: SDCL 10-4-24.10 Exemption for dwelling of paraplegic or amputee veteran or surviving spouse

benefits.benefit: Disabled veteran license plates ($10, no registration fee)
benefits.details: A veteran who receives a veteran's allotment for a total service-connected disability, a K award, or a statutory benefit for loss of use of extremities (disability incurred in wartime or armed-conflict service) can get disabled veteran plates for $10 initial and $10 annual renewal, with no annual registration fee, plus a $12 mailing fee. Up to two sets of plates are allowed, usable on cars, pickups or vans (heavier pickups and motorhomes pay regular fees). Apply with form MV-4000 through the county treasurer or Department of Revenue.
benefits.source_title: SDCL 32-5-160 and 32-5-157 (military specialty plates)

benefits.benefit: Reduced-fee hunting and fishing card
benefits.details: Residents who receive a VA allotment for a 40 percent or greater service-connected disability, or the K award, can get a small game plus fishing license card for $10, valid four years. The 40% threshold is the real minimum, not 10%. Send the application, VA letter and fee to Game, Fish and Parks, Fort Pierre.
benefits.source_title: SDCL 41-6-10.2 Certain disabled residents eligible for reduced license fees

benefits.benefit: Lifetime state park entrance license and 50% camping discount
benefits.details: Residents with a VA letter or K award showing 100% total service-connected disability (also POWs and Purple Heart recipients) get a lifetime park entrance license with free vehicle entry and 50% off camping and electrical fees. Apply online through Go Outdoors South Dakota and upload the VA document; GFP says status updates come within two weeks.
benefits.source_title: Military Park Entrance Licenses (SD Game, Fish and Parks)

benefits.benefit: Disabled veteran special hunts (deer, pheasant)
benefits.details: GFP and nonprofit sponsors hold free special hunts for disabled veterans. The 2025 resident deer hunt required a VA rating of 20% or more service-connected disability, a K award, or Purple Heart; the special pheasant hunt uses the same 20% threshold for residents and nonresidents. Apply by the posted deadline (2025 deer hunt: July 31); dates change yearly.
benefits.source_title: Disabled Veteran/Purple Heart Recipient Special Pheasant Hunt

benefits.benefit: Free tuition for veterans at state schools
benefits.details: Wartime veterans who are South Dakota residents get tuition-free undergraduate study at Board of Regents schools and technical colleges for one month of academic time per month of qualified service, with a minimum of one and maximum of four academic years. A veteran qualifying solely through disability needs a VA rating of 10% or higher. Federal education benefits must be exhausted first, and the Board of Regents determines eligibility.
benefits.source_title: SDCL 13-55-2 Veterans entitled to free tuition at state institutions

benefits.benefit: Free tuition for children of residents who died in service
benefits.details: The child (under 25) of a South Dakota resident who died in service in the armed forces is entitled to free tuition at Board of Regents schools and technical colleges. This applies to death in service, not to children of living disabled veterans. A separate law covers children and spouses of National Guard members who died or were totally and permanently disabled on duty.
benefits.source_title: SDCL 13-55-6 Free education of children of residents who died during service

benefits.benefit: Veterans preference in public employment
benefits.details: Eligible veterans get preference for appointment, employment and promotion in state, county, municipal and school district jobs, and must be interviewed if minimally qualified. A veteran with a service-connected disability is preferred over a nondisabled veteran. SD does not use fixed point values; apply through the hiring agency and identify veteran status on the application.
benefits.source_title: SDCL 3-3-1 Veterans preferred in public employment

benefits.benefit: No state income tax
benefits.details: South Dakota has no personal income tax, so military retirement pay and VA disability compensation are not taxed by the state. The Department of Revenue states it has no corporate, unitary or personal income tax. No application is needed.
benefits.source_title: SD Department of Revenue Sales and Use Tax Guide (July 2026)

states.name: Tennessee
notes: Tennessee property tax relief is a reimbursement, not an exemption. You pay the tax first, then the state reimburses you, and only on the first $175,000 of market value. The Comptroller says you must have already paid your taxes when you first apply.

The property tax program has no income limit for disabled veterans. The income limits on the Comptroller brochure apply to the separate elderly and disabled homeowner programs. Eligibility is checked against VA records through the F-16 consent form, so a pending or temporary 100% rating is a risk.

The qualifying disabilities are narrow: paraplegia, paralysis of both legs, loss or loss of use of two or more limbs, legal blindness, 100% permanent and total from POW service, or a service-connected permanent and total disability as determined by the VA. A 100% rating that is not marked permanent and total may not qualify.

The state veterans page for surviving spouses still shows an old $100,000 cap. The 2026 Comptroller brochure shows $175,000 for surviving spouses too. Use the Comptroller figure and confirm with your county trustee.

The free Disabled Veteran (DV) plate is not tied to the rating alone. The state lists loss or loss of use of a foot or hand, permanent loss of vision in both eyes, or a 100% permanent and total service-connected disability. Only the first plate is free. The county motor vehicle privilege tax exemption needs 100% permanent and total (or former POW).

The TWRA disabled veteran hunting and fishing license is a one-time $10 fee for residents either 100% permanent and totally disabled from a service-connected cause or 30% or more disabled by reason of war service. The 30% route is tied to wartime service, so check eligibility with TWRA if your service was not during a war period.

State parks give 100% service-connected veterans 50% off camping and cabins year-round, with other Tennessee resident veterans getting 25% in season and 50% in December through February. Premium sites are excluded, and the tn.gov veterans page still shows the older, narrower discount rules.

Tennessee has no tax on wages or on military retirement or VA compensation, and the Hall tax on interest and dividends ended for tax years beginning January 1, 2021. Property taxes and sales taxes still apply.

State tuition help is narrow. Tennessee waives tuition for spouses and dependents of POW, MIA, killed-in-action, or died-on-duty service members, not for dependents of living disabled veterans. The Helping Heroes Grant depends on specific post-9/11 campaign medals, not a rating.

Several tn.gov veterans pages are old or inconsistent with each other (surviving spouse cap, state park discounts, parking statute text from 2010). When in doubt, the Comptroller property tax brochure and the 2026 OREA report are the most recent official sources.

benefits.benefit: Property tax relief for disabled veterans
benefits.details: The state reimburses county and city property taxes on the first $175,000 of market value of your primary residence. You qualify with a VA service-connected permanent and total disability, 100% P&T from POW service, or specific losses (paraplegia, paralysis of both legs, loss or loss of use of two or more limbs, legal blindness). There is no income limit. Apply with the county trustee (or city collecting official) when you receive your 2026 tax bill; the deadline is 35 days after the delinquency date and taxes must be paid by then. Whether a P&T TDIU rating counts was not stated on the official pages.
benefits.source_title: Comptroller of the Treasury, 2026 Property Tax Relief Program brochure

benefits.benefit: Property tax relief for surviving spouses of disabled veterans
benefits.details: A surviving spouse who has not remarried can receive the same reimbursement on the first $175,000 of market value if the veteran met the disability requirements at death. Relief also extends to spouses of veterans whose death resulted from a VA-determined service-connected, combat-related cause. Apply with the county trustee using form F-16S with a death certificate and personal ID. The tn.gov veterans page still lists an older $100,000 cap, so confirm the figure with the trustee.
benefits.source_title: Comptroller of the Treasury, 2026 Property Tax Relief Program brochure

benefits.benefit: County motor vehicle privilege tax exemption
benefits.details: Veterans with a 100 percent permanent, total service-connected disability, and former prisoners of war, are exempt from the county motor vehicle privilege tax (the wheel tax). Submit evidence of the disability to the county officer who collects the tax, usually the county clerk. The exemption is under T.C.A. 5-8-102.
benefits.source_title: County Motor Vehicle Privilege Tax (Tennessee Department of Veterans Services)

benefits.benefit: Free Disabled Veteran license plate
benefits.details: The first Disabled Veteran (DV) plate is issued free for one vehicle under T.C.A. 55-4-256. Qualifying: loss or permanent loss of use of one or both feet or hands, permanent impairment of vision in both eyes, or a 100% permanent and total service-connected disability (the Comptroller's 2026 report lists these four). Additional plates cost the normal fees. Apply at your county clerk.
benefits.source_title: State Benefits and Services for Veterans in Tennessee (Comptroller OREA, March 2026)

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran parking placard and decal
benefits.details: Veterans eligible for a free DV plate may, from July 1, 2026, choose a free Disabled Veteran placard instead; a veteran who keeps the free plate can get a placard for the standard passenger registration fee. A veteran who chooses a non-free or other specialty plate can get a free disabled driver decal, which gives disabled parking privileges. Apply at your county clerk using Department of Revenue form RV-F1310301. Proof of eligibility under T.C.A. 55-4-252 is required.
benefits.source_title: Application for Disabled Person License Plate, Placard, or Decal (RV-F1310301, Rev. 07/26)

benefits.benefit: TWRA disabled veteran hunting and fishing license
benefits.details: A one-time $10 hunting and fishing license, valid for life, for Tennessee residents certified by the VA as 100% permanent and totally disabled from a service-connected cause, or 30% or more disabled by reason of war service. This is a TWRA specialty license (listed as Type 198 in the state's veteran benefit matrix), so you apply with TWRA rather than at a normal agent. I could not open the TWRA application page itself.
benefits.source_title: Hunting and Fishing Licenses (Tennessee Department of Veterans Services)

benefits.benefit: State park camping and cabin discount for 100% service-connected veterans
benefits.details: Tennessee resident veterans with a 100% service-connected disability get 50% off cabin rentals and campsites year-round; premium sites are excluded. Bring proof of Tennessee residency, veteran status, and a VA certification of your percentage. Other Tennessee resident veterans get 25% off in March through November and 50% in December through February, plus 25% off lodge rooms, 20% off golf green fees and carts, and 15% off gift shops.
benefits.source_title: Discounts (Tennessee State Parks)

benefits.benefit: Veterans Day free camping night and golf round
benefits.details: On Veterans Day, Tennessee resident veterans get one free night of camping (premium sites excluded) and a free 18-hole round of golf at state park courses. The Comptroller also lists complimentary camping and golf on each service branch's birthday. Reserve camping by phone at 1-888-867-2757 and show proof of residency and veteran status.
benefits.source_title: Veterans Programs and Benefits (Tennessee State Parks)

benefits.benefit: Helping Heroes Grant
benefits.details: The grant pays $1,000 per semester for full-time students (12 or more hours), or $500 for 6 to 11 hours, up to eight full-time semesters. Applicants must be honorably discharged Tennessee residents of at least one year without a bachelor's degree, and hold the Iraq, Afghanistan, Global War on Terrorism Expeditionary (on or after 9/11/2001), or Inherent Resolve campaign medal. It is not tied to a disability rating.
benefits.source_title: State Benefits and Services for Veterans in Tennessee (Comptroller OREA, March 2026)

benefits.benefit: Tuition waiver for dependents of POW, MIA, killed-in-action or died-on-duty service members; in-state tuition for veterans
benefits.details: Spouses and dependent children (under 23) of a POW, MIA, service member killed in action, or one who died of injuries on active duty can get a tuition and specified fee waiver at state colleges and universities. Veterans and eligible dependents using federal education benefits cannot be charged out-of-state tuition. I found no state tuition waiver for dependents of living disabled veterans; a bill for a general veterans waiver did not advance.
benefits.source_title: State Benefits and Services for Veterans in Tennessee (Comptroller OREA, March 2026)

benefits.benefit: No state tax on wages; Hall income tax repealed
benefits.details: Tennessee has no individual income tax on wages, and the Hall income tax on interest and dividends was repealed for tax periods beginning on or after January 1, 2021. No Hall tax return is needed for those years. The Department of Revenue pages do not name military retired pay or VA disability compensation, so ask the Department if you have a specific question about them.
benefits.source_title: Hall Income Tax (Tennessee Department of Revenue)

benefits.benefit: State employment veterans' preference
benefits.details: Honorably discharged veterans who meet the minimum qualifications for a preferred-service state job must be invited to the first-round interview, and the veteran gets preference when qualifications are equal. Passing over a veteran requires a written reason filed with the Commissioner. A spouse or surviving spouse is also invited if the veteran is 100% service-connected, permanently and totally disabled, or died in the line of duty. Submit a DD-214 or similar proof with the application; veterans also get 60 extra months of service credit for layoff order.
benefits.source_title: Department of Human Resources Policy 12-007, Veterans' Preference (Rev. 10/01/2025)

benefits.benefit: Service-disabled veteran-owned business assistance and handgun permit discount
benefits.details: The Governor's Office of Business Initiatives and Development helps service-disabled veteran-owned businesses compete for state contracts if the owner has at least a 20 percent service-connected disability. Separately, honorably discharged veterans get $35 off the initial enhanced handgun permit fee ($100 eight-year or $300 lifetime) from the Department of Safety. Neither depends on a higher rating.
benefits.source_title: State Benefits and Services for Veterans in Tennessee (Comptroller OREA, March 2026)

states.name: Texas
notes: Texas has two different property tax breaks. The partial break (Tax Code 11.22) goes from $5,000 to $12,000 off assessed value, depending on your rating. The total homestead break (11.131) is for a 100% rating or unemployability only. There is nothing in between.

The partial 11.22 break comes off the 'assessed value' and you can use it on only ONE property. Each taxing unit (school district, county, city) applies it separately, so the real dollar savings are small. The 11.131 break wipes out the tax on your whole home.

The 100% break (11.131) covers only your residence homestead. The statute says '100 percent disability compensation' with a 'rating of 100 percent disabled or of individual unemployability.' It does not say 'permanent and total.' A TDIU rating counts. Show the appraisal district your VA award letter.

Apply at the county appraisal district where the home sits (Form 50-114 for 11.131, Form 50-135 for 11.22). The normal deadline is April 30. The Comptroller says you can file up to five years after the tax delinquency date. Once approved, you usually do not have to refile, but the chief appraiser can ask you to confirm every so often. Answer that letter or you can lose the break.

An unmarried surviving spouse keeps the 100% break on the same home. If the spouse remarries, the break ends. If the spouse moves, the new home gets an exemption only equal to the dollar amount on the old home in its last year, so it may not be a full exemption.

New for 2025: voters approved Proposition 7 in November 2025, and Tax Code 11.136 (HB 2508) gives a total homestead exemption to an unremarried surviving spouse of a veteran who died from a PACT Act presumptive condition, even if the veteran was never rated 100%. Ask your appraisal district how to file.

Disabled veteran plates need 50% (or 40% for loss of a lower extremity) and the plate is NOT a parking pass. Since 2022 (SB 792) you can park in a disabled space only with a plate or placard showing the International Symbol of Access. A plain DV plate does not allow it. You need a doctor's statement for the ISA version.

Registration fee waiver is only for ONE vehicle, owned by you, 18,000 lbs or less. The fee for the first set of DV plates is $3. You still pay other costs at the county tax office (inspection, sales tax on a purchase, and so on).

Thresholds differ by benefit: 50% for plates and the free hunting/fishing Super Combo, 60% for the free driver license and the Disabled Veterans state park pass, 70% for a free stay in a State Veterans Home. Do not assume one rating opens every door.

The Hazlewood Act is separate from the GI Bill and is NOT based on disability rating. A veteran needs Texas as the place of entry or home of record, 181 days of active duty, and an honorable or general under honorable discharge. The spouse and children of a veteran rated 100% P&T or TDIU can use their own hours, and the veteran does not need to live in Texas.
Texas has no state income tax. The state constitution bans one. VA disability pay is also tax-free federally.

State employment preference points: 10 points on a competitive exam for any veteran, plus 5 more for a veteran with a service-connected disability. The preference only applies when you are qualified and score at least the minimum.

benefits.benefit: Disabled veteran partial property tax exemption
